techniques.materials: The press can bend its container: see the jelly press for the edge displacement, and the button fill can change colour by a gradient climbing through it rather than a cross-fade.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Bento unfolds on one shared curve
techniques.summary: One layout opens into the next: every tile travels from its old box to its new one (position, size, radius, fill) on the same front-loaded curve, the main tiles together and the edges a few frames later; content keeps its size and is revealed by the moving boxes, pictures re-crop as their boxes grow.
techniques.recipe: <Bento frame={f} tiles={[{ A, B, content | image }]} start={at} delays={[0, 0, 2, 8, 18]} />. Lay A out as the state before (thumbnails in a panel, a row of chips) and B as the dashboard. decay: 0.8 is the alternative form (80 % of the remaining distance kept every frame at 30 fps).
techniques.timing: 44 f on E.snapOut (42-60 f); delays 0-18 f.
techniques.use_when: A panel becomes a dashboard, a list becomes a grid, an overview opens.
techniques.avoid_when: The tiles carry long text that would be cut by the moving boxes mid-read.

techniques.name: The one spring: a container pops open
techniques.summary: The film's single overshoot: on the click, the container (a button becoming its confirmation, a pill becoming a menu) springs open past its size and settles; nothing else in the film overshoots.
techniques.recipe: springBox(f, start, { A: button, B: confirmation }, film) drawn as one rounded box (or <Card spring={{ start, from }}>); fade the new label in over the first 15 f. Name the element class in timeline SPRING_CLASS.
techniques.timing: SPR.landing (zeta 0.59, about 10 % over, home in 23 f at 60 fps); start it on the click or one or two frames before the container is seen.
techniques.use_when: The one moment the product answers the user.
techniques.avoid_when: Type, logos that already move on a curve, or a second class of element in the same film.

techniques.name: Chat bubbles cut on and slide home
techniques.summary: Each message cuts on at full size below its slot and slides up on an exponential while the conversation lifts a little to make room; replies come a beat later, a typing bubble pulses until the answer replaces it.
techniques.recipe: <Bubbles frame={f} messages={[{ text, side, at }, { kind: 'typing', ... }]} role='caption' lift={{ share: 0.25, tau: 4 }} header={avatar} />. bubbleY / bubbleState / bubbleFrames give the numbers and the sound cue frames.
techniques.timing: tau 12 f (10-16), home at 50 f, travel 56 px at 1080p (38-70), reply 32 f later (20-32).
techniques.use_when: An assistant, a team thread, a support conversation, a message composer.
techniques.avoid_when: More than four bubbles in one beat; text below the caption role on screen.

techniques.name: Imagery develops from a duotone
techniques.summary: Thumbnails, screenshots or built panels arrive as a duotone in the film's own ink and accent and come into full colour column by column, so a grid lands as one wave instead of a pop.
techniques.recipe: <Develop frame={f} start={at} index={column} image={{ src }} tint={{ shadow, highlight }} width height /> per picture (or children for built UI); tintSrc takes a supplied pre-tinted plate. The tint is a static filter, the colour an opacity fade.
techniques.timing: 24 f per picture on M.develop (20-26), columns 4 f apart (0-6); steps 16 fps for a stepped develop.
techniques.use_when: A grid of results, a gallery, a feed loading, a screenshot entering.
techniques.avoid_when: A single hero picture that should simply cut on.
techniques.materials: Gradient-map roll: the tiles start washed out (the map mixed 55 % toward the stage) and every tile keeps changing its map, about 6 f per map through six to eight pastel maps, staggered about 6 f a tile, before landing on true colour (90 f in all). A cluster can also lose contrast and re-tint into a two-ink duotone as it shrinks into the cut (12 f).
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Hard UI against eased type
techniques.summary: The product changes state like software: counters tick linear values at different rates and are still counting when the shot cuts, a list jumps whole rows with nothing in between, a selection snaps in one frame, while the copy around it eases.
techniques.recipe: countLinear(f, { from, perSec, start }, film).shown in tabular figures (or <Roll hard steps={linearSteps(...)}>); <HardStep jump={rowHeight} every={4} ...> for a list; snapBox() for a selection. Declare the jumps (declares()).
techniques.timing: Counters linear for 1.2-1.6 s, rates about 14 : 5 : 1 when several share a frame, cut mid-count; list jumps of one row, every 4-8 f.
techniques.use_when: Live data, dashboards, analytics, logs, queues.
techniques.avoid_when: The number is the payoff: then land it (steppedTail) and hold it.

techniques.name: Supplied screenshots move like built UI
techniques.summary: Real product screenshots and product shots enter, unfold, develop and get pushed into with the same grammar as built UI; the one element the film acts on is rebuilt live on top so it can press, spring or count.
techniques.recipe: <Card image={{ src: staticFile('shot.png'), fit: 'cover', focus: { x, y }, zoom, zoomTo, zoomStart, zoomDur }} enter={...} />; <Bento tiles={[{ A, B, image }]} />; <Develop image={{ src }} />. Supply images at 2x their largest on-screen size; crop the focus onto the feature; overlay the acting element as live UI at the same place and size.
techniques.timing: As the primitive used; a slow push inside a card zooms x1.05 -> x1.15 over 4 s.
techniques.use_when: Any film made from a supplied brand kit or product screenshots; update videos with 2-4 changes.
techniques.avoid_when: Screenshots smaller than their on-screen size (they go soft): rebuild those as live UI.

techniques.name: A product moment in one camera
techniques.summary: One continuous camera over one desk: the panel enters front-loaded on a tilted plane, the cursor swings upright and presses, the one spring pops the container open, the next card lands while the panel steps back, everything unfolds into the dashboard on one shared curve, pictures develop, a flick lands on the item that matters and a live counter is cut mid-count.
techniques.recipe: Design the overview layout in screen px at the pull-back framing with the copy cell left empty, map it to desk px; each beat is a camera key (scale + anchor of that layout) joined by strongInOut / liftOut reframes and linear creeps. Beat 1 <Card enter lean>, cursorState(tilt swing, click ring); beat 2 press() + springBox() (SPRING_CLASS = the container) and stepValue() badges; beat 3 cardArrive + demote centred on it, <Bubbles anchor=bottom> above a composer; beat 4 <Bento> with tile contents fading up as boxes open, <Develop> thumbnails, the light pool brightened once; beat 5 flickState (declares -> CAMERA_BLUR) and countLinear, hard cut mid-count.
techniques.timing: About 9 s at 60 fps plus a 1 s end card: enter 40 f, press at 2 s, spring 8 f after the press, card lands at 3.2 s, unfold at 5.4 s (44 f), flick at 7.5 s, cut at 8.9 s. One calm fragment per beat, at line size or bigger, in the empty cell.
techniques.use_when: The signature shot of a launch film, or each change of an update video (one moment per change, built UI or a supplied screenshot card with its one live element rebuilt).
techniques.avoid_when: A film whose product is not a screen (use the camera and type devices).

techniques.name: Pill breathes into a window
techniques.summary: An image in a pill mask stretches, holds, contracts into the cut at its fastest, and the next shot opens as a window from the pill's own box, growing in a few held steps while the old frame steps back.
techniques.recipe: pillBreath(f, { start, from, to, h, stretch, hold, contract, end }) drives the pill's width; cut on .cut. Then <Window frame start={cut} rects={[pillBox, mid, large]} radius={[h / 2, ...]} oldScale={[1, 1, 0.94, 0.86, 0.86]} cadence={16} old next />.
techniques.timing: Stretch 44 f on E.snapOut (90 % in the first 16), hold 12 f, contract 22 f on E.launchIn to 0.86 of the width (the last step the fastest); window 4 held steps on 16 fps (about 15 f at 60 fps).
techniques.use_when: A framed image or card should become the next scene.
techniques.avoid_when: The image is small text (it must read before it moves).

techniques.name: Exposure bloom into the next scene
techniques.summary: The whole frame over-exposes on an accelerating curve (brightness plus a one-hue veil), the scenes hand over inside the light, and the next scene settles out of a small overshoot of its own brightness.
techniques.recipe: <Exposure frame at={hit} up down peak brightness swap={{ at, frames }} a={outgoing} b={incoming} />; a short charge pulse (charge) before it if the music has a pickup.
techniques.timing: Rise 40 f on E.buildIn, veil 0.82, brightness x1.5, the swap 10 f before the peak with a dissolve of at most 6 f under the light, settle 26 f on E.linear (the incoming scene peaks about 11 % over its rest in mean luma).
techniques.use_when: A hit or a drop, into a reveal or a lockup; once or twice a film.
techniques.avoid_when: The look is a light, white world already (there is no headroom: use a light sweep).

techniques.name: Light sweep across a landing
techniques.summary: A soft band of light swings across the frame as a product lands, accelerating like a beam passing the lens: a light event without a glow on any element.
techniques.recipe: <LightSweep frame start frames band angle gain />, screen blend, one hue (white or a pale accent tint), on a dark stage.
techniques.timing: 44 f on E.launchIn across the frame plus the band, band 0.45 of the width, gain 0.2-0.55.
techniques.use_when: A product or card lands on an ink stage and the act needs its light event.
techniques.avoid_when: Paper grounds (a white band on paper is invisible; use an exposure or a light field).

techniques.name: Dive through a soft layer
techniques.summary: A soft foreground layer (mist, a frosted panel, a cloud bank) rises while the scene behind defocuses and travels up; for a few frames there is only the soft layer, the cut hides there, and the next subject rises out of it with its focus racking a beat behind its position.
techniques.recipe: } />: a static plate with soft edges, never an animated blur radius.
techniques.timing: Rise 40 f (ease-in), defocus to 16 px at 1080p, 12 f fully covered (the cut in the middle), clear 20 f; the subject rises 0.12 of the height over 18 f and racks from 14 px over 36 f, starting 4 f after it moves.
techniques.use_when: Moving from a statement into a product shot; a depth change.
techniques.avoid_when: Flat graphic films with no depth planes.

techniques.name: Flash cut inside a whip
techniques.summary: The camera whips on an ease-in that never brakes; one over-exposed frame with a faint ghost, one dark frame of horizontal streaks, and the next shot is already sliding in and pulls back as it lands.
techniques.recipe: <FlashCut frame cut whip={{ dir }} slide pull out in />; put the swell's peak on the flash frame. The whip's tail and the slide's head carry the whip-shutter streak (smear 'draw', house: DirBlur at 360 degrees); smear 'shutter' declares those frames as camera blur for the finishing pass instead. Declare the flash (declares()).
techniques.timing: Whip 24 f on E.launchIn over 0.24 of the frame width (fastest on its last frame); flash 1 f at about 92 % white with a 0.3 ghost; streak 1 f; slide 28 f on E.snapOut from 0.55 of the width, opening at several times the whip's last speed, so its first frames are the most smeared of the cut and it sharpens as it lands; pull 28 f to 0.65 on E.glideOut.
techniques.use_when: A fast camera move between two parts of the product; the energetic join of a launch film.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm films with no whips; more than once a film.

techniques.name: Block step and silhouette
techniques.summary: Two flat blocks cover the old frame one frame each, then the incoming element appears as a flat silhouette of itself and steps back to the real thing in three even steps.
techniques.recipe: <BlockStep frame at blocks={[rectA, rectB]} silhouette={{ rect: incomingBox, decay: 3 }} outgoing incoming />; declares its flashes and stepped frames.
techniques.timing: 1 frame per block, the silhouette at 1, 2/3, 1/3, 0 over three frames; on a hit.
techniques.use_when: A hard beat with nothing to carry across it.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm films; more than twice a film; never in the accent colour.
techniques.materials: The incoming page arrives as a pure white rectangle, then decays through grey to its real dark self one step a frame (white overlay opacity 1, 0.65, 0.35, 0, no easing between), landing on a VO syllable; a 2 px white rim light with a soft glow brightest at the bottom-left keeps the page's edge lit from below.

techniques.name: Blob ring frames the statement
techniques.summary: A soft ring of one colour swirls in around the frame and holds the next statement in its clear middle, breathing (it tightens and loosens) while its centre wanders a little.
techniques.recipe: <BlobRing frame start hole soft tighten release wobble color /> over the statement.
techniques.timing: Swirl 8 f from 1.6x the rest hole; hole 0.74 x 1.12 of the frame, soft edge 0.36 of the radius; tighten to 0.86 over 28 f on M.ringTighten; wobble 25 px over 2 s.
techniques.use_when: A section change into one centred statement; two or three times a film at most.
techniques.avoid_when: Busy frames; a statement that is not centred.
techniques.materials: The brush blob under a word starts spinning, collapses edge-on into a thin vertical streak for one nearly empty frame, reappears as a thick open arc round the next word (ring thickness about 25 % of its radius), then grows about 3x a frame for 3-4 frames past the frame edge and settles as a breathing vignette (hole about 1250 x 1000 px). Ring body blurred 40-60 px with a lighter inner edge feathered 150-250 px; the words inside go from grey to ink and the accent word from a pale tint to the accent.

techniques.name: Soft wipe (feathered or gradient edge)
techniques.summary: The next shot is revealed behind a wide soft edge that decelerates across the frame (feathered), or a panel or picture washes on behind an edge as wide as most of it at one speed (gradient).
techniques.recipe: <Wipe frame start kind="feather" angle feather outgoing incoming /> (`feather` is the edge width in px; kind="gradient" for the wash, whose edge is 0.7 of `span`); edgeMask({ left: 250 }) on a line that scrolls through the frame. The wipe is finished on the frame its run ends (wipeEnd()), even when its edge lands a hair short of the frame: <Wipe> stops drawing the outgoing shot from there. A hard edge that pushes the old shot along is kind="push" (the panel push-wipe); a line of type keeps its edge about a letter wide (the soft-edge write-on, or the TypeLine preset `develop`).
techniques.timing: Feathered: 350 px edge at 1080p, 30 f on E.softOut (lands at about a third of its starting speed). Gradient: edge 70 % of the element it reveals, 3360 px/s at 1080p (112 px/f at 30 fps).
techniques.use_when: A quiet reveal across the frame or a panel.
techniques.avoid_when: A hard edge (that is the push-wipe, kind="push"); a line of type behind the wide gradient ramp (it reads as half-faded words, fade soup).
techniques.materials: The photos first take a gradient-map cast that creeps in from the top-left (shadows deep, mids pink, highlights warm, strength 0 -> 70 % over 24 f), then a broad soft white wash crosses left to right (feather about 40 % of the panel width, accelerating); just ahead of the white the photos turn warm, and the warm front rhymes with the palette of the sentence that follows.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: The interface cast in relief under one key
techniques.summary: The product's screens and cards stand as shallow blocks on a floor of their own colour, lit by one directional key: every raised thing casts a shadow, sits on a contact shadow and shows lit and shaded faces in one hue, so the film reads as an object in light instead of a flat screen.
techniques.recipe: Lay the interface out on the floor in px at 1080p and give each element a height by importance (4-40 px; a hero up to 260). Draw it with <ReliefScene blocks camera keyLight floor ink /> under a high three-quarter camera (pitch 50-62, focal about 1.8 x frame height); map each card's HTML onto its top face with `content`. Key from keyLightState: house elevation 34, azimuth 315; one shadow group at 0.18 of ink (up to 0.45 at night on a deep ground) with a fixed 1.5 px penumbra. Taller blocks shade the tops of lower ones automatically. Blur the far rows in a second scene with one fixed blur for depth.
techniques.timing: The camera drifts or trucks on every hold (creep); the key moves on its own clock (a rake of 20-40 deg over a shot, or a light event).
techniques.use_when: A product with a real interface (cards, lists, a dashboard) and a story about what matters in it.
techniques.avoid_when: Photographic product footage carries the film; a relief next to footage reads as two worlds.

techniques.name: Noon lift: the light climbs and one thing keeps its shadow
techniques.summary: A raking key climbs from 8 to 72 degrees in about 1.2 s: every long shadow collapses and the world brightens, while the one element the product surfaces keeps rising and keeps the only long shadow.
techniques.recipe: In a relief (cl-key-light-relief) add the event { kind: 'noon', at, from: 8, to: 72 } (house 1.2 s on E.strongInOut). Ten frames after it starts, raise the surfaced block's height 18 -> 260 px over about 1.2 s on E.glideOut and give its top face the accent. Push the camera toward it on the same beat. Print the line about it raised on the floor in front of it so its shadow shrinks too.
techniques.timing: Lift 72 f; rise 70-75 f starting 10 f in; shadows: a 20 px card goes from 142 px to 6 px, the 260 px block keeps 84 px.
techniques.use_when: The film's point is that one thing matters among many (the alert, the free hour, the anomaly).
techniques.avoid_when: Nothing in the world is raised: the lift then only brightens a flat ground.

techniques.name: Stop-motion collage build
techniques.summary: The evidence for one claim piles up as cut-out pieces born whole on an irregular hand-timed cadence, some re-cut larger, a faint oversized ghost here and there, the camera stepping on births and one slow push underneath.
techniques.recipe: const s = collage({ n, start, seed, mean: 4, min: 1, max: 10, camera: { push: { at, dur: 92, amount: 0.3 } } }, film); draw each piece where collageElement(frame, i, s).on, at its scale, inside <Stepped fps={16}>; the push from collageCamera outside it. Pieces carry real content (a chart, log lines, a deploy chip, a teammate), never grey bars.
techniques.timing: Births every 4 f on average (1-10 f), re-cuts x1.8-2.1 7-10 f later, ghosts 5-8 f at 0.08-0.15, push +30 % over 92 f (M.collagePush).
techniques.use_when: Many small proofs of one point; an update with several changes shown at once.
techniques.avoid_when: Pieces would need to be read one by one: then show them one per beat.
techniques.materials: Every tile lands as a flat colour block first: a solid pastel rectangle cuts on, and 2-6 f later the photo replaces it in exactly that rectangle (a hard swap, no cross-fade); some tiles never resolve; tile pops on the 8th-note hats.

techniques.name: Mosaic iris from a point
techniques.summary: A ring of square cells in the accent's own family opens from a point the eye is on (a status dot, a period) and the next scene shows clear inside it.
techniques.recipe: <MosaicIris at origin={dot} frames={18} ring={195} cell={30} colors={mosaicFamily(accent)} outgoing incoming />. Cells exist only in the ring; the inside is tinted and soft for its first 8 f.
techniques.timing: 18 f to the far corner, front-loaded (E.snapOut).
techniques.use_when: The outgoing shot ends on a small round mark.
techniques.avoid_when: The point is near a frame edge (half the ring is lost).

techniques.name: Corner markers that stretch and snap
techniques.summary: Small squares on the corners of the word or figure in focus jump to the next target on a 16 fps clock: their leading ends jump, their trailing ends follow a pose behind, a long stretch splits into a piece and an echo; no tween frames.
techniques.recipe: <Markers boxes={[...]} onsets={[...]} /> with boxes from the type layout and onsets on word onsets (house size 24, jump 0.83, lead 0.38, trail 0.315). Optional blink { seed } for an uneven flicker.
techniques.timing: Settled in 5-6 poses (8-9 f at 24 fps).
techniques.use_when: Pointing at one word, a number, a UI element while the copy reads.
techniques.avoid_when: More than one target at once.

techniques.name: The supplied mark cast in the film's relief
techniques.summary: The brand's logo, supplied as SVG, is cast in the same lit relief as the film: its parts slide in from alternating edges and stop dead with their shadows, the part that plays the film's device rises and takes the accent, then the mark slides aside and the name arrives hot, printed raised on the floor.
techniques.recipe: logoParts(svg) -> per part pathPolys() -> ReliefScene blocks (h 20-30 px; the device part rises to 60-80 px on E.snapOut); offsets from assembleFor(); lockupState().x slides the blocks; the name as raised floor type with hotGlyphState colours; the key moves slowly through the hold (azimuth +15-25 deg) so the end lock is alive without a glow.
techniques.timing: Assembly about 1.3 s, the device rise 30 f, the slide 34 f, the name a letter every 5 f.
techniques.use_when: A film built as a relief or with a key-lit world; any supplied mark without holes or with simple parts.
techniques.avoid_when: Logos with fine detail under 2 % of the mark (they become slivers in relief).

techniques.name: Move accelerates into the cut
techniques.summary: The shot leaves by speeding up (a drift, a push, a pull-back, a card shrinking away) and the cut lands on its fastest frame; even a slow push that would normally settle keeps rising into the cut.
techniques.recipe: scaleBreath (push into .cut) or punchOut; put the cut on .cut / peakFrame. Anatomy: Ease-in over the last 6-24 f; a held line growing 0.18 %/f then +3.2 % in its last 6 f; a 3-frame counter-move (0.997, 0.990, 0.976) after a slow push. Sound: Kick 24 ms after the cut; a riser or a level swell into it; a spoken word on the cut.
techniques.timing: Last 6-70 f on an ease-in; cut speed 6-30 px/f or 0.4-1.5 %/f.
techniques.use_when: Nearly every cut; the end of a film (the last frame at peak speed).
techniques.avoid_when: Settling into the cut (that reads as a stall).

techniques.name: Asymmetric whip: long build, short brake
techniques.summary: A fast reframe whose speed builds for most of the move and brakes in the last third, crisp at the peak (no blur needed below about 100 px/f at 1080p); the copy swaps inside the peak frames.
techniques.recipe: whip({ frames: 32 }) + swapAt(whip.peak). Anatomy: Build 60-70 % of the move, brake 30-40 %; a slight zoom-out rides along; placeholder -> typed swap at the peak; a second, faster whip can follow immediately. Sound: A pop or a pluck at the peak (within 30 ms).
techniques.timing: 23-69 f; peak 50-178 px/f at 63-70 % of the move; house 32 f, peak 1600 px/s.
techniques.use_when: Changing subject inside one shot; racing up or down a phone; tilting into darkness.
techniques.avoid_when: Symmetric eases (they read as a slide).

techniques.name: Camera follows the caret
techniques.summary: While text types in a field cropped by the frame, the camera pans with the caret (in pulses, starting a few frames before the typing), and may pull back in one frame to show the whole field when the line ends.
techniques.recipe: typeSchedule() positions -> a camera x with a short lead; the jump-out as a HardStep on the framing. Anatomy: Pan speed 1-40 px/f tracking the caret; the pan starts 7 f before the typing; a one-frame jump-out at the end; a decaying roll drift while the next label types. Sound: Spacebar presses.
techniques.timing: Over the typing (50-145 f); jump-out 1 f; settle 32 f.
techniques.use_when: Typing in close-up.
techniques.avoid_when: Following every character exactly (lead it slightly).

techniques.name: The camera operates a flat UI
techniques.summary: The real app UI is never animated as layers: the camera zooms out, scrolls and pushes over one flat canvas, so the product looks untouched and the editing does the talking.
techniques.recipe: One camera() on a single flat or built canvas; moves from lib/camera-moves. Anatomy: Zooms x0.70-0.92 and scrolls 94-551 px; a symmetric 1.33x zoom; an S-curve push of +30 % on a finished layout. Sound: Voice.
techniques.timing: Zooms 30-40 f; calm scroll+zoom 75 f; S-push 92 f.
techniques.use_when: Walkthroughs of a real product from screenshots.
techniques.avoid_when: Fake layer animation on a screenshot.

techniques.name: Base sinks away from the launching object
techniques.summary: As an object launches (a send button, a card), the camera pushes slightly while the base it sat on drifts down and accelerates out of frame, so the object seems to lift off.
techniques.recipe: parallax with the base on its own layer and an E.buildIn drop. Anatomy: Camera push +2-4 %; base y on an ease-in to about 29 px/f; never settles. Sound: Kicks under it.
techniques.use_when: The moment a request is sent; an object leaving its container.
techniques.avoid_when: Moving the object itself fast at the same time.

techniques.name: Composition jump-reframes on each arrival
techniques.summary: While a collage is sparse, the whole composition jumps in one frame (about 180 px, or x1.11) each time an element arrives, holding 2-10 f between jumps.
techniques.recipe: collage({ camera }) steps on births (x1.05-1.11 or 150-200 px). Anatomy: Single-frame reframes on births; holds 2-10 f. Sound: None needed.
techniques.timing: Holds 2-10 f.
techniques.use_when: Stop-motion collage builds.
techniques.avoid_when: Smooth films.

techniques.name: Zoom into an object on a log curve
techniques.summary: A point or a small object grows by 3-8x in log space (accelerating then decelerating, or decelerating from the start) and keeps going past frame fill, softening as it grows; an input box can enter barrel-distorted and straighten as it grows.
techniques.recipe: zoomThrough({ factor, frames, ease }) with lc() log blending. Anatomy: Scale on a log curve (tau about 7-15 f on the tail), slight roll 2.5 -> 0 deg/f; optional softening; barrel bulge for 6 f at the start. Sound: The fastest frame on a vocal sound or a glockenspiel note. Materials: The world is seen through a feathered porthole that opens faster than the footage zooms: the window grows about 7.6x (feathered 6 % of the radius) while the plate inside scales only about 1.9x, on twos with a few single-frame exceptions; the plate is a soft, deliberately upscaled frame.
techniques.timing: 50-86 f for x3-8; peak 0.25 log/f.
techniques.use_when: Dot to planet, a mark to a world, the prompt box becoming the stage.
techniques.avoid_when: Linear scale (it reads as slowing down).
techniques.materials: The world is seen through a feathered porthole that opens faster than the footage zooms: the window grows about 7.6x (feathered 6 % of the radius) while the plate inside scales only about 1.9x, on twos with a few single-frame exceptions; the plate is a soft, deliberately upscaled frame.

techniques.name: Long exponential camera settle
techniques.summary: One long move that decays exponentially over 1-2.5 s (a pull-back of 15 %, a 357 px slide, a layout easing out to 0.88, a push of 1.21x on a finished line), settling just before the next beat; it can start with a tiny anticipation push.
techniques.recipe: A move on E.glideOut (or a decayEase) between two framings; anticipation via reversal with a short pull. Anatomy: Quint- or circ-out; t50 about 0.12-0.2 s, t90 about 0.6 s; optional +0.8 % push before a pull-back. Sound: The bed; the next beat lands on the settle.
techniques.timing: 46-160 f; tau about 48 f.
techniques.use_when: Calm shots after a busy one; holds on photos and dashboards.
techniques.avoid_when: Ending the settle after the next cut (then it is not a settle).

techniques.name: Macro pan across giant type
techniques.summary: The camera slides across type so big it never fits the frame (half the frame height or more), fast at first and decaying, crisp in the centre and soft at the frame edges; a timeline can pan toward the past with speed swells.
techniques.recipe: camera x on E.snapOut over a single huge <Words>; edge softness as a static mask with two blur levels. Anatomy: Start 300+ px/f decaying about 1/t; edge softening; swells (185 px/f, 318 -> 20 -> 261...) while a tilt accelerates. Sound: Kicks on the cut and mid-pan; a stab at the end.
techniques.use_when: A giant number, a date line, a word as landscape.
techniques.avoid_when: Text that must be read whole.

techniques.name: Camera reframes to make room
techniques.summary: When a new element is about to arrive, the camera (or the content) pulls back, shrinks or slides to make room, timed to finish one frame before the new element shows; a push can stay centred on an inline icon so the words part around it.
techniques.recipe: A camera move ending at the new element's onset - 1 (whip or E.glideOut); for an icon-centred push, anchor = the icon. Anatomy: Pull-back to 0.69-0.75; a kick of -6.3 %/f at peak; a 368 px slide with an early speed peak (18 % of the move) and a long tail; a two-phase pull (decelerate, re-accelerate, settle). Sound: A kick or a click. Materials: When the cluster outgrows the panel, the whole composition shrinks about 18 % between two drawings with no in-betweens (no blur, no overshoot), paired with a new tile's cut-on, and the slow pan continues.
techniques.timing: 30-60 f; peak at 18-56 % of the move.
techniques.use_when: Adding a second line, more cards, a label, a result under a search bar.
techniques.avoid_when: Making room after the element has appeared.
techniques.materials: When the cluster outgrows the panel, the whole composition shrinks about 18 % between two drawings with no in-betweens (no blur, no overshoot), paired with a new tile's cut-on, and the slow pan continues.

techniques.name: Masonry wall scrolls in, drifts, scrolls out
techniques.summary: A masonry of framed photo cards with words in the gaps scrolls up on an expo-out entry, decays to a slow drift, then leaves on a circ-in.
techniques.recipe: flickState with a short ramp, or a camera y on E.snapOut then E.launchIn. Anatomy: Entry 22 px/f with 72 % of the travel in the first 10 %; drift 0.7-0.9 px/f; exit circ-in. Sound: The bed.
techniques.timing: In 60 f, cruise, out 42 f.
techniques.use_when: A wall of examples or use cases.
techniques.avoid_when: Text inside the moving cards.

techniques.name: Background plate speeds up and slows with the read
techniques.summary: An aerial footage plate zooms and pans continuously, faster in the intro, slower while text is on screen, faster again at the exit.
techniques.recipe: Footage speed keys or a camera creep() whose rate is keyed to the copy's on-screen spans. Anatomy: Zoom +0.20 %/f and pan -2.4 px/f in the intro, +0.09 %/f and -1.1 px/f under text. Sound: Follows the riser.
techniques.use_when: Footage behind type.
techniques.avoid_when: Fast plates under reading.

techniques.name: Punch-in zoom carried by a few frames
techniques.summary: A zoom whose change happens in 1-3 explosive frames after a short creep, then an expo tail; punch-ins can be hidden on spoken words, and two punches in a row replace one push.
techniques.recipe: <SnapZoom to pre post defocus>. Anatomy: Creep (+0.04 -> +3.3 %/f), 1-3 big frames (x1.15, 1.38, 1.60), tail; x1.11-1.47 per punch; optional 5.6 px defocus on the jump frame and a 3 f ease-in before. Sound: On the spoken word (-10 ms) or the hit.
techniques.timing: 18-45 f in all; jump 1-3 f; tail 20-40 f.
techniques.use_when: A hit, a label landing, the spoken key word.
techniques.avoid_when: Every cut (save it for hits).

techniques.name: Ring or field spins in and bleeds off
techniques.summary: A ring of chips, a ring of tiles or a whole field of tiles arrives already turning and its rotation decays by a constant ratio to a slow cruise that never stops.
techniques.recipe: Build: rotationDecay(f, { start, w0: 8, ratio: 0.94, cruise: 0.5 }) (fx/Orbit, degrees and ratios per 60 fps frame): the ring arrives turning at w0 and bleeds off by the ratio to a cruise that never stops, closed form; <OrbitRing decay> draws the ring. Anatomy: Start 2.5-15 deg/f, decay x0.88-0.95 a frame, cruise 0.1-2.4 deg/f. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: 30-100 f to the cruise.
techniques.use_when: Integrations, sources, a galaxy of features around a centre.
techniques.avoid_when: Rotation that stops dead.

techniques.name: Whip zoom with roll and counter-roll
techniques.summary: The camera whips to a new subject with an accelerating zoom (about x2) and a roll of up to +17-28 deg with motion blur, then counter-rolls past level and settles; a flat grid can tip into a perspective floor this way; a whip-left with a x1.9 zoom lands on the end of a sentence.
techniques.recipe: whip({ roll, dip }) with the motion-blur pass on the fast frames. Anatomy: Zoom peak 1.078 a frame, roll +2.3 to +5.2 deg/f then a counter-roll to -4.5 deg/f; blur on the fastest frames. Sound: None needed; a kick on the landing.
techniques.use_when: A big change of subject; flat to 3D.
techniques.avoid_when: Roll over about 30 deg; readable text during the whip.

techniques.name: Background steps back behind the type
techniques.summary: The picture behind a line gets a pale haze and a defocus, a canvas fades into a blurred image, a colour field fades to the neutral stage under the UI, or a dark vignetted plate puts the headline in the bright centre.
techniques.recipe: <RackFocus levels> on the background with a veil layer; vignette as a static plate. Anatomy: Background luma lifted (151 -> 224) and defocused; or a vignette with corners at a third of the centre. Sound: None. Materials: Calm, uncanny photoreal plates (a lone chair in a meadow, a misty window) in one cool grade carry the copy: an elliptical vignette about 45 % darker at the corners, a lift behind the type, saturation about 0.7; the plates creep almost imperceptibly (0.02-0.4 % a frame) while the copy changes on them.
techniques.timing: 30-38 f; a fade 23 f sine.
techniques.use_when: Type over footage or a busy picture.
techniques.avoid_when: Dark drop shadows behind type.
techniques.materials: Calm, uncanny photoreal plates (a lone chair in a meadow, a misty window) in one cool grade carry the copy: an elliptical vignette about 45 % darker at the corners, a lift behind the type, saturation about 0.7; the plates creep almost imperceptibly (0.02-0.4 % a frame) while the copy changes on them.

techniques.name: Object materialises through a colour wash
techniques.summary: A board or object starts as a flat colour overlay and sweeps through tints before landing on its true colours; or an object is recoloured through a gradient map for 5 frames on a hit.
techniques.recipe: <Develop> (duotone tint -> full colour) for the wash; a one-hue flash as a HardStep overlay on the object. Anatomy: Overlay colour -> tints -> true colours; gradient-map flash on an object within 22 f. Sound: A hit on the flash.
techniques.timing: Wash 54 f; flash 10 f inside 22 f.
techniques.use_when: The first appearance of a product board; a hit on a dock or icon row.
techniques.avoid_when: A second multi-hue wash in the same film.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: The cut frame glows and decays
techniques.summary: On the cut frame the whole stage lifts into a soft glow centred on the subject and decays by a constant ratio over half a second; a dark scene can open over-bloomed and let its halo fall.
techniques.recipe: <Exposure> with up 0, peak on the cut and down 30 on an exponential. Anatomy: Peak on one frame, decay x0.92 a frame toward the base; halo falls about 70 %. Sound: A whoosh into the cut, or an orchestral stab on the beat.
techniques.timing: Peak 1 f, decay 30-39 f.
techniques.use_when: A cut onto a small bright subject on a dark stage.
techniques.avoid_when: Light stages (it reads as a flash fault).

techniques.name: Soft blobs drift behind the copy
techniques.summary: Large soft colour masses (500-900 px) drift and breathe slowly behind the type, so no ground is flat; a blob can wander continuously and ignore the cuts, or drift and shrink behind a held logo; the colourway can change on cuts.
techniques.recipe: <LightField pools={[...]}> with Lissajous loops; colourway per shot. Anatomy: 22-37 % of the frame each, about 1 px a frame, area breathing; variant: static soft glows bleeding from the corners with faint layout lines. Sound: None. Materials: A mesh gradient built from two inks: saturated pools of the accent in a pale grey-tinted base with near-white highlights along one S-shaped ribbon; blob blur 25-35 % of the frame width; the shapes drift and bend about 0.5 % a frame and stay continuous across cuts in the same colourway. Two-lobe version: a cool lobe and a warm lobe meeting at a soft vertical seam where their mix shows, the shape morphing from a wedge to an ellipse to a pill over about 2 s spans. Add grain at 1.5-2 % or bake the lobes as dithered plates: large soft gradients band at 8 bits.
techniques.timing: Continuous; contours repeating every 60 f, bands every 116 f; drift 87 f decelerating.
techniques.use_when: Text-led films on a coloured ground.
techniques.avoid_when: A second mesh field in other hues; blobs that move faster than about 1 px a frame.
techniques.materials: A mesh gradient built from two inks: saturated pools of the accent in a pale grey-tinted base with near-white highlights along one S-shaped ribbon; blob blur 25-35 % of the frame width; the shapes drift and bend about 0.5 % a frame and stay continuous across cuts in the same colourway. Two-lobe version: a cool lobe and a warm lobe meeting at a soft vertical seam where their mix shows, the shape morphing from a wedge to an ellipse to a pill over about 2 s spans. Add grain at 1.5-2 % or bake the lobes as dithered plates: large soft gradients band at 8 bits.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Cards flood with colour and defocus one by one
techniques.summary: On the line "more than anyone can track", each card turns fully into the brand colour and blurs into a soft blob in a few frames, staggered around the ring, then the whole frame fades to white.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: Cards with an overlay of the accent (opacity tween) and RackFocus levels per card; Exposure to white at the end. Anatomy: Per card a colour flood overlay plus a fixed defocus ladder; clockwise stagger; white fade. Sound: Voice cadence.
techniques.timing: Flood 8 f, fade 10 f, stagger 5-6 f.
techniques.use_when: Showing overload: too many tools, tabs, tasks.
techniques.avoid_when: Light brand colours (the blobs disappear).

techniques.name: Floor glow under the stage, brightening into reveals
techniques.summary: A one-hue glow rises from the bottom 25-30 % of the frame under UI or type; it brightens into reveals and transitions, can undulate in soft lobes, and is stronger on the end card.
techniques.recipe: <LightField floor={{ plate, height: 0.27, breathe, rises }}>. Bake each stop set with scripts/dither-gradient.py (kind floor) and move the plates by transform; never an animated CSS gradient. Anatomy: Bottom band luma rising 4 -> 189 into a reveal; lobes slowly undulating; strength stepping up on the end card. Sound: A sub-bass hit on the rise; an outro pad under the sink. Materials: The floor glow is a horizon at dusk, not one colour: a near-white core with a cool tint at the very bottom edge, then the accent body, a deeper hue and a fade to black (radial ellipse about 140 % of the frame wide and 60 % tall, centred just below the frame); it rises over about 68 f as the panel rises. The closing version is a row of 4-5 soft lobes along the bottom third (500-700 px wide, blur about 80 px) with darker gaps, rising and falling out of phase (20-40 px, 2-4 s periods) and sinking 300 px in 30 f before the logo. A three-hue aurora can rise under a translucent prompt box (coverage 2 -> 28 % of the panel in 48 f, then breathing 25-35 %, its core drifting and tilting about 20 deg), visible through the box's lower third.
techniques.timing: Rise 68 f ease-out; continuous breathing; sinks 32 f at the end.
techniques.use_when: Dark or near-white product stages that should not be flat.
techniques.avoid_when: Glow behind a single element; saturated glow.
techniques.materials: The floor glow is a horizon at dusk, not one colour: a near-white core with a cool tint at the very bottom edge, then the accent body, a deeper hue and a fade to black (radial ellipse about 140 % of the frame wide and 60 % tall, centred just below the frame); it rises over about 68 f as the panel rises. The closing version is a row of 4-5 soft lobes along the bottom third (500-700 px wide, blur about 80 px) with darker gaps, rising and falling out of phase (20-40 px, 2-4 s periods) and sinking 300 px in 30 f before the logo. A three-hue aurora can rise under a translucent prompt box (coverage 2 -> 28 % of the panel in 48 f, then breathing 25-35 %, its core drifting and tilting about 20 deg), visible through the box's lower third.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Soft light hops to the active card
techniques.summary: A soft light appears behind one card or tile and moves to the next as each becomes active; a dark grid of keycap tiles lights up tile by tile as labels fade in.
techniques.recipe: LightField pool moved between card centres on E.snapOut. Anatomy: Soft light about 100 px around the active element; moves card to card; grows about 2.5x on the tile variant. Sound: None, or a soft tick per hop. Materials: The light is motivated: a small passing foreground dot leaves a soft radial glow on each card it crosses (a pale accent tint at about 0.55 at the core, radius about 70 px), blooming 2 f after the dot passes and fading over 20 f, so the glow seems lit by the dot.
techniques.timing: 28 f per hop; tile bloom 14 f.
techniques.use_when: Walking through KPI cards or a grid of features.
techniques.avoid_when: Glow halos on light grounds.
techniques.materials: The light is motivated: a small passing foreground dot leaves a soft radial glow on each card it crosses (a pale accent tint at about 0.55 at the core, radius about 70 px), blooming 2 f after the dot passes and fading over 20 f, so the glow seems lit by the dot.
conditions: light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo

techniques.name: Ghost pre-flash of an upcoming element
techniques.summary: A huge, faint version of an element that is about to arrive flashes behind the frame for a few frames before the real element lands.
techniques.recipe: Build: <GhostPreflash land x y>{element}</GhostPreflash> (fx/Flashes): the element at 5.5x, 12 %, for 6 f (creeping 8 % larger), ending 6 f before it lands; a stepped run. Anatomy: Oversized ghost (5-6x) at 8-15 % strength for 5-8 f; the real element lands 3-11 f later. Sound: A whoosh on the flash. Materials: The ghost can be any layer of the coming shot: a full-frame tinted texture at about 35 % for 10 f, a huge faint line etching at about 10 % and twice its final size for 16 f, a silhouette for 2 f, a coloured glow at 20 % screen over the current plate for 20 f. Small marks can do the same job: corner marks switch to the next shot's accent 4-8 f before the cut, one corner a frame.
techniques.timing: Ghost 5-8 f; real element +3-11 f.
techniques.use_when: A collage or stop-motion build that should anticipate its next piece.
techniques.avoid_when: Clean UI films.
techniques.materials: The ghost can be any layer of the coming shot: a full-frame tinted texture at about 35 % for 10 f, a huge faint line etching at about 10 % and twice its final size for 16 f, a silhouette for 2 f, a coloured glow at 20 % screen over the current plate for 20 f. Small marks can do the same job: corner marks switch to the next shot's accent 4-8 f before the cut, one corner a frame.

techniques.name: Light bands flow along a column
techniques.summary: Bands of a lighter tint sweep down a coloured column at constant speed, new pulses every 25 f: the column reads as a channel with something flowing.
techniques.recipe: <LightField bands={[{ plate, width, y, period, dir: 'down' }]}>. Anatomy: Leading edge at a constant 256 px/f; pulses every 25 f. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Constant speed; continuous.
techniques.use_when: A pipe, a column, a stream of data.
techniques.avoid_when: Beat-locking it (it should run free).

techniques.name: Type filled with a gradient that blooms
techniques.summary: A key phrase grows a little and its fill turns from white into a soft gradient that blooms, or each word of a hero line carries its own soft gradient and lands in silence.
techniques.recipe: HueSweep with a brand path, or the phrase clipped to a baked dithered gradient plate revealed by opacity. Recipe: a glow copy (blur 20 px, opacity 0.5) under a fill copy clipped to a baked dithered gradient plate; scale on the wrapper. Anatomy: Fill shift white -> gradient over the scale-up (25-30 %), soft bloom; per-word gradients on paper. Sound: The music stops for about 1 s under it. Materials: Construction: the phrase grows 25-30 % over about 58 f while its fill shifts in the first 24 f from white to a horizontal two-hue gradient (a lilac-like left to a sky-like right), with a glow made of a duplicate blurred 18-24 px at about 50 % in a deeper hue behind it; the second word held slightly out of focus (4-6 px). Behind a card, big type can carry a gradient that fades from the saturated hue to nearly the ground colour across the word, so the card in front reads first and the phrase reads as an echo.
techniques.timing: 42-68 f expo-out.
techniques.use_when: A brand that owns a gradient; a hero line once.
techniques.avoid_when: More than one gradient phrase per film; a gradient that is not the film's own family.
techniques.materials: Construction: the phrase grows 25-30 % over about 58 f while its fill shifts in the first 24 f from white to a horizontal two-hue gradient (a lilac-like left to a sky-like right), with a glow made of a duplicate blurred 18-24 px at about 50 % in a deeper hue behind it; the second word held slightly out of focus (4-6 px). Behind a card, big type can carry a gradient that fades from the saturated hue to nearly the ground colour across the word, so the card in front reads first and the phrase reads as an echo.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo

techniques.name: Ground gradient swaps or floods
techniques.summary: Behind a locked picture the two stops of a vertical gradient trade places; or a brand gradient floods half the frame behind stripes.
techniques.recipe: Baked dithered gradient plates cross-faded by opacity. Bake every gradient with scripts/dither-gradient.py from one stop list in the brand tokens. Anatomy: Stops swap over 48 f; flood coverage 0.14 -> 0.96 in 100 f. Sound: A reverse-cymbal swell. Materials: One gradient family everywhere: every gradient in the film (strips, light floods, skies, mesh grounds) uses the same five stops, ordered by lightness so no muddy midpoint appears (e.g. a warm stop always sits between the hot hue and white, never beside the cool one); large soft gradients carry a fine per-pixel dither (sigma about 0.75 levels) that only shows under a contrast boost. Variants: a diagonal three-hue ground under floating panels; a pale sky radial (near-white centre, pale blue corners) with blurred clouds drifting about 0.5 px/f that hides every UI scene in air.
techniques.use_when: Any film that carries one gradient family.
techniques.avoid_when: House films.
techniques.materials: One gradient family everywhere: every gradient in the film (strips, light floods, skies, mesh grounds) uses the same five stops, ordered by lightness so no muddy midpoint appears (e.g. a warm stop always sits between the hot hue and white, never beside the cool one); large soft gradients carry a fine per-pixel dither (sigma about 0.75 levels) that only shows under a contrast boost. Variants: a diagonal three-hue ground under floating panels; a pale sky radial (near-white centre, pale blue corners) with blurred clouds drifting about 0.5 px/f that hides every UI scene in air.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: A photo turned into a two- or three-ink gradient map
techniques.summary: A photograph (clouds, a landscape, a soft figure) is mapped by luminance onto the film's inks: shadows to the deep ink, mids to the accent, highlights to a pale tint, so real imagery carries the brand palette; the map can hold or drift slowly (a head turning from one ink to the next).
techniques.recipe: Photo with a gradeFilter table built from the brand stops (SVG feComponentTransfer); a drifting map = two statically filtered copies cross-faded by opacity, never an animated filter. Anatomy: Desaturate, then a three-stop table per channel (dark, mid, light); an optional blur (12-30 px) for a defocused figure; slow drift about 2 px/f; optional tiny specks and soft horizontal glints over a two-ink field. Sound: Music; no sound of its own. Materials: Two-ink field: luminance 0 -> deep ink, 0.5 -> accent, 1 -> pale tint. Infrared: swap the red and green channels so foliage turns crimson while the sky stays blue. Defocused figure: blur 30 px, then a four-stop map whose head and body stops drift apart.
techniques.timing: Holds a whole shot; a drifting map changes its stops over 30-100 f with no snaps.
techniques.use_when: Real imagery that must live in a strong palette; an opening field; an infrared or thermal flavour for vision and generation products.
techniques.avoid_when: Faces that must read naturally; product screenshots.
techniques.materials: Two-ink field: luminance 0 -> deep ink, 0.5 -> accent, 1 -> pale tint. Infrared: swap the red and green channels so foliage turns crimson while the sky stays blue. Defocused figure: blur 30 px, then a four-stop map whose head and body stops drift apart.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Ground colour changes per shot and per act
techniques.summary: The ground itself is a beat: shots alternate paper, black with a fine grid, a full brand field, a texture; an act flips the film from a light stage to a dark world and stays there; brand moments sit on a warm stage and the product on a cool one.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a GROUNDS list in the timeline indexed by shot; the flip is a hard cut. Anatomy: A ground per shot from a set of 3-5; one act flip per film; one ground per world. Sound: A music change on the act flip.
techniques.timing: Changes on cuts and transitions only.
techniques.use_when: Any film with more than four shots.
techniques.avoid_when: Two neighbouring shots on the same ground with different content.

techniques.name: Ground darkens or drains as an exit
techniques.summary: The white page darkens to black with luma halving per frame while its elements shrink out; a panel drains to grey and darkens slowly; the ground dims to true black under an opening.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: ground colour tween on E.buildIn; shrink the elements with exits 'launch' on scale. Anatomy: Accelerating darken (ease-in), chips shrinking one by one; drain S-curve then linear darken. Sound: A snare starting it. Materials: Grades as a transition: before a chapter cut the whole frame drains (saturation about 60 -> 15 %, brightness to 0.75) over 16 f ease-in, then a hard cut lands on the brightest frame of the film, so the cut reads as a flash without a white frame. When a white page darkens (luma halving each frame), white pills that were invisible on it suddenly read as raised capsules for a beat before they shrink away.
techniques.timing: 25-40 f; drain 33 f then 128 f.
techniques.use_when: The end of a section; an opening that builds on black.
techniques.avoid_when: A plain fade to black between unrelated shots.
techniques.materials: Grades as a transition: before a chapter cut the whole frame drains (saturation about 60 -> 15 %, brightness to 0.75) over 16 f ease-in, then a hard cut lands on the brightest frame of the film, so the cut reads as a flash without a white frame. When a white page darkens (luma halving each frame), white pills that were invisible on it suddenly read as raised capsules for a beat before they shrink away.

techniques.name: Ground flips on one frame as punctuation
techniques.summary: The background inverts (dark to light) on one frame while the objects stay; or a whole background layer switches from dim grey to the accent on the key word; or a colour change passes through a one-frame near-black dip on a pop.
techniques.recipe: HardStep on the ground colour; the dip as a one-frame fill. Anatomy: One-frame switch; optional one-frame dip; objects unchanged. Sound: The resolving word or a pop 33 ms after. Materials: Ground and type swap colours through one half-blend frame: the type turns 50 % for a single frame, then the whole palette has swapped (accent type on white instead of white on accent) while small labels keep their colour.
techniques.timing: 1-2 f; a dip variant 12 f to the dip, 10 f back.
techniques.use_when: The key word of a line; a beat inside a held shot.
techniques.avoid_when: More than one or two per film (polarity flips are the loudest punctuation).
techniques.materials: Ground and type swap colours through one half-blend frame: the type turns 50 % for a single frame, then the whole palette has swapped (accent type on white instead of white on accent) while small labels keep their colour.

techniques.name: Hard colour swaps that step the size
techniques.summary: A shape (a pair of circles, discs, a column) hard-cuts through three fills a few frames apart, each swap also stepping it about 4 % larger; or a column switches colour on the frame it passes half its width.
techniques.recipe: fillSwapState(f, { at, n: 3, every: 10, grow: 0.04, fills }). Anatomy: 3 swaps, each with a scale step x1.04; text dims a frame before; variant: a column widens 6x and swaps colour at half width with a band of the old colour inside. Sound: Swaps next to a kick and a sub-drop. Materials: The pair cuts through three fills, each held exactly 10 f and each slightly larger (+4 % a step), on third-beats; the text colour switches on the same frame as the fill, and the words can first sink into the disc colour over 6 f before the first swap.
techniques.timing: Swaps 10 f apart at 60 fps (6 Hz); widen 20 f cubic-out.
techniques.use_when: A beat-cut on a simple graphic; building energy before a reveal.
techniques.avoid_when: More than one run per act.
techniques.materials: The pair cuts through three fills, each held exactly 10 f and each slightly larger (+4 % a step), on third-beats; the text colour switches on the same frame as the fill, and the words can first sink into the disc colour over 6 f before the first swap.

techniques.name: Heat ramp as the arrival and exit colour system
techniques.summary: Every arrival cools from a warm tint to the ink and every exit heats back up and bleaches to white; colour leads the fade, so type seems to burn in and burn out.
techniques.recipe: HueSweep with back for exits (one hue path, lightness doing the work). Anatomy: Arrival: pale warm -> accent -> deep -> ink; exit: ink -> warm -> pale -> white, colour leading opacity. Sound: None of its own.
techniques.timing: Cool 10-15 f; heat 8-23 f.
techniques.use_when: A whole film's colour grammar, one film at a time.
techniques.avoid_when: Brands without a warm accent; mixing with other accent systems.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
techniques.ban_safe_variant: One hue: pale accent -> accent -> ink on arrival, the reverse plus a fade on exit.

techniques.name: Small token cycles through hues
techniques.summary: A version number or a pill border keeps cycling through hues (or a rotating multi-colour stroke) while the wordmark stays ink.
techniques.recipe: Brand path colour cycle; the border as a conic gradient (a baked plate) rotated by transform. Anatomy: Hue stops 22-26 f each; a border gradient rotating about 6 deg a frame. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Stops 22-26 f; continuous.
techniques.use_when: A version tag or an "active" pill in a brand with a multi-colour system.
techniques.avoid_when: House films (it reads as a template).
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
techniques.ban_safe_variant: The token breathes in lightness at the accent hue (a 0.05-0.10 L swing over 1-2 s).

techniques.name: Core glows up to white-hot
techniques.summary: The core of a hero object brightens to white with a soft halo (or a point's halo blooms wide and contracts, or a held word sits on a faint bloom).
techniques.recipe: A baked halo plate whose opacity follows haloLevel(); never an animated blur. Anatomy: Core brightness 153 -> 240 in luma with a halo; halo 250 px contracting to 120 px in one step; repeated beats. Sound: A celesta note 53 ms before.
techniques.timing: 19 f cubic-out, repeated; halo held 5 f then one-step contraction.
techniques.use_when: A brand that supplies glow; a living hero object.
techniques.avoid_when: House films (a radial glow is the stock look).
conditions: light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo

techniques.name: Light cone drops and flashes twice
techniques.summary: An inverted-triangle beam drops from the top edge, widening, and flashes colour twice on UI pops.
techniques.recipe: LightField glowRise on a static cone plate scaled by transform; flashes as opacity steps. Anatomy: Width 487 -> 1447 px circ-out; two colour flashes 0.25 s apart. Sound: The second flash 34 ms after a UI pop.
techniques.timing: 38 f; flashes at about 15 f and 30 f.
techniques.use_when: A spotlight on a hero object.
techniques.avoid_when: Saturated beams.

techniques.name: A fluid swirl of light floods the dark frame and settles
techniques.summary: On an empty dark frame a fluid wave of light rolls in from one corner, a white-hot area followed by curling arms of a pale tint and the accent like ink in water lit from behind, and within half a second it calms into the slow drifting colour field that holds the logo or the line.
techniques.recipe: Exposure for the light rise plus baked blob plates rotated by transform; the displacement as a static turbulence map at two or three fixed strengths cross-faded, or a pre-rendered swirl clip. Anatomy: Three soft blobs (white, a pale tint, the accent) blurred 80-150 px, rotating about a corner pivot from 60 to 0 deg through a low-frequency displacement (scale 120 -> 0); peak mean luma about 4x the ground; settles into 3-4 drifting blobs. Sound: A whoosh or swell; the line lands after it. Materials: White hotspot, pale tint, accent, deep ground; the hotspot sits in the corner the swirl comes from and is the last thing to fade.
techniques.timing: 30-36 f from dark to the settled field.
techniques.use_when: A section opener or the frame before the logo on a dark film.
techniques.avoid_when: More than once; light grounds.
techniques.materials: White hotspot, pale tint, accent, deep ground; the hotspot sits in the corner the swirl comes from and is the last thing to fade.

techniques.name: Previous hero knocked back in one frame
techniques.summary: When the big type arrives, the previous hero drops to about 55 % strength in a single frame, so the eye moves to the new element.
techniques.recipe: Build: knockback(f, land) (fx/Flashes): the previous hero's strength drops to 55 % on the new hero's landing frame (one stepped frame). Anatomy: One-frame opacity step to 0.55. Sound: None.
techniques.use_when: Stacking a new statement over a previous visual.
techniques.avoid_when: Fading it slowly (that reads as indecision).

techniques.name: Element enters over-exposed and decays to its tone
techniques.summary: New figures appear as flat bright white for a few frames and drop to their real tone in one step; a cut-out subject flashes bright on release while the caption slips behind it.
techniques.recipe: Build: <EntryFlash at color> inside the arriving element (fx/MicroUI): a flat light overlay holds 10 f and drops in one step; mode="decay" fades 1 -> 0 in 5 f (the accent-flash tile on a cut-on). Anatomy: White hold 4 f, one-step drop, near and far figures 2 f apart; variant: +60 L* flash on release, decaying 20 f, with a depth swap of the caption. Sound: A mouse-click on the release. Materials: On the first frame after the white flash, figures arrive as one-frame vertical smears (about 150 px, luminance kept, a 3 px colour split), then sharp flat white silhouettes that decay to grey halftone.
techniques.timing: Hold 10 f, drop 1 f; flash hold 5 f, decay 20 f.
techniques.use_when: Figures arriving in a graphic world; the release moment of a selection.
techniques.avoid_when: Faces that must be read from the first frame.
techniques.materials: On the first frame after the white flash, figures arrive as one-frame vertical smears (about 150 px, luminance kept, a 3 px colour split), then sharp flat white silhouettes that decay to grey halftone.

techniques.name: Rainbow arcs, prism beams and auras composited into plates
techniques.summary: Generated or photographic plates carry light painted into them: a full spectral arc over a figure, a broad warm prism beam falling through the body, a soft aura behind the head, a horizontal spectral band across a face, floating double-exposed shapes and a local glow that fades slowly around the feet, all grained together with the plate.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: SVG and CSS overlays in screen blend over a Photo, plus one grain layer; bake each spectrum as a dithered PNG. Anatomy: Arc: a seven-stop spectrum stroke about 60 px wide, blur 6 px, screen at 0.6. Beam: transparent -> warm at 0.55 -> transparent over about 240 px. Aura: radial, about 260 px. Spectral band: about 20 % of the frame tall, screen at 0.45, blur 12 px. Local glow: radial about 150 px fading 0.8 -> 0.1 over a 240 f hold. Grain about 4 % over everything. Sound: None of its own. Materials: Arc stops outer to inner: red, coral, a thin yellow, a thin green, sky, violet, fading into the sky colour; double exposures at 45 % in lighten.
techniques.timing: Static in the plate; the camera push moves everything together; local glows fade across the hold.
techniques.use_when: An imaging or generation brand whose plates are the hero; slow holds.
techniques.avoid_when: Product UI; documentary footage.
techniques.materials: Arc stops outer to inner: red, coral, a thin yellow, a thin green, sky, violet, fading into the sky colour; double exposures at 45 % in lighten.
conditions: the film's one spectral accent

techniques.name: A window floats inside radial light streaks
techniques.summary: The final product window floats on black with a thin coloured rim light, and around it broad light streaks radiate from the frame centre (a warm one, a white one, a cool one, a deep one) separated by black gaps, bending past the corners like light leaking round the window.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a conic gradient of hard colour stops and black gaps baked as a dithered PNG, blurred once, radially masked and scaled by transform; the rim is a box-shadow. Anatomy: Rim 1.5 px plus a 4 px blur at about 60 % in a tint of the accent; streaks 200-400 px long, blurred 20-40 px, radial from the centre, hidden behind the window by a radial mask (transparent to 70 % of the closest side); drift outward about 1.5 px/f while the window pulls back 6 %. Sound: The last strong kicks. Materials: Conic stops e.g. warm 0-6 %, gap to 10 %, white 18 %, gap 24 %, cool 33 %, gap 40 %, deep 52 %; the window pure white.
techniques.timing: 30-40 f to the end.
techniques.use_when: The last product frame of a dark launch film, after a glass or light act.
techniques.avoid_when: Light grounds; the middle of a UI demo.
techniques.materials: Conic stops e.g. warm 0-6 %, gap to 10 %, white 18 %, gap 24 %, cool 33 %, gap 40 %, deep 52 %; the window pure white.
conditions: the film's one spectral accent

techniques.name: Image resolves through representations
techniques.summary: An image is generated in front of the viewer: coloured dots pop into a grid with accelerating density, recolour toward the photo, then one frame of halftone, one frame of pixel mosaic, then the sharp photo; or a post image fills like a progressive render on twos (blank, a soft blob, rough shapes, final).
techniques.recipe: Build: <Cascade at src x y w h cols rows unlit palette> (fx/Cascade): round dots pop in power-in 2.3 over 38 f up to 58 % of the cells (each 1.4x large, settling in 4 f) in seeded palette tints (or vivid picture colours), recolour to the picture (14 f), then one beat each of halftone, mosaic and the photo (2.4 f each); ghost lets the empty grid carry the picture; the grid is sampled from src once (useImageGrid) or passed as grid; mode="progressive" loads blank, three fixed blur levels, sharp, on twos (46 f). Start it from a QuadLoader on the grid's centre cells. Anatomy: Dot fill power-in (0.6 -> 58 % coverage), recolour 6 f, final stages 1 f each; progressive stages on twos. Sound: A chat pop, a bubble pop, a cork pop on the reveal. Materials: The generated image grows from a speck to full width on twos while its content evolves like a diffusion render: pastel blobs (blur 12 px), then coloured clouds over dunes, then candy-coloured hills, then the final picture, each state about 6 f and sharper than the last.
techniques.timing: Fill 38 f, recolour 14 f, stages 2-3 f each at 60 fps; progressive 46 f.
techniques.use_when: Image generation, rendering, any "it makes the picture" beat.
techniques.avoid_when: Without a final image that rewards the wait.
techniques.materials: The generated image grows from a speck to full width on twos while its content evolves like a diffusion render: pastel blobs (blur 12 px), then coloured clouds over dunes, then candy-coloured hills, then the final picture, each state about 6 f and sharper than the last.

techniques.name: Full-frame satin folds of colour that roll through hues
techniques.summary: Behind small captions the whole frame is a soft field of tall curved folds like satin or an aurora: dark ribbons sweep diagonally through bright bands and the colour phase slowly rolls from one hue through its neighbour into a deep shade; the calm cousin is a field of glossy diagonal stripes over a two-ink gradient that fades to black at the edges.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: render two fold plates offline as dithered PNGs (scripts/dither-gradient.py) and move and skew them by transform, cross-fading the two phases instead of animating colour. Anatomy: Folds: one colour strip, sin(x * 12 + 0.8 sin(y * 3) + t) through a four-stop ramp, skewed so the folds lean, blurred about 20 px; dark ribbons 80-140 px, highlights about 200 px; phase cycle about 2 s; ripple travel about 3 px/f. Stripes: highlight +12 % luma, 4 px blur, at 135 deg, drifting 1 px/f. Sound: VO or music only. Materials: Ramp: deep shade -> shadow hue -> accent -> highlight tint. Stripes over a radial gradient (120 % x 90 % at the lower left: light tint, accent at 45 %, near-black at 80 %).
techniques.timing: Continuous, never a held frame.
techniques.use_when: A section of short captions over pure colour; music-led films.
techniques.avoid_when: Under dense UI; next to another full-frame colour field.
techniques.materials: Ramp: deep shade -> shadow hue -> accent -> highlight tint. Stripes over a radial gradient (120 % x 90 % at the lower left: light tint, accent at 45 %, near-black at 80 %).
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: People become flat colour silhouettes
techniques.summary: The people in a collage of tiles switch to flat colour silhouettes with a scattered stagger, then the backgrounds go flat too: a segmentation look that says "the AI sees them".
techniques.recipe: Recipe: Cutouts mattes (hand-traced polygons) filled flat, switched on per tile with a seeded stagger. Anatomy: Per tile a matte layer in one flat colour; staggered over 4 f; backgrounds follow. Sound: None, or a soft scan.
techniques.timing: 23 f ease-in.
techniques.use_when: A film about vision, detection or editing.
techniques.avoid_when: Without hand-made mattes (it needs clean cut-outs).

techniques.name: A light sheen crosses a landing object once
techniques.summary: A soft pale band about 1.5 letters wide crosses the end logo or a turning object once; mirrored highlights glide along an object's rims; a title fades up with a light sweep and a 1.2-1.4x brightness overshoot.
techniques.recipe: <LightSweep band={0.45} frames={34}> clipped to the element; rims: LightSweep clipped to the stroke. Recipe: the rounded rect stroked twice with a bright dash (strokeDasharray 120 of 1000) moving in opposite directions from the end, plus a blurred glow copy. Anatomy: Band 0.45 of the element width moving at about 24 px/f; rim variant: two short streaks mirrored about the centre, front-loaded then linear. Sound: The final kick after the sweep. Materials: A bright C-shaped end cap on a glass pill's rounded end (peak luma 150-200 on a dark panel, glow about 10 px) holds 12 f, then divides: one highlight runs along the top rim and one along the bottom for about 40 f, like light rolling off a glass edge.
techniques.timing: 26-48 f near-linear (rim: fast start 39 px/f then 15-28 px/f).
techniques.use_when: An end logo landing, a hero object turning, a title reveal.
techniques.avoid_when: Repeating sheens; a sheen on every element.
techniques.materials: A bright C-shaped end cap on a glass pill's rounded end (peak luma 150-200 on a dark panel, glow about 10 px) holds 12 f, then divides: one highlight runs along the top rim and one along the bottom for about 40 f, like light rolling off a glass edge.

techniques.name: Coloured dots bleed along a border into one spectral ring
techniques.summary: A black pill border carries a few small coloured dots, each matching an integration or a category; colour leaks out of every dot along the border in both directions until the segments meet and the border is one continuous spectral ring, the dots shrinking as they empty, and the ring then turns slowly.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: per dot a copy of the rounded rect stroked in the dot's colour and masked by a dash (strokeDasharray 2 x spread, strokeDashoffset = position - spread) over a base copy in ink; spread on an in-out. Anatomy: Stroke 3 px, radius 20 px; per dot a gradient segment along the perimeter whose half-length grows from 0 to 25 % of the perimeter on an in-out; outside the segments the stroke stays ink with a soft mix; dots 9 -> 3 px losing 40 % saturation; the ring then rotates about 3 deg/f. Sound: The label swap and the ring's completion on one kick. Materials: Segment ends feather over about 8 % of the perimeter; neighbouring hues meet without a grey seam (order the dots by hue around the shape).
techniques.timing: Leak 12 f, dots absorbed on the next kick (with the label swap), ring turns 60 f.
techniques.use_when: Integrations, works-with-everything, a many-source product; one moment.
techniques.avoid_when: Single-source products; next to another spectral accent.
techniques.materials: Segment ends feather over about 8 % of the perimeter; neighbouring hues meet without a grey seam (order the dots by hue around the shape).
conditions: the film's one spectral accent

techniques.name: False-colour palette cycles, then resolves material by material
techniques.summary: A 3D room is shown in a thermal false-colour palette whose hues rotate while the camera pushes in, then each material resolves to its real look in turn (desk, wall, ceiling).
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a grey plate through a static colour-map filter whose hue is rotated per frame, per-material masks fading to the true plate. Anatomy: Hue rotation on a luminance map; resolve per material mask. Sound: A riser into it, then quiet. Materials: A blurred backdrop photo (12 px) inside an iris is gradient-mapped to saturated pastels with a map whose hue keeps rolling (about 6 f per stop through six stops) under a thin white cell grid (1 px at 35 %, 12 px pitch), while the whole layer fades out over 36 f.
techniques.timing: Cycle 77 f; resolves 12-20 f each inside a 53 f window.
techniques.use_when: A film about sensing, rendering or AI vision.
techniques.avoid_when: Without a real 3D or photo plate to map.
techniques.materials: A blurred backdrop photo (12 px) inside an iris is gradient-mapped to saturated pastels with a map whose hue keeps rolling (about 6 f per stop through six stops) under a thin white cell grid (1 px at 35 %, 12 px pitch), while the whole layer fades out over 36 f.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Cycle a two-tone map of the accent's lightness steps, then resolve.

techniques.name: Tiles warm up, then bleach to white
techniques.summary: All tiles on a wall warm from grey through a tint over a few frames, then bleach to pure white: a colour pulse that carries a transition.
techniques.recipe: <Exposure> with hue = a pale tint of the accent and swap at the peak. Anatomy: Grey -> tint -> pale -> white; whole wall at once. Sound: A sub on the bleach.
techniques.timing: Warm 18 f, bleach 20 f.
techniques.use_when: Leaving a grid of images into a white scene.
techniques.avoid_when: Warm hues in a cool brand.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Pulse through a tint of the accent, then bleach.

techniques.name: Category tint crossfades through grey
techniques.summary: Video panels fade in from white into a duotone with a small saturation overshoot; with each category the tint changes by passing through a neutral grey, so two tints never mix into a third hue.
techniques.recipe: tintThroughGrey(f, { a, b, grey }) on a Develop duotone. Anatomy: Duotone in; saturation overshoot +52 % then settle; crossfade via grey. Sound: A ding on the first, a sub on the last.
techniques.timing: Crossfades 13-18 f each; lines 35 f.
techniques.use_when: Several categories or use cases shown on the same panels.
techniques.avoid_when: More than about four tints.

techniques.name: A tint wave travels through the words and drains
techniques.summary: A band of tint moves through a line (or a running counter's digits) as the words arrive, peaking on each word as the voice lands it and draining behind; it can park on the last word.
techniques.recipe: HueSweep on the line with starts on the voice onsets, sweepOn 'all', back on early words; park with Chain accent="hold". Recipe: background linear-gradient(90deg, ink 0 40 %, deep 45 %, accent 50 % 58 %, deep 63 %, ink 68 % 100 %), background-size 300 %, background-clip text, position 100 -> 0 %. Anatomy: Tint band about 1.5 words wide; the picture leads the voice by 1-3 f; drain 12-16 f for early words, the last word lingers; variant: a second, slower wave 30-45 % behind a write-on front; variant: the band parks on the last word. Sound: Voice words land with the tint peaks. Materials: Band shoulders: when the accent travels through type, the band's edges are never a fade to grey. On black type the stops go black -> a deep shade of the accent (about 0.4 letter wide) -> the accent core (1-1.5 letters) -> the deep shade -> black inside single letters; on white type the shoulders are a pale tint instead. Band speed about 1 letter per 4 f on a giant word; in a sentence the head can run about 20 px/f and park on the keyword. Over a counting number the band is a soft-edged tint about 1.5 digits wide crossing in about 50 f while the digits keep running.
techniques.timing: Word peaks 8 f apart at 60 fps; drain 12-16 f; one pass about 1 s on a counter.
techniques.use_when: A headline voiced word by word; a counter that should feel alive; a phrase whose last word is the point.
techniques.avoid_when: A grey mid-tone in the band (give it shoulders); a second multi-hue accent in the same film.
techniques.materials: Band shoulders: when the accent travels through type, the band's edges are never a fade to grey. On black type the stops go black -> a deep shade of the accent (about 0.4 letter wide) -> the accent core (1-1.5 letters) -> the deep shade -> black inside single letters; on white type the shoulders are a pale tint instead. Band speed about 1 letter per 4 f on a giant word; in a sentence the head can run about 20 px/f and park on the keyword. Over a counting number the band is a soft-edged tint about 1.5 digits wide crossing in about 50 f while the digits keep running.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Type changes colour with what is behind it
techniques.summary: A soft blob slides under a typed word and the letters over it knock out to white; big type takes its colour from a blurred image blooming behind it; a small caption flips colour the frame a picture passes under it.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: render the text twice and clip the white copy with the blob's (static, transformed) mask; or mix-blend-mode difference on a flat field. Anatomy: Two copies of the type (ink and knockout), the knockout clipped by the blob or image shape. Sound: None. Materials: A defocused, heavily grained iridescent image (teal, magenta, coral on periwinkle) blooms up from a corner behind the giant type (coverage 7 -> 80 % in 32 f) and splits the letters white or black in screen space: white where the bloom covers the paper, black elsewhere, with a mask feather of about 150 px and grain sigma about 1.5.
techniques.timing: Blob 22 f expo-out; bloom 33 f; flips on one frame.
techniques.use_when: Type that shares the frame with moving colour.
techniques.avoid_when: Low contrast in the mixed state.
techniques.materials: A defocused, heavily grained iridescent image (teal, magenta, coral on periwinkle) blooms up from a corner behind the giant type (coverage 7 -> 80 % in 32 f) and splits the letters white or black in screen space: white where the bloom covers the paper, black elsewhere, with a mask feather of about 150 px and grain sigma about 1.5.

techniques.name: A tile lights from beneath and spills onto its neighbours
techniques.summary: When a key or tile lights, the light is not contained in it: a deep accent glow fills the tile and a white-hot spot sits on one edge, washing over the gap and half the next tile as if a light were under the keyboard; the dark tiles round it pick it up.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a baked radial plate (white core, accent body) scaled by transform in screen blend at the tile's edge. Anatomy: Tile near-black, radius 24 px, 1 px top inner highlight; light: a near-white core (r about 60 px) at the tile's edge, an accent body (r about 220 px), falloff to transparent; a floor glow along the bottom third; it grows about 2.5x over 14 f.
