Sound: VO. Materials: Glow anatomy: core, body and falloff, three stops, never a uniform halo; the core sits off-centre on the edge nearest the next tile.
techniques.timing: Bloom 14 f, then holds with the camera move.
techniques.use_when: Keyboard, grid and tile UIs on dark grounds; choosing one option.
techniques.avoid_when: Light grounds.
techniques.materials: Glow anatomy: core, body and falloff, three stops, never a uniform halo; the core sits off-centre on the edge nearest the next tile.

techniques.name: Tiles pass through a wireframe look
techniques.summary: Collage tiles turn white with thin dark outlines in 2 frames (a structural x-ray), the outlines and caption turn a pale tint and fade to white.
techniques.recipe: HardStep to an outline version of each tile (a pre-drawn stroke layer), then a fade to the ground. Anatomy: Two-frame switch, then a tint, then white. Sound: A whoosh.
techniques.use_when: A transition that reveals structure.
techniques.avoid_when: Busy tiles.

techniques.name: Big statistic lands oversized with tiny labels
techniques.summary: A huge stat (216-256 px tall) appears at 118 % and settles to size, with small labels above and below ("over", "views").
techniques.recipe: Oversize from 1.18 + Words labels. Anatomy: Scale 1.185 -> 1 quad-out; labels at the ui role. Sound: None needed; or a hit.
techniques.use_when: The headline number of a film.
techniques.avoid_when: Labels as large as the number.

techniques.name: Spec drawing with breathing dimension bars
techniques.summary: A construction drawing (hairline guides, a dashed centre line, a hatched shape, circles with anchor handles, ratio labels like "x" and "0.5x") where only the dimension bars move: they contract, hold 4 frames and expand back, opposing bars in counter-phase.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: static SVG drawing; bars as rects with an in-out width tween. Anatomy: Hairlines 1 px; bars contract 124 px in-out, hold 4 f, expand with a long tail. Sound: A kick on the drawing's arrival.
techniques.timing: 54 f per breath; 76 f in counter-phase.
techniques.use_when: Brand or product construction; precision claims.
techniques.avoid_when: Labels that are fake numbers.

techniques.name: Chart built from tiny cells that fill
techniques.summary: A bar chart made of small rounded squares (about 22 px with 4 px gaps): the first column fills from pale to full, the grey grid fades in, then the cells fill in column bursts (about one column a frame) while a cut to a wider framing keeps filling; a hexagon map of dots fills with coloured dots, scattered then dense, in sync with a counter, then snaps grey.
techniques.recipe: Build: <CellChart at cols rows values color empty> (fx/Charts): 22 px cells with 4 px gaps; order="column": the first column fills pale to full (14 f), the empty grid fades in (12 f), then one column bursts on every 2 f; order="scatter" fills seeded cells sparse then dense (60 f, E.buildIn) with cellChartCount() driving the counter; desat={{ at }} snaps the fill grey (8 f); mask shapes the grid (a hexagon map). Anatomy: Cells on a grid; fill order by column (bursts) or scattered-then-dense; the accent area grows about 40x in 8 f; a button can shrink into the first cell. Sound: Pops and ticks on the bursts.
techniques.timing: First column 14 f; grid fade 12 f; bursts 16 f; scattered fill 60 f with the counter; desaturate 8 f.
techniques.use_when: Any metric that grows; the payoff number of a product film.
techniques.avoid_when: Smooth bars next to it; more than one colour per series.

techniques.name: A row of dots rides a wave in stop-go pulses
techniques.summary: A row of dots (larger in the troughs, a few hollow rings) rides a sine wave that travels right in pulses: moves, stops, moves.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: dot y = A sin(kx - phase(f)), phase stepping by pulses. Anatomy: Pulses 60 f with 12 f holds at 7-10 px/f. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: 60 f per pulse.
techniques.use_when: Signal, activity, rhythm.
techniques.avoid_when: Continuous motion (the stops are the look).

techniques.name: Count grows geometrically, then jumps to the total
techniques.summary: A small header chip counts in quarter-second steps that grow x1.6-1.9 each (23, 43, 72, 125, 201, 360, 661), then jumps straight to the total (3,412).
techniques.recipe: Roll with explicit steps (a geometric list, then the total). Anatomy: Steps every 15 f; the final jump on a beat. Sound: Under the scroll.
techniques.use_when: "Reading N items" moments; scale reveals.
techniques.avoid_when: Linear counting for big totals.

techniques.name: Small bevelled metal numerals for rank
techniques.summary: Rank numbers beside list rows are tiny bevelled metal glyphs (the first gold, the second silver, the third bronze) while lower ranks stay plain grey.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: background-clip:text with a four-stop vertical gradient and a 1 px light text-shadow. Anatomy: A vertical four-stop gradient with a dark middle band (the classic chrome) clipped to the glyph, plus a 1 px bright top-edge shadow. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Static; scrolls with the list.
techniques.use_when: Leaderboards and rankings inside UI; one list.
techniques.avoid_when: Big display numbers.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Silver only for the first rank, plain grey below.

techniques.name: Small data glyphs inside cards
techniques.summary: Cards carry tiny data visualisations: a dotted world map with one accent square at the location, a row of dots as a level meter, three small colour chips with counts as a status panel.
techniques.recipe: kit parts (Meter, Badge) and small SVG dot maps. Anatomy: Dots about 6 px; one accent element per glyph. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Appear with their rows.
techniques.use_when: Profiles, dashboards, rows of results.
techniques.avoid_when: Unreadable micro text.

techniques.name: Node graph draws its links
techniques.summary: Relations drawn as a graph: right-angled connector lines draw from thumbnails (with small chips) while a table goes from skeleton bars to rows; scattered nodes fade in, spokes draw out from a hub, then the nodes morph into an even fan row on an over-damped spring; video thumbnails connected by thin lines sit around a title and ride the whip pans; selected thumbnails pop back to colour one by one as the cursor clicks and dashed links with small labels draw between them.
techniques.recipe: SVG paths with strokeDrawn(); node positions blended between two layouts (scatter, row) on an over-damped curve. Anatomy: Links drawn at pen speed; nodes about 10-60 px; spokes in 12 f; morph about 32 f over-damped. Sound: Onsets on the links; a ding on the last.
techniques.timing: Links 28-50 f; nodes 13 f each; morph 32 f.
techniques.use_when: Integrations, knowledge graphs, connected data, workflows.
techniques.avoid_when: Graphs with more than about 12 nodes on screen.

techniques.name: A ring of dots orbits a falling counter and contracts
techniques.summary: Dots on a tilted ring (sized by depth, white ones outlined) rotate around a small counter that rolls down; the ring contracts and collapses into the counter.
techniques.recipe: Build: <OrbitRing r={contracting radius} tilt={60} depth={[0.65, 1]} hero={<Roll>}> (fx/Orbit, fx/Roll): dots sized by depth orbit the rolling counter; shrink r over 90 f, then collapse 12 f on E.buildIn. Anatomy: Dots 55-85 px by depth; contraction 90 f; collapse 12 f circ-in. Sound: None needed. Materials: The ring is a tilted perspective orbit of black and white dots: near dots big and soft (up to 44 px, blur 3-5 px), far dots small and sharp (16 px); it shrinks 40 % while orbiting, then in the last 8 f the dots crowd into a clump that becomes a button arriving with a horizontal smear (20 px, then 8, then sharp).
techniques.timing: Counter 60 f; contraction 90 f; collapse 12 f.
techniques.use_when: A total that gathers many parts.
techniques.avoid_when: Busy rings with labels.
techniques.materials: The ring is a tilted perspective orbit of black and white dots: near dots big and soft (up to 44 px, blur 3-5 px), far dots small and sharp (16 px); it shrinks 40 % while orbiting, then in the last 8 f the dots crowd into a clump that becomes a button arriving with a horizontal smear (20 px, then 8, then sharp).

techniques.name: Digits roll or resolve into place
techniques.summary: Huge numbers cropped by the edge roll down into place with a fast decay, up to three rows stacking; a thin big score resolves digit by digit behind a leading dash, its label following.
techniques.recipe: <Roll> (rolling) or Roll hard with a per-digit start. Anatomy: Roll 12 f expo-out per swap; digit-by-digit resolve over 32 f. Sound: A glockenspiel.
techniques.use_when: Big numbers, scores, amounts.
techniques.avoid_when: Digits rolling at different speeds without reason.

techniques.name: One full-spectrum object in a one-hue film
techniques.summary: In an otherwise one-hue film one small object runs through the whole hue wheel: a pie of about 24 thin wedges with hairline separators, or a tiny concentric target icon. It is the only multi-hue thing on screen, so it reads as data or as a signal, never as decoration.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a CSS conic gradient with hard stops (pie) or a radial gradient with hard stops (target); hard stops do not band. Anatomy: Pie: a wedge every 15 deg round the wheel, 1 px separators at 20 % white, about 320 px across. Target: four near-hard rings with a 1-2 px blend. Entry: one frame at 1.15x and 1.3 brightness, then rest. Sound: None. Materials: Wheel order cyan, azure, blue, violet, magenta, pink, red, orange, amber, yellow, green, teal.
techniques.timing: Cuts on in one frame with its widget; holds.
techniques.use_when: A dashboard widget, a category chart or an icon that must stand out; the film's one spectral accent.
techniques.avoid_when: Any other multi-hue element in the same film.
techniques.materials: Wheel order cyan, azure, blue, violet, magenta, pink, red, orange, amber, yellow, green, teal.
conditions: the film's one spectral accent

techniques.name: Counter lands in decelerating steps
techniques.summary: A big number counts one unit a frame, then one every 2 frames, then every 3, landing exactly as the scroll settles.
techniques.recipe: steppedTail(to, end) from Roll. Anatomy: Step durations 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 4, 6 f. Sound: A stab or an impact on the landing. Materials: With proportional digits and a fixed suffix the gap breathes (a narrow one opens a visible gap); use tabular figures or place the suffix after the measured digits every frame.
techniques.timing: 20 f at 60 fps.
techniques.use_when: The payoff number.
techniques.avoid_when: Easing the digits smoothly.
techniques.materials: With proportional digits and a fixed suffix the gap breathes (a narrow one opens a visible gap); use tabular figures or place the suffix after the measured digits every frame.

techniques.name: Tag the chosen data, wash out the rest
techniques.summary: A grid of thumbnails switches to a warm duotone in a few frames, column labels fade in, tag pills grow on the chosen items and the untagged items wash out.
techniques.recipe: Develop reversed (colour to tint) for the untagged items; pill-label-build for the tags. Anatomy: Tint 15 f; labels 6-10 f apart; pills 18 f each; washout 35 f. Sound: None needed.
techniques.timing: 160 f in all.
techniques.use_when: Filtering, classification, search results.
techniques.avoid_when: Tagging too many items.

techniques.name: Segmented tick gauge
techniques.summary: Under a small label, a gauge of about 32 thin vertical ticks (3 px wide, 25 px tall) shows a value: most dark, the rest light.
techniques.recipe: Build: <TickGauge value on off> (fx/MicroUI): 32 ticks 3 px wide, 25 px tall, 3 px gaps; with at (and from) it fills one tick a frame. Anatomy: Ticks with 2-3 px gaps; filled share = the value. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Static, or a fill of 1 tick a frame.
techniques.use_when: A percentage that should read at a glance.
techniques.avoid_when: Animating every tick at once (fill left to right if it moves).

techniques.name: Barrel-roll fly-in down a corridor
techniques.summary: The camera rolls about 175 deg while flying down a corridor of light tiles to a hero object, pushing about 2x.
techniques.recipe: lib/camera roll + k on one ShotFn; tiles as a parallax field. Anatomy: Roll on a sine-out, push on an ease-in-out, light tiles passing. Sound: The music drops out.
techniques.use_when: The hero reveal of a 3D world, once.
techniques.avoid_when: UI films; readable type during the roll.

techniques.name: Device hinges open and its world pops around it
techniques.summary: A thin slab hinges open into a laptop (screen growing 44 -> 466 px with a slight yaw), then an envelope rises from behind the screen and a notification dot and a chat pill pop around it.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Flip3D kind="hinge" at x y w h front> (fx/Flip): the screen turns -90 -> 0 deg about its bottom edge on E.snapOut (22 f); the satellites pop with Cards or MicroUI after it. Anatomy: Hinge rotateX quad-out; satellites pop 6, 4, 6 f in sequence. Sound: A bubble pop on the envelope. Materials: The dark screen picks up a soft diagonal reflection (white at about 45 % with a cool tint, band at about 60 deg) that grows and slides across as the device yaws toward the camera, strongest mid-turn, fading as the camera pushes in.
techniques.timing: Hinge 22 f; satellites 10-15 f each.
techniques.use_when: Introducing a device or an app in context.
techniques.avoid_when: Too many satellites.
techniques.materials: The dark screen picks up a soft diagonal reflection (white at about 45 % with a cool tint, band at about 60 deg) that grows and slides across as the device yaws toward the camera, strongest mid-turn, fading as the camera pushes in.

techniques.name: Exploded view: panels push out, spin, collapse
techniques.summary: A face panel lifts off a 3D object and floats, the inner panels push outward into an exploded cube inside a larger box, the camera spins slowly in isometric, then everything collapses back.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: CSS 3D faces (preserve-3d) offset along normals by one progress value; spin as the container's rotateY. Anatomy: Panels offset along their normals; isometric camera spin on a sine-out; collapse on an ease-in. Sound: None needed.
techniques.timing: Explode 78 f, spin 98 f, collapse 35 f.
techniques.use_when: Explaining an architecture, layers or what is inside.
techniques.avoid_when: Flat 2D products.

techniques.name: Flat shape builds into a 3D object
techniques.summary: A flat outline grows into a solid: a triangle gains a fourth vertex out of plane and turns as a wireframe, its faces fill one after another; a square outline grows into a tumbling cube; a pyramid forms in halves around a hero; flat cards morph into glossy 3D balls while a ring spins.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: CSS 3D (preserve-3d) faces with stroke-only first, fills on per-face onsets. Anatomy: Wireframe 1-2 px; faces fill 2-3 f apart; tumble 180 deg slow-in slow-out. Sound: A note on the first face fill; a celesta with the core glow. Materials: Construction hairlines stay drawn on top of the shaded solid: every edge, including back edges seen through a clear face, remains a 1 px light line at about 70 % with a non-scaling stroke through the whole beauty hold.
techniques.timing: Construct 18-72 f.
techniques.use_when: A product about structure, models, building; a hero object reveal.
techniques.avoid_when: Glossy 3D in a flat UI film.
techniques.materials: Construction hairlines stay drawn on top of the shaded solid: every edge, including back edges seen through a clear face, remains a 1 px light line at about 70 % with a non-scaling stroke through the whole beauty hold.
conditions: glass as a material with real frost or refraction, not a default card style

techniques.name: Cards fly in and drift in depth forever
techniques.summary: About twenty tilted 3D cards fly in from all edges in a third of a second and decelerate to a slow drift that never stops; each tile keeps its own arc, one approaching, one receding, others drifting across.
techniques.recipe: Cards cardArrive per card with a seeded tilt, then a closed-form drift with a slow z term. Anatomy: Fly-in p90 34-41 px/f decelerating to 1.15 px/f (half-life about 0.2 s); per-tile depth arcs (206 -> 397 px, 375 -> 129 px). Sound: The music drops out under the drift.
techniques.timing: Fly-in 85 f; drift 285 f.
techniques.use_when: Galleries, templates, examples as a world.
techniques.avoid_when: Straight-line drifts (give each an arc).

techniques.name: Soft foreground objects pass close to the lens
techniques.summary: Out-of-focus objects in the foreground (warning signs in the corners, big soft black dots drifting in, a dark silhouette across the bottom) give the frame a near layer.
techniques.recipe: Foreground layer at a fixed ladder blur level, moved by parallax w > 1. Anatomy: Foreground blur 10-20 px; drift along curved paths settling around the subject. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Arrivals 40 f sine-out; static blur moving with parallax.
techniques.use_when: Tabletop sets, data scenes, a zoom that needs depth.
techniques.avoid_when: Bokeh over the subject's face or the copy.

techniques.name: Frosted panel over a living plate
techniques.summary: A card shows the same moving footage behind it, heavily blurred and slightly brightened, while the plate outside stays sharp; the material the camera dived into becomes the UI's background; an app window floats on warm light; a frosted card rises with a solid offset twin behind it.
techniques.recipe: RackFocus levels clipped to the card (a fixed blur copy of the plate under the card's mask). Safer than backdrop-filter: render the title twice, a sharp copy clipped outside the card's rect and a blurred, dimmed copy clipped inside it. Anatomy: Backdrop blur about 25 px inside the card; twin offset 45 px right, 60 px down. Sound: A whip whoosh. Materials: Frost construction: where a card overlaps the headline the letters show through as soft dimmed shapes (backdrop blur 8-12 px, letters at 40-50 % luma, no refraction offset), the card's rim stays crisp and its soft shadow darkens the letters just above it; a frosted bar over a halftone sky averages the dots into soft colour because its blur exceeds the dot pitch (blur 24 px, white at 22 %, a 1.5 px bright top edge, an inner shadow at the bottom). The ground behind a composer can be the same glass heavily defocused (blur 60-90 px) with pastel caustic patches and a faint rainbow arc at 8 % for 8 f, drifting against the camera.
techniques.timing: Continuous with the plate; rise 30 f expo-out.
techniques.use_when: Brands with a glass language.
techniques.avoid_when: Frost as a default card style; more than one glass language per film.
techniques.materials: Frost construction: where a card overlaps the headline the letters show through as soft dimmed shapes (backdrop blur 8-12 px, letters at 40-50 % luma, no refraction offset), the card's rim stays crisp and its soft shadow darkens the letters just above it; a frosted bar over a halftone sky averages the dots into soft colour because its blur exceeds the dot pitch (blur 24 px, white at 22 %, a 1.5 px bright top edge, an inner shadow at the bottom). The ground behind a composer can be the same glass heavily defocused (blur 60-90 px) with pastel caustic patches and a faint rainbow arc at 8 % for 8 f, drifting against the camera.
conditions: glass as a material with real frost or refraction, not a default card style
the film's one spectral accent

techniques.name: Hero objects fly with physical arcs
techniques.summary: Objects move like objects: a glossy sphere is thrown in on a parabola (x and y on different ease-outs) and the camera tracks and overtakes it; a sphere enters huge and rolls to the vanishing point; a disc, a ring and a cylinder fly past along a diagonal axis toward the camera; small cubes rain out of a tile with the near ones defocused; a cube rides through a cylinder seen refracted; two spheres slide in from both sides and spring-land.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Flight at from to apex scale={[a, b]} stretch orient>{object}</Flight> (fx/Flight): x on E.glideOut and the lift on its own curve (a parabola-like arc in closed form), stretched along the velocity at speed; scale by depth through scale; RackFocus by depth for the near ones. Anatomy: Parabolic paths; scale by depth (422 -> 71 px); fly-bys 120 -> 900 px in 5 f; rain 2 f apart at 15-30 px/f; spring zeta 0.70 with 7 % overshoot. Sound: A snare on the rain; a bubble pop at the landing peak. Materials: Glossy objects share one shading recipe: a pale highlight upper-left, the accent through the middle, a deep shade at the base and a large soft halo of the accent around them on light grounds (radial gradient at 35 % 30 %: near-white, light tint 30 %, accent 65 %, deep 100 %; halo blur about 60 px at 60 %). Pills get an extrusion: a duplicate in the deep shade offset (-8, +10) px behind, and a 1 px light inner top edge.
techniques.use_when: 3D brand worlds; a hero object reveal.
techniques.avoid_when: UI films; objects moving on straight eased lines.
techniques.materials: Glossy objects share one shading recipe: a pale highlight upper-left, the accent through the middle, a deep shade at the base and a large soft halo of the accent around them on light grounds (radial gradient at 35 % 30 %: near-white, light tint 30 %, accent 65 %, deep 100 %; halo blur about 60 px at 60 %). Pills get an extrusion: a duplicate in the deep shade offset (-8, +10) px behind, and a 1 px light inner top edge.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Card or model turns 180 deg with the edge-on frame on the beat
techniques.summary: A card rotates about its axis in perspective (long ease-in, quicker ease-out) and goes edge-on exactly on the downbeat, swapping its face there; a 3D model inside a card turns from front to side to back.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Flip3D at={flipAt(beat, {})} x y w h front back> (fx/Flip): a 180 deg turn on E.whipBuild (65 f, peak speed near 58 %) whose edge-on frame lands on the beat and swaps the faces there (declared a morph seam). Anatomy: Peak 8.4 deg/f at 58 %; face swap on the edge-on frame. Sound: The edge-on frame on the downbeat (-37 ms).
techniques.timing: 65 f; model turn 28 f.
techniques.use_when: Revealing the other side; turning a product.
techniques.avoid_when: Flips with readable text on both sides at once.

techniques.name: Layers move at different rates
techniques.summary: Text, tiles and the paper grid push at three different rates (text x1.16, tiles x1.08, grid not at all); walking silhouettes at five sizes move at speeds matching their depth; defocused tiles drift slowly behind a close-up.
techniques.recipe: parallax(layers, move) with w 1, 0.5, 0. Anatomy: Rates 1 : 0.5 : 0 (type, cards, ground); far layers blurred one level. Sound: A stop-down under a fast push.
techniques.timing: Over the move (35-63 f); background drift 1-3 px/f.
techniques.use_when: Any flat frame that should read with depth.
techniques.avoid_when: Equal rates (it reads as one flat layer).

techniques.name: Pull-back where the foreground lands first
techniques.summary: Opening on a button over a dot grid, the camera pulls back; the foreground lands about 10 frames before the background, so the depth reads from the timing alone.
techniques.recipe: parallax(layers with different frames) on one pull. Anatomy: Background on a soft-start ease-out (peak -5.5 %/f at f7) in log scale; foreground on a shorter curve. Sound: A glockenspiel-like note at 0.05 s.
techniques.timing: Background 58 f; foreground 38 f.
techniques.use_when: Openers on a single object over a textured ground.
techniques.avoid_when: Equal timing on both layers.

techniques.name: Frosted glass tiles with rainbow prism rims
techniques.summary: Icons orbit inside thick frosted-glass squircles whose edges glow with thin rainbow fringes (one hue on the lit side, its opposite on the other) like light split by a glass edge, while the icon inside stays crisp; out-of-focus tiles become pastel rainbow smudges.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a squircle with a padded conic-gradient border masked to the rim, a white frost fill; the conic angle follows the tile's rotation. Anatomy: Tile 140 px, radius 36; frost white at 35 % over a 14 px backdrop blur; a 6-10 px rim of a conic spectrum whose order follows the light direction; bokeh tiles blurred 12-25 px keeping their colours. Sound: None of its own.
techniques.timing: A continuous orbit; the dispersion turns as each tile turns.
techniques.use_when: An integrations orbit or icon cloud in a light, airy world.
techniques.avoid_when: Dark grounds; flat UI.
conditions: the film's one spectral accent

techniques.name: Glass objects refract the world behind them, then turn opaque
techniques.summary: Dark glass spheres fly in, and for their first frames the background shows through them, darkened, magnified and bent (grid lines and a light line displaced inside, a slight colour split on the bright lines); as they land they turn opaque.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a clipPath circle holding a scaled, blurred, darkened copy of the backdrop layer, a radial caustic and a rim stroke; the copy's opacity animates. Anatomy: Inside the circle: the backdrop scaled 1.1-1.2x about the sphere's centre, blurred 2-4 px, brightness 0.25, a 2 px channel split on bright lines; a caustic radial gradient from the accent at 80 % to transparent over 30 % of the radius; the refracted copy's opacity 1 -> 0 over the landing. Sound: Bubble pops on the landing, leading the picture by about 30 ms. Materials: Magnification 1.15, blur 3 px, brightness 0.25, caustic in the accent at 0.8.
techniques.timing: Clear 6 f, half 2 f, nearly opaque by 10 f more, overlapping the landing overshoot.
techniques.use_when: A 3D or glass act; objects that frame a hero.
techniques.avoid_when: Flat UI films.
techniques.materials: Magnification 1.15, blur 3 px, brightness 0.25, caustic in the accent at 0.8.

techniques.name: Tiles orbit a hero on a ring
techniques.summary: Six or seven app tiles orbit a horizontal ring around a hero object at constant angular speed; front tiles pass in front of it, back tiles behind.
techniques.recipe: Build: <OrbitRing x y n r speed tilt render hero> (fx/Orbit): items on a tilted ring (ringPoint: depth scale 0.72-1.08) at constant angular speed, back items drawn behind hero and front items in front. Anatomy: Ring in perspective; z-order by angle. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Constant over 128 f.
techniques.use_when: Integrations or features around a product.
techniques.avoid_when: Fast orbits (about 60 deg/s).

techniques.name: Object rises into frame as focus racks in
techniques.summary: A floating platform or object rises into frame, slowing, while the image racks from soft to sharp, the focus landing later than the position.
techniques.recipe: Cards enterState + RackFocus levels with the focus starting 4 f after the move. Anatomy: Rise 9 -> 2 px/f; focus lags by 20 f. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Rise 18 f; focus 40 f.
techniques.use_when: Introducing a 3D object or a device.
techniques.avoid_when: Racking before the move.

techniques.name: Only what matters stays in focus
techniques.summary: Focus does the pointing: the layout blurs and darkens while the camera pushes and a toast appears sharp over it (the defocus leading the toast by 4-6 f); older chat messages blur and grey as they scroll under the header; the second word of a pair is held soft; a window zooms in while its wallpaper pulls into focus.
techniques.recipe: <RackFocus levels hero>. Anatomy: Background defocus 19-28 px plus a 15 % darken; hero sharp above. Sound: Whooshes leading the toast. Materials: Fake lens depth on flat UI: in a list only the focused row is sharp and each row further away is softer (blur proportional to the distance from a focus band, isotropic, no bokeh shapes); foreground icons in the corners are huge and fully defocused; plain colour tiles placed in a grid as blurred out-of-focus depth (4-6 px, growing toward the edge) make sharp icons read nearer.
techniques.use_when: Directing attention without moving things.
techniques.avoid_when: Blurring the copy the viewer must read.
techniques.materials: Fake lens depth on flat UI: in a list only the focused row is sharp and each row further away is softer (blur proportional to the distance from a focus band, isotropic, no bokeh shapes); foreground icons in the corners are huge and fully defocused; plain colour tiles placed in a grid as blurred out-of-focus depth (4-6 px, growing toward the edge) make sharp icons read nearer.

techniques.name: Soap-bubble glass with thin-film rainbow bands
techniques.summary: A character or product sits under a clear glass dome that shimmers like a soap bubble: broad concentric pastel rainbow bands follow its curvature, strongest near the rim and fading at the crown, and the world behind is slightly desaturated and bent.
techniques.recipe: 3D: a hemisphere with a physical material (transmission 1, thickness 0.15, roughness 0.04, iridescence 1, IOR 1.3, film thickness 120-780 nm) under an environment map. 2D: concentric bands baked as a dithered PNG in screen blend inside a circle mask, a white rim, and a backdrop copy scaled 1.03 and desaturated inside. Anatomy: Five band hues (pink, peach, mint, lilac, sky), each 6-10 % of the radius wide, 25-40 % opacity, soft 20 px edges; a white fresnel rim at about 0.6 at grazing angles; the background inside desaturated about 30 % and shifted 2-4 % radially. Sound: An airy pad.
techniques.timing: Present for the shot; the bands drift 1-2 % a second with the camera.
techniques.use_when: A hero object that should feel protected, new or magical; airy pastel worlds.
techniques.avoid_when: Dark, technical films.
conditions: the film's one spectral accent

techniques.name: Camera tilt turns a flat graphic into a space
techniques.summary: A flat column or ring becomes a perspective runway or a side-view carousel as the camera tilts; a grid ceiling or floor appears.
techniques.recipe: lib/camera pitch on a 3D-transformed container (perspective 1200 px). Anatomy: Tilt of 564 px or a swing from axial to side view; grid planes appear. Sound: Between beats. Materials: After the grid tips into a perspective floor, a minute paragraph lies on the floor beside an object, rotated and foreshortened with it and softened by the floor's depth of field: animate the camera, not the text.
techniques.timing: 23-25 f in-out; then a constant orbit of 100 f.
techniques.use_when: Moving from a flat 2D graphic into a 3D world.
techniques.avoid_when: Without depth cues ready on the other side.
techniques.materials: After the grid tips into a perspective floor, a minute paragraph lies on the floor beside an object, rotated and foreshortened with it and softened by the floor's depth of field: animate the camera, not the text.

techniques.name: Shadows and rims tinted with the accent
techniques.summary: Cards and objects cast shadows in a dark tint of the accent instead of grey, and a round window carries a soft rim of the accent's light on one side, so the whole layout feels lit by the brand's world.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: box-shadow with an accent rgba; an offset coloured shadow for a lit rim. Anatomy: Card shadow 0 20px 50px in the accent at 35 %; a porthole rim 6px 8px 18px in the accent at 45 % on one arc (4 to 7 o'clock); card rim 1 px white; backdrop blur 10 px when the card is translucent. Sound: None. Materials: The shadow hue is the accent pulled toward its darker neighbour, never black; keep its alpha 0.3-0.45.
techniques.timing: Static material; the rim intensifies as the object defocuses into the next scene.
techniques.use_when: Light grounds with a strong accent; floating cards; a portal or porthole.
techniques.avoid_when: Dark grounds, where tinted shadows vanish; mixing with grey shadows in one film.
techniques.materials: The shadow hue is the accent pulled toward its darker neighbour, never black; keep its alpha 0.3-0.45.

techniques.name: Type sits between layers of the picture
techniques.summary: Type is placed in depth: a near tile slides over the headline and clears; across a cut the caption stays put but the product is now in front of it; a headline sits behind a circle and rises out from behind it; a large phrase fades in behind a card that overlaps it; words are uncovered by tiles sliding away.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: render the type between two picture layers (a matte of the foreground object above it). Anatomy: Z-order changes on cuts; occluding objects moving across the type. Sound: A drum on the cut. Materials: Captions move through the plates like props: over the subject, then behind her after the mask, a product standing in front of two letters, a giant word rising behind the product; one plane change per beat, always on a cut or the mask-confirm frame. During a fast pull-back the headline can tuck behind the rising panel's top rim (the panel moving about 1.8x the headline's speed, a vertical blur of 40-60 px on both).
techniques.timing: Occlusions 38-66 f; cut 0 f.
techniques.use_when: Making type and product share one space.
techniques.avoid_when: Occluding the key word for long.
techniques.materials: Captions move through the plates like props: over the subject, then behind her after the mask, a product standing in front of two letters, a giant word rising behind the product; one plane change per beat, always on a cut or the mask-confirm frame. During a fast pull-back the headline can tuck behind the rising panel's top rim (the panel moving about 1.8x the headline's speed, a vertical blur of 40-60 px on both).

techniques.name: A pixel glyph swings in as an extruded voxel solid
techniques.summary: A giant pixel numeral or symbol first shows as a sliver of grey side faces, then swings to face the camera as a voxel solid (white front cells, light grey extruded sides on every step) and settles flat into a slow pan.
techniques.recipe: CSS 3D: a preserve-3d group of cell boxes (front and side faces) under one perspective rotation; a flat SVG once the angle reaches 0. Anatomy: One box per on-cell of a 7 x 9 bitmap; front faces white, side faces 78-83 % grey, extrusion 0.4 of a cell; cells about 60 px at 1080p; perspective rotateY 70 -> 0 deg. Sound: Music onset just before; a whoosh under whatever reveals it. Materials: Side faces #C8C8C8 to #D4D4D4; edges keep 1-2 px of grey anti-alias so the solid stays crisp.
techniques.timing: 12 f expo-out, then the pan.
techniques.use_when: A pixel-font identity; one hero glyph (a currency sign, a number, a mark).
techniques.avoid_when: Soft, organic brands.
techniques.materials: Side faces #C8C8C8 to #D4D4D4; edges keep 1-2 px of grey anti-alias so the solid stays crisp.

techniques.name: Soft window-blind shadows across the set
techniques.summary: Broad soft diagonal shadow stripes (window blinds) fall across a tabletop set and move with it, so the scene reads as a real room.
techniques.recipe: A baked shadow plate (dither-gradient 'shadow' kind) with stripes, inside the set's transform. Anatomy: Static stripe plate in the ground's hue, multiplied, carried with the set. Sound: None. Materials: One shadow pass unites photographed and drawn pieces: a real photo cut-out lies among flat illustrated stickers and a drawn note, and a single set of soft diagonal window-blind shadows (bands 140-180 px at 1080p, a 60 px gaussian edge, a dark tint of the ground at multiply) crosses all of them, so the photo and the drawings share one room.
techniques.timing: Static; moves with the camera.
techniques.use_when: Tabletop or desk sets with objects.
techniques.avoid_when: Moving the stripes independently of the set.
techniques.materials: One shadow pass unites photographed and drawn pieces: a real photo cut-out lies among flat illustrated stickers and a drawn note, and a single set of soft diagonal window-blind shadows (bands 140-180 px at 1080p, a 60 px gaussian edge, a dark tint of the ground at multiply) crosses all of them, so the photo and the drawings share one room.

techniques.name: Camera orbits a panel in 3D
techniques.summary: A floating panel or page turns in 3D (its far side receding, the yaw flipping), sometimes with a slight wide-lens bulge on a push; new content pops in during the tail.
techniques.recipe: Cards enterState lean on rotateY, or the camera's yaw in lib/camera.ts; barrel bow as a static SVG displacement map at two strengths. Anatomy: Yaw 2-8 deg (far side scaling 1 -> 0.85); a push of x1.57 with 3-5 % barrel bow; content pops in the tail. Sound: A level dip before the flash it leads into.
techniques.timing: 34-54 f; 5 f ease-in, peak 45 px/f, long quart-out tail.
techniques.use_when: Product screens that should feel like objects.
techniques.avoid_when: Yaw beyond about 15 deg on readable UI.

techniques.name: One composition rule per act
techniques.summary: An act keeps exactly one centred object on black for its whole length (a dot, a line, a triangle, a prism), then the next act flips to an off-centre cropped UI: the composition change marks the act change.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a layout rule per act in the timeline. Anatomy: Centred single object vs off-centre crop. Sound: A section change on the switch.
techniques.timing: Acts of 2-3 s.
techniques.use_when: Films with a construction act and a product act.
techniques.avoid_when: Mixing the two rules within one act.

techniques.name: Arrows as motion motifs
techniques.summary: An arrow splits into a row of arrow glyphs pointing in different directions (each new glyph ink for one frame, then the accent); outlined chevrons rise past a word; pale arrows drift outward from a hero icon; a white arrow shoots from the frame edge into its target in 2 frames and holds.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: SVG arrow glyphs with HardStep colour and simple transforms. Anatomy: Glyph row tightening on an ease-out; chevrons decelerating; drift 120 px; shoot 2 f. Sound: The voice onset on the shoot.
techniques.use_when: Direction, growth, uploads, "go".
techniques.avoid_when: Decorative arrows that point nowhere.

techniques.name: Headline set so large the frame crops it
techniques.summary: A light headline (ascenders 20 % of the frame height) runs off the right edge, its last letter half cut, while its words fade in and the frame drifts.
techniques.recipe: Words at a size wider than the frame, ink-in-place entrance. Anatomy: Static crop; words ink in place; drift under it. Sound: A breath swell; key-click ticks on word onsets.
techniques.timing: Held 68 f.
techniques.use_when: Openers on a misty plate; editorial covers.
techniques.avoid_when: Cropping a letter that changes the word.

techniques.name: L-brackets frame a word and shrink-wrap it
techniques.summary: Thin L-shaped corner brackets (top-right and bottom-left, or top-left and bottom-right) frame a word and shrink-wrap it as it changes; on a swap they retract their arms to bare bars and regrow on the opposite corners; tiny L ticks ride along with every copy of a line; small link chips framed by brackets flicker at the frame edges.
techniques.recipe: Markers with corners ['tr','bl'] drawn as L strokes (two thin rects per corner), mode 'glide'. Anatomy: 2 px strokes, arms 35-60 px; shrink 221 -> fit; follow swaps with a 14 f cubic-out; retract 8 f, bars 4 f, regrow 6 f. Sound: With pops or kicks.
techniques.timing: Shrink 38 f quad-out; follow 14 f; flicker 4-8 f.
techniques.use_when: Framing the key word; technical, precise brands.
techniques.avoid_when: Thick brackets; all four corners (two diagonal ones read better).

techniques.name: Connector lines draw from one element to the next
techniques.summary: A straight line grows down from a title to a new note while a curved line grows from an icon, one frame apart, so the new element is visibly connected to what made it.
techniques.recipe: SVG paths with strokeDrawn() or a linear dash tween. Anatomy: 2 px lines, linear-ish growth, 1 f offset between lines. Sound: None. Materials: Lines start as single dots: a small round dot appears where the line will start and holds 10 f, stretches slowly into a dash (8 f), then draws fast to its end (14 f) while the camera pans; a line drawn out of a node keeps a fixed amount of ink, so it thins as it lengthens (width = 80 / length clamped to 1-4 px). A leftover arc can leave by retracting from its start toward the frame edge (34 f, ease-in) while the next word decodes.
techniques.timing: 8-12 f each.
techniques.use_when: Showing relations: a source to a result, a step to the next.
techniques.avoid_when: Lines that draw after the element has settled.
techniques.materials: Lines start as single dots: a small round dot appears where the line will start and holds 10 f, stretches slowly into a dash (8 f), then draws fast to its end (14 f) while the camera pans; a line drawn out of a node keeps a fixed amount of ink, so it thins as it lengthens (width = 80 / length clamped to 1-4 px). A leftover arc can leave by retracting from its start toward the frame edge (34 f, ease-in) while the next word decodes.

techniques.name: The tagline is set as a string inside the product UI
techniques.summary: The line of copy is not laid over the UI: it is a real string inside it (the subtitle of the top result, a field's text, a notification) at UI size, typed by the same typing primitive as the rest of the film and marked only by being the one line in a second voice.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: put the copy into the UI mock's data and animate it with TypeOn or Chain. Anatomy: One metadata string replaced by the copy; marked by a second type voice or the accent; it continues by typing later in the shot. Sound: Key ticks, if any.
techniques.timing: Present from the row's arrival; highlighted about 52 f; the continuation typed in about 30 f.
techniques.use_when: Update films and UI-led launches, where overlaid copy would fight the UI.
techniques.avoid_when: Lines longer than the field; UI sizes that become illegible in vertical.

techniques.name: Corner dots bracket the line; one pops big on entry
techniques.summary: Four tiny squares (8-10 px) mark the corners of a text block; one corner pops in as a large blob and shrinks to size, and the dots drift outward as the line grows; reused for each new line.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Corners size={9} mode="glide" pop={{ corner: 'tr', from: 2.5, frames: 18 }}> (fx/Corners): one corner enters oversized and settles on M.oversize; the others follow the growing line on E.jump. Anatomy: Pop 64 x 52 -> 33 x 22 px; drift about 4 px/f following the text box with a lag. Sound: With the title.
techniques.timing: Pop settle 18 f; drift continuous.
techniques.use_when: A system of brackets across a whole film's copy.
techniques.avoid_when: Large dots that compete with the type.

techniques.name: Tiny labels in the empty corners
techniques.summary: Three or four very small all-caps labels (10-12 px) and a contact line sit in the empty corners around a headline, arriving 1-2 frames apart and leaving with it.
techniques.recipe: Words at the ui role, pop entrance, staggered 4 f. Anatomy: Corner placement, all caps, tracked out. Sound: None. Materials: A tiny label decodes through random letters of the same width (2 + 2 + resolve, 10 f) as its tick dot appears under it.
techniques.timing: 3-5 f apart in; out with the line.
techniques.use_when: Poster-like frames; an editorial end card.
techniques.avoid_when: Labels that need reading (they are texture).
techniques.materials: A tiny label decodes through random letters of the same width (2 + 2 + resolve, 10 f) as its tick dot appears under it.

techniques.name: Four tiny corner squares that blink and jump
techniques.summary: Four small squares (14-25 px, slightly rounded, grey or ink) mark the corners of an invisible box around the current words. Each corner blinks on and off on its own uneven rhythm (on 1-8 f, off 1-6 f, rarely all four together), and the box never tweens: it jumps to new extents on word onsets (sometimes 3 f before a long word, so the frame is ready), often larger than the text; markers can each teleport on their own frame (1-6 f apart) along a layout grid, blink for a few frames after arriving, glide with the line's re-centre instead, or linger and blink alone after the phrase is gone.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Corners boxes onsets end color size={22}> (fx/Corners): per-corner seeded blinks (short 2-4 f flickers and 12-34 f holds, off 2-8 f), per-corner jump stagger (house TR 0, TL 2, BL 8, BR 9 f), boxes on word onsets (2-6 f early for a long word), end + linger (15 f); mode="glide" follows a re-centre on E.jump; cornerFrames() lists every jump for ticks. Anatomy: Corner rects at the box corners (inside the box), visibility from a seeded run-length pattern per corner (about 50-60 % on); box from a keyed table on onsets; optional per-marker jump order (TR, TL, BR, BL); optional glide on the re-centre curve with single-corner drop-outs of 1-3 f. Sound: None of its own, or ticks and hi-hats on the word steps; silence during the hold.
techniques.timing: Box steps on word onsets (or 6 f early at 60 fps); blink runs on 2-16 f, off 2-12 f at 60 fps; marker stagger 2-12 f; linger 15 f after the text.
techniques.use_when: A text-led opener or a calm statement that needs a living, technical frame; pointing at a word or a figure; any film with a tool or precision idea.
techniques.avoid_when: Glow on the squares; tweening the box; markers on every line of a film (one act).

techniques.name: Product stays fixed while the world swaps behind it
techniques.summary: The product (a phone in a hand, a bottle) stays locked in place while the background swaps every 5-6 frames through photos of different places and textures; a heavily blurred background can change on every letter of a typing logo.
techniques.recipe: HardStep over a background list under a fixed Cutouts/Photo of the product. Anatomy: Hard swaps on a fixed cadence; product cut out on top; optional slow push across the run. Sound: Ticks or key presses on the swaps.
techniques.timing: Swaps every 10-15 f at 60 fps; 7-8 backgrounds.
techniques.use_when: Showing versatility (works anywhere, with anything).
techniques.avoid_when: Moving the product.

techniques.name: Hard split: image half, text half
techniques.summary: The frame divides vertically: one half a mockup or picture, the other half a ground with type; the image half can carry a stepped dithered border.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: two AbsoluteFill halves with their own content. Anatomy: 50/50 split; cuts swap both halves together. Sound: Cuts on beats.
techniques.timing: About 95 f per pair.
techniques.use_when: Product plus claim, side by side.
techniques.avoid_when: Centred copy in the text half (left-align it).

techniques.name: Left-aligned stack builds downward beside the product
techniques.summary: Beside a tilted phone, a top-anchored left-aligned stack builds line by line every 5-7 f, each line rising about 50 px from a third strength.
techniques.recipe: <Words> per line with starts 12 f apart, left-aligned. Anatomy: Left margin about 158 px; lines added below; the last line in the accent. Sound: Voice.
techniques.timing: Lines 10-14 f apart; each 30 f.
techniques.use_when: Feature lists next to a device.
techniques.avoid_when: Centred stacks next to off-centre products.

techniques.name: Marker-pen strokes write on, slash and erase
techniques.summary: Hand-drawn marker strokes in one bright colour (about 30 px, rounded) write on over the type: a big X slashes a word, holds and erases top-down; a zigzag arrow starts as a dot and draws through the line; an underline writes right to left and erases in drawing order across a cut; small arrows write and erase between words, overlapping; a dashed arrow writes dash by dash; doodles are cut mid-erase.
techniques.recipe: Build: <PenStroke at d={penPaths.x(box).d} color width={30}> (fx/PenStroke): strokes share one pen (write 20 f on E.stdInOut, split by length; sequence="chain" makes the X's second stroke start as the first ends: 61 % of it in 5 of 17 f), hold 8 f, erase in drawing order (16 f) or erase={{ order: "reverse" }}; penPaths: underline (rtl), x, ring, arrow, zigzag; dash={{ n }} writes dash by dash; penEraseShare() to cut a doodle mid-erase. Anatomy: Stroke draw-on at pen speed with an ease-in-out; erase as a second draw-off in drawing order; X = two strokes, the second starting as the first ends; dash-by-dash reveal. Sound: A kick on the slash; bubble pops on the underline; an onset on the X. Materials: Marker strokes have dry, fibrous edges (plus or minus 2-3 px of edge noise at about 1/6 px frequency), round blobby caps 1.1x the stroke width, small width changes along the stroke, a flat fill and no transparency: they sit opaque over black or white letters.
techniques.timing: Write 17-22 f; hold 8-10 f; erase 12-22 f; an X in 17 f with most of it in 5 f.
techniques.use_when: Opinionated copy (crossing out the old way); playful launches; timelines.
techniques.avoid_when: Neat vector strokes (it must look drawn); more than one colour.
techniques.materials: Marker strokes have dry, fibrous edges (plus or minus 2-3 px of edge noise at about 1/6 px frequency), round blobby caps 1.1x the stroke width, small width changes along the stroke, a flat fill and no transparency: they sit opaque over black or white letters.

techniques.name: Photo cards with a mat and a thin coloured outline
techniques.summary: Photos sit inside a white mat with a thin coloured outline that follows the outer radius, like framed prints in a wall.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: nested rounded rects; Cards with image. Anatomy: Photo radius about 24 px, mat 12 px, 2 px outline. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Static.
techniques.use_when: Masonry walls and galleries.
techniques.avoid_when: Heavy shadows on top.

techniques.name: Tiny labels pop in mirrored pairs and drift out
techniques.summary: Ten tiny metric labels pop in pairs mirrored about the centre and drift outward slowly.
techniques.recipe: Words pairs with mirrored x and an outward drift. Anatomy: Pairs 2-3 f apart; drift outward. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Pairs over 25 f; drift 36 f.
techniques.use_when: Surrounding a hero number with context.
techniques.avoid_when: Labels that must be read.

techniques.name: A set of physical objects as the film's vocabulary
techniques.summary: Logos become die-cut stickers with a white border and a soft shadow lying on a cutting mat; letters sit on square tiles that drift apart radially under a pull-back, each at its own speed.
techniques.recipe: Cutouts with paper border; tiles as Cards with radial drift. Anatomy: Sticker border 6-8 px, contact shadow; tiles about 70 px each with one letter. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Static, or a radial drift over 36 f.
techniques.use_when: Tabletop, crafted films.
techniques.avoid_when: Mixing object styles.

techniques.name: Thin outline shapes frame a caption on a photo
techniques.summary: White 1-2 px outlines (a circle overlapping a rounded rectangle, a huge thin circle, a pill) sit centred on photos around a small one-word caption, contracting 5 % around it or sliding in, while the photo pushes.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: SVG outlines centred on the caption with E.snapOut scale; Photo push under them. Anatomy: Outlines contract on expo-out (peak 10 px/f) or slide in (60 px/f first frame) or expand circ-out. Sound: Kicks and a whoosh on the cuts. Materials: On live footage a thin white outline circle (about 420 px) or stadium sits off-centre and the phrase assembles word by word inside it, each word fading from grey to white about 10 f apart, overlapping the subjects with no backing.
techniques.timing: 16-22 f; captions fade 10 f.
techniques.use_when: Photo-led films with short captions.
techniques.avoid_when: Thick strokes; outlines that touch the subject's face.
techniques.materials: On live footage a thin white outline circle (about 420 px) or stadium sits off-centre and the phrase assembles word by word inside it, each word fading from grey to white about 10 f apart, overlapping the subjects with no backing.

techniques.name: Corner swatches take their colour from the picture
techniques.summary: Four flat 20 px squares frame a word like crop marks, and on every card they take new colours picked from that card's image.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Corners colors={[[tl, tr, bl, br], ...]}> (fx/Corners): per box, per corner colours picked from each card's image, swapped on the cut (the box changes on its onset). Anatomy: Corner marks as palette chips; recolour on the cut frame. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Recolour 0 f on each cut; cards 20-30 f.
techniques.use_when: Word cards over changing imagery; a film about images or design.
techniques.avoid_when: Colours that clash with the house accent (pick from the image's own palette).

techniques.name: Thin pen lines circle, underline and point
techniques.summary: A thin hand-drawn line annotates: an ellipse draws around a word while the word types (a short dash appears 4 f before at the ellipse's start); a loop circles a word or a dot; a curved arrow swings into a dot and retracts; a wavy underline appears under a new word on twos; a closed contour draws at constant pen speed; a thin ellipse orbits a photo.
techniques.recipe: SVG path + strokeDrawn() at constant pen speed (65 px a frame), inside <Stepped on={2}> for the hand feel. Anatomy: 1.5-3 px strokes, slightly irregular; pen speed about 65 px/f at 60 fps, slower at corners; on twos for a hand feel. Sound: A paper rustle; none for most. Materials: A rising zigzag trend line scribbles through a big number (three segments, ending in an arrowhead past the last digit, 30 f expo-out, arrowhead on the last frame) and holds until the stat breaks apart. Annotations leave as the hero changes state, not after: the loop and arrow un-draw in 2 steps over 4 f.
techniques.timing: Ellipse 28 f with the word; loops 20-25 f; underline 5 f in two steps; arrow draw 10 f, hold 15 f, retract 10 f.
techniques.use_when: Circling the key word; pointing at the subject; editorial and voice-led films.
techniques.avoid_when: Perfect geometric circles (that is a ring, not a pen).
techniques.materials: A rising zigzag trend line scribbles through a big number (three segments, ending in an arrowhead past the last digit, 30 f expo-out, arrowhead on the last frame) and holds until the stat breaks apart. Annotations leave as the hero changes state, not after: the loop and arrow un-draw in 2 steps over 4 f.

techniques.name: Objects pop around a word at full size
techniques.summary: Around a word or a stacked lockup, sticker objects, ad images or tilted app chips pop on at full size, no scale or fade, staggered by 1-4 frames (one settles 7 px), framing the word with context.
techniques.recipe: HardStep visibility per object, positions laid around the word's box. Anatomy: Cut-ons at full size; tilts 5-15 deg; lines 2-3 f apart. Sound: Chat pops. Materials: The chips pop exactly where the next words land, so for about 20 f the sentence is tangled with the logos (text over chips, no knockout; chips tilted -25 to +20 deg, white pills with a 1 px border at 6 % and a 6 % shadow); then the chips drift about 220 px upward on an expo-out and the line clears (cleared by 0.7 s).
techniques.timing: 1 f each; 1-4 f stagger.
techniques.use_when: Showing what a word covers (integrations, formats, uses).
techniques.avoid_when: More than about eight objects.
techniques.materials: The chips pop exactly where the next words land, so for about 20 f the sentence is tangled with the logos (text over chips, no knockout; chips tilted -25 to +20 deg, white pills with a 1 px border at 6 % and a 6 % shadow); then the chips drift about 220 px upward on an expo-out and the line clears (cleared by 0.7 s).

techniques.name: Grey problem pills, then blue benefit pills
techniques.summary: A grey wordmark with an OFF toggle and grey problem pills floating in from the corners; later the same layout in the brand colour with benefit pills floating in from three edges, mirroring it: the before and after share one layout.
techniques.recipe: Cards enterState from edges, same positions for both states, colour swapped. Anatomy: Pills enter expo-out (52 % in 10 %) 300-400 px from edges and idle; grey vs accent. Sound: An uplifter sweep on the benefits. Materials: Benefit pills fade from the accent at their left end to a pale tint and almost white at their right end (stops 0 / 40 / 75 / 100 %), with a 1 px white inner highlight on the top edge and a soft white glow past their end, so each pill dissolves into the light.
techniques.timing: Pills 48-94 f each, 80-120 f apart.
techniques.use_when: Problem/solution structures.
techniques.avoid_when: Changing the layout between the two states.
techniques.materials: Benefit pills fade from the accent at their left end to a pale tint and almost white at their right end (stops 0 / 40 / 75 / 100 %), with a 1 px white inner highlight on the top edge and a soft white glow past their end, so each pill dissolves into the light.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Four de-synchronised mini-films in a gutterless grid
techniques.summary: The frame is split into four panels with no gutters (or near-invisible hairlines), each running its own mini-film in its own style; cuts happen in one panel at a time on an irregular clock (never two on the same frame, at least two panels always moving); motifs echo across panels; near the loop's end the panels relay scenes to each other so the loop never visibly restarts.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: CSS grid 2x2, each cell a scaled 1920x1080 composition in <Loop> with awkward periods; merge all cut frames and nudge apart any within 6 f. Anatomy: Panels 960 x 540 at 1080p; per-panel state changes about every 1 s; cut gaps 12-88 f at 60 fps, irregular; a motif from one panel reappearing (inverted) in another. Sound: One shared bed; pane cuts driven by SFX onsets (whooshes, pops, keypresses), not the beat.
techniques.timing: Panel cuts 12-88 f apart; relays 16 f apart at the loop end.
techniques.use_when: Social loops and hero loops that must show breadth; feature reels.
techniques.avoid_when: Synchronised cuts across panels; 9:16 frames (panels get too small).

techniques.name: A ring draws around the subject, then ripples
techniques.summary: A thin ring draws clockwise around a caption on twos (60 % of the sweep in the first 4 frames), or a clean ring snaps on around a scribble and a second, larger ring appears and fades as a ripple.
techniques.recipe: SVG circle with dash offset (E.snapOut) on twos; the ripple a second circle scaling and fading. Anatomy: Ring radius about 370 px or 110-150 px; draw on an ease-out; ripple ring 4 f. Sound: A breath or a short vocal sound. Materials: The ring is born as a tiny comet dash: a 20 px glowing dash with a colour fringe across it appears up-left of the caption for 4 f, then jumps to an 85 deg arc and keeps drawing clockwise into the full ring (on twos). The halo can be a thick translucent glass ring (about 16 px wide, a pale tint at 35 %, a brighter 2 px inner edge, a 12 px outer bloom) with a fainter second ring outside, which turns into a dark shadow ring (10 px at 80 -> 15 %) as the dot becomes a solid disc.
techniques.timing: Draw 25 f on twos; ripple 10 f.
techniques.use_when: Marking a point of interest in a voice-led graphic film.
techniques.avoid_when: Glowing rings in house films.
techniques.materials: The ring is born as a tiny comet dash: a 20 px glowing dash with a colour fringe across it appears up-left of the caption for 4 f, then jumps to an 85 deg arc and keeps drawing clockwise into the full ring (on twos). The halo can be a thick translucent glass ring (about 16 px wide, a pale tint at 35 %, a brighter 2 px inner edge, a 12 px outer bloom) with a fainter second ring outside, which turns into a dark shadow ring (10 px at 80 -> 15 %) as the dot becomes a solid disc.
conditions: light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo

techniques.name: Design-tool selection box snaps to each word
techniques.summary: A caption sits inside a thin selection rectangle with small square handles at its corners; each appended word snaps the box to the new width in one frame; a square frame with corner nodes and full-frame crosshair hairlines grows around a hero; new card corners start as long diagonal strokes and collapse into square handles.
techniques.recipe: snapBox() from HardStep for the rect; handles as Markers with jump 1. Anatomy: 1-2 px rect, 8-12 px handles; snap per word; crosshair hairlines across the frame; diagonal strokes collapsing with tau about 1 f. Sound: Voice; a cut and voice for the hero frame.
techniques.timing: Snaps 8-15 f apart; frame grows 10 f; collapse 23 f.
techniques.use_when: Design, editing or creation tools; pointing at a hero object.
techniques.avoid_when: Easing the box (it is a tool, it snaps).

techniques.name: Tiles in a mixed shape vocabulary
techniques.summary: A layout uses a small set of shapes (circles, a rounded square, pills, photos with asymmetric corners), flat colour blocks mixed among photos, tinted photo cards, coloured tag chips and side accent bars, all cropped by the frame.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: per-tile border-radius arrays; colour blocks as Cards. Anatomy: Mixed radii (one corner fully round, others small); colour blocks 40-120 px. Sound: Pops and a ding. Materials: Every frame device is drawn from the logo's parts before the logo appears: the photo mask, the hairline caption frames, the pair of circles and the blobs are the mark's rounded rect, its circular cut-out and its dot; a construction drawing shows the primitives with anchor nodes; the film resolves on their assembly.
techniques.timing: Static after the unfold; tags pop 4-8 f.
techniques.use_when: Bento and collage layouts that should feel designed, not templated.
techniques.avoid_when: Every tile the same radius.
techniques.materials: Every frame device is drawn from the logo's parts before the logo appears: the photo mask, the hairline caption frames, the pair of circles and the blobs are the mark's rounded rect, its circular cut-out and its dot; a construction drawing shows the primitives with anchor nodes; the film resolves on their assembly.

techniques.name: Arrows shoot outward on a swap
techniques.summary: On the swap frame, thin light arrows appear at both ends of a phrase and travel outward (170 and 250 px) and fade, like the phrase pushing outward.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: two small SVG arrows translated on E.snapOut with an opacity hump. Anatomy: Two arrows, power-out travel, fade in-out. Sound: The big hit.
techniques.timing: Left 26 f, right 48 f; fade 34 f.
techniques.use_when: A phrase that expands in meaning (more, wider, everywhere).
techniques.avoid_when: Arrows on every swap.

techniques.name: Each word arrives on its own torn layer
techniques.summary: Each new word is printed on its own torn-paper image layer, which tears into view in stop-motion steps; the sentence builds across a stack of torn images.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: an SVG torn-edge mask whose reveal advances in held steps inside <Stepped>. Anatomy: Layer = image + word; the tear edge advances in 4 held steps (15, 45, 72, 100 %); layers stack. Sound: Paper tears within ±80 ms of beats. Materials: Each torn layer carries its own copy of the growing sentence, so where a new layer has torn in partway the text on it and below it sit a few pixels apart and words break across the tear (the offset = half the width of the newly added word); tear edges irregular 3-6 px with hard alpha; a new layer every 20 f.
techniques.timing: Tear steps every 10 f (30-40 f per layer), layers 50-65 f apart.
techniques.use_when: A crafted, editorial film with images; a statement that grows over several pictures.
techniques.avoid_when: Product UI films.
techniques.materials: Each torn layer carries its own copy of the growing sentence, so where a new layer has torn in partway the text on it and below it sit a few pixels apart and words break across the tear (the offset = half the width of the newly added word); tear edges irregular 3-6 px with hard alpha; a new layer every 20 f.

techniques.name: Tracking squares jump over a crowd every frame
techniques.summary: Small squares and arrow glyphs pop on random people in a crowd, repositioned every frame (1, 12, 5 per frame), like a tracker searching, then lock on one.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a seeded table of positions per frame over a list of head positions; HardStep visibility. Anatomy: Seeded positions per frame; count varies per frame. Sound: None needed.
techniques.timing: 28 f at 60 fps, new positions every frame.
techniques.use_when: Detection, targeting, finding the one.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm films.

techniques.name: Twin discs grow and hold words
techniques.summary: Two touching discs scale up on an expo-out and thin words appear inside them one at a time.
techniques.recipe: Cards springBox or enterState on two circles; Words inside. Anatomy: Discs about 180 px, touching; words at f+4, +7, +13. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Discs 16 f expo-out; words 6-12 f apart.
techniques.use_when: A two-part idea (before / after, you / us).
techniques.avoid_when: Long words that crowd the discs.

techniques.name: Sentence placed around an object
techniques.summary: A sentence is distributed around a picture or card instead of sitting on one line: the first half top-left and the second bottom-right of a growing image cluster, words as tiles in the gaps of a masonry wall, one word above and one below the newest card riding its perspective, or one word cut on while a pull-back brings the other in from the frame edge.
techniques.recipe: Words placed in the object's coordinate space (inside its transform); pull-back via camera. Anatomy: Words placed on the object's corners or in its gaps; they share its plane and drift; the next card can occlude them. Sound: A fast air whoosh; a soft UI tap then silence.
techniques.timing: Words 10 f apart; cut on with the card; pull-back -4.3 % in 2 f.
techniques.use_when: When copy and imagery share a frame and the layout should feel designed.
techniques.avoid_when: Read order that becomes ambiguous.

techniques.name: Two words part around the subject, then converge
techniques.summary: Two caption words either side of the subject slide apart with an expo-out (the maximum split on the strongest kick), hold, then converge on an expo-in.
techniques.recipe: Two Words with mirrored x on E.snapOut, exit 'launch' toward each other. Anatomy: Split 180 px; 77 px/f first frame; hold; converge. Sound: Kick + sub-drop on the maximum split.
techniques.timing: Part 28 f, hold 18 f, converge 24 f at 60 fps.
techniques.use_when: Framing a person or product with two words.
techniques.avoid_when: Subjects that move a lot.

techniques.name: Blobs fuse and split, then collapse into the mark
techniques.summary: Two huge blobs enter from both edges, fuse into a gooey shape that shrinks and bulges, split into circles, approach again and repeat three times, shrinking each time, and collapse into the mark.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: an SVG gooey filter (a static blur + alpha threshold, built once) over two circles moved in closed form. Anatomy: Enter 149 px/f; fuse; split expo-out; approach expo-in; bulge +11 % area and a +12 % rebound. Sound: A drum at the fusion; a deep boom on the mark. Materials: The blobs are jelly, not perfect metaballs: in flight they stretch along their travel with flattened leading faces (rx = r(1 + kv), ry = r / (1 + kv), rotated to the heading); slowing, they become wobbling circles whose flat facet travels round the edge (r(1 + 0.06 sin(3 theta + 0.2 f))); they fuse, split and fuse again on hits before collapsing to the dot of the mark. Crisp edges, no blur or shadow; a goo filter (blur 18 then an alpha threshold) merges them.
techniques.timing: Cycles of 18-28 f; 90 f in all.
techniques.use_when: A brand with round forms; an energetic end.
techniques.avoid_when: More than three cycles.
techniques.materials: The blobs are jelly, not perfect metaballs: in flight they stretch along their travel with flattened leading faces (rx = r(1 + kv), ry = r / (1 + kv), rotated to the heading); slowing, they become wobbling circles whose flat facet travels round the edge (r(1 + 0.06 sin(3 theta + 0.2 f))); they fuse, split and fuse again on hits before collapsing to the dot of the mark. Crisp edges, no blur or shadow; a goo filter (blur 18 then an alpha threshold) merges them.

techniques.name: Colour blocks swarm into letter slots and become glyphs
techniques.summary: Coloured rectangles flash at scattered spots for two frames each, converge, become letter-sized placeholders in the wordmark's slots, and swap to glyphs one by one; the mascot fills in to black.
techniques.recipe: Build: <BlockSwarm at text x y font palette> (fx/Gather): one block per letter flashes at a seeded spot for two frames (4 f at 60), each pose nearer its slot (18 f), sits as a letter-sized placeholder (6 f), then the glyphs swap in left to right every 3 f; letterSlots() gives the boxes; fill the mascot with Develop or a tint. Anatomy: Blocks held 2 f at random spots; converge; placeholders in letter boxes; glyph swaps every 1-2 f. Sound: A whoosh, a bubble pop, a key click.
techniques.timing: Swarm 18 f; swaps 2-4 f apart; fill 16 f.
techniques.use_when: Playful brands with a palette; a wordmark reveal.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm films.

techniques.name: Brand colour withheld until the mark lands
techniques.summary: The mark stays white or ink until everything has cooled, then switches to the brand colour in one frame; or the wordmark is re-coloured for each background and lands on the brand colour last.
techniques.recipe: HardStep on the mark's fill. Anatomy: One-frame switch; a stepped colour sequence per background. Sound: The switch 157 ms after a beat. Materials: Over a warm plate the white wordmark first turns the plate's complement for 4 f (it reads as a translucent multiply), then the brand colour fills the letters from the bottom up with a hard, unfeathered boundary (half, then full, one step every 2 f); the mark switches 2 f before the letters.
techniques.timing: 1 f switch; 8 f in 4 steps.
techniques.use_when: End cards and lockups.
techniques.avoid_when: A brand colour that is already everywhere in the film.
techniques.materials: Over a warm plate the white wordmark first turns the plate's complement for 4 f (it reads as a translucent multiply), then the brand colour fills the letters from the bottom up with a hard, unfeathered boundary (half, then full, one step every 2 f); the mark switches 2 f before the letters.

techniques.name: Light comets spiral out and collapse into the logo
techniques.summary: Two point-symmetric light comets (a bright head, a curved tail) spiral out from the centre, orbit once and collapse into the logo's position at full speed, where the mark appears.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Comets at x y color> (fx/Gather) centred on the mark: two point-symmetric flat heads with tapering tails spiral out (10 f, E.snapOut, to 450 px), orbit (8 f) and collapse on E.buildIn (26 f), arriving at about 85 px per 30 fps frame; land the mark on cometsState().land. Ban-safe: no halo. Anatomy: Expand 10 f, orbit 8 f, collapse 26 f (radial 110 px/f at the end); tails 19-84 px. Sound: A run of whooshes, then a hit on the mark. Materials: The last word dims from white to grey over 14 f while its corner brackets shrink to small hooks; one frame after the dim ends two curved light comets appear crossing the word's centre and swing outward (head at full white, tail 20-85 px, a halo of about 150 px at 4-6 % over the stage, screen blend); the word's ghost stays faintly visible under them for 12 f.
techniques.timing: 34 f at 60 fps.
techniques.use_when: A dark film's logo reveal.
techniques.avoid_when: Light grounds; glow-heavy comets in house films.
techniques.materials: The last word dims from white to grey over 14 f while its corner brackets shrink to small hooks; one frame after the dim ends two curved light comets appear crossing the word's centre and swing outward (head at full white, tail 20-85 px, a halo of about 150 px at 4-6 % over the stage, screen blend); the word's ghost stays faintly visible under them for 12 f.
conditions: light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo

techniques.name: CTA peeks in cropped, then cuts to centred
techniques.summary: A call-to-action tag peeks in at the edge of a grid, cropped, and creeps wider for about a second; hard cut to the tag centred and whole, breathing.
techniques.recipe: Cards with a creep, then a cut to a centred Card with Oversize from 1.04. Anatomy: Peek creep 52 f; cut; breathe 24 f expo-out. Sound: A kick on the cut.
techniques.use_when: Ending on a registration or sign-up.
techniques.avoid_when: Long peeks.

techniques.name: How the film leaves: fade, cut or defocus
techniques.summary: The last frames leave on purpose: the logo holds a third of a second and fades out on a sine over 20 f to a few black frames; or a hard cut to black on a drum hit with the tail ringing into silence; or the mark keeps receding and blurs out into silence.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: an opacity or defocus ramp on the end card group, aligned with the music's end. Anatomy: Fade 20 f sine; black 3-50 f; recede 0.3 %/f with a 38 f ease-in defocus. Sound: A sub-drop tail; a drum hit then silence; audio dropping to silence.
techniques.use_when: The final second of a film.
techniques.avoid_when: An abrupt end with the music still running.

techniques.name: App icon de-blurs while its monogram writes and lines converge
techniques.summary: A rounded app-icon tile cuts in blurred at about 2.3x and shrinks to size while sharpening; inside it a monogram is written with a pen; about 16 curves draw in from the frame edges converging on it.
techniques.recipe: Oversize from 2.3 with defocus; the monogram path with strokeDrawn(); converging curves as SVG paths with dash growth. Anatomy: Icon settle 71 f; pen 26 f; lines with linear ink growth 66 f. Sound: Voice.
techniques.timing: Icon to size 28 f, settle 140 f.
techniques.use_when: An app's end card.
techniques.avoid_when: Too many converging lines (over about 20).

techniques.name: Line-art pattern fills the end card
techniques.summary: Large thin outlines (2-3 px) of a motif in a lighter tint of the accent fill the end card behind the title and logo.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: an SVG line-art layer inside the end card's drift. Recipe: interpolate between a few hand-drawn key paths on a 24 f cycle, or offset each point by noise(i, f). Anatomy: Static line art, drifting with the card. Sound: None. Materials: The line art is alive: the outlines behind the end card keep morphing (tongues stretch, curl and change silhouette, 4-8 px of tip travel a frame) so the field flickers gently like a drawing of fire; stroke about 4 px at 1080p in a pale tint of the ground's hue at about 45 % contrast, round joins, no fill.
techniques.timing: Static.
techniques.use_when: End cards on a full accent field.
techniques.avoid_when: Motifs unrelated to the brand.
techniques.materials: The line art is alive: the outlines behind the end card keep morphing (tongues stretch, curl and change silhouette, 4-8 px of tip travel a frame) so the field flickers gently like a drawing of fire; stroke about 4 px at 1080p in a pale tint of the ground's hue at about 45 % contrast, round joins, no fill.

techniques.name: Logo assembles from parts
techniques.summary: The mark builds from its parts entering from alternating edges with uneven gaps (panels front-loaded, thin parts as constant-speed stripes that stop dead, small details popping last); a custom round glyph assembles from arc pieces that grow along the circle.
techniques.recipe: <AssembledMark> / assembleFor(logo, ...). Anatomy: Gaps 4/3/3/7/7/4 f at 24 fps; panels 7-12 f expo-out each; arcs 14 f. Sound: A pop on each main part.
techniques.use_when: Logos made of geometric parts.
techniques.avoid_when: Even gaps (they read mechanical).

techniques.name: Logo grows out of a line, a bar, a pixel monogram
techniques.summary: The mark is reached through a chain of simple states: a hairline fades in, grows into a tall bar that splits into stripes, the stripe stack squashes (anticipation) and each stripe slides sideways into the pixel mark; or two dots grow into a pixel monogram glyph by glyph, which collapses into a bar, which becomes the symbol.
techniques.recipe: MorphChain with explicit states (line, bar, stripes, mark) and HardStep for the stripe offsets; logoParts() for the final mark. Anatomy: Fade 8 f (63 % in the last frame); grow 28 f; squash -5 % then -30 %; stripes slide 23 f on an S-curve; monogram build 38 f, collapse 8 f, bar 1 f. Sound: A reverse-cymbal swell bed; a pluck on the slide; a drum on the build.
techniques.use_when: Brands with a geometric or pixel mark; the opening or the closing of a film.
techniques.avoid_when: Chains longer than four states.

techniques.name: Logo cuts in oversized and settles
techniques.summary: The mark or wordmark cuts in larger than its rest (1.3-1.9x), often defocused or tinted, and settles down with nearly half the move on the first frame; a square can jump 85 % in one frame and ease the rest over a long tail; a wordmark can resolve from a tint and blur, then drift away accelerating.
techniques.recipe: <Oversize from={1.4} dur={30} defocus> on the mark; Lockup snap for a one-frame jump. Anatomy: Scale 1.34-1.86x -> 1; blur peaks 3 f after entry then clears; colour tint -> ink (or a hue sweep). Sound: The voice saying the name 3 f after the picture; a snare on the jump.
techniques.timing: 28-62 f; 47 % of the travel in the first frame.
techniques.use_when: Lockups, end cards, the brand's first appearance.
techniques.avoid_when: Scaling the logo up from nothing.

techniques.name: Logo slams in on one blurred frame
techniques.summary: A big logo glyph fills its quadrant with a heavy motion blur on the last frame of a grid, moving diagonally: a one-frame slam.
techniques.recipe: A one-frame layer with a pre-blurred version of the glyph. Anatomy: One frame, blur along the direction of travel. Sound: None needed.
techniques.use_when: Closing a grid section on a hit.
techniques.avoid_when: More than one frame.

techniques.name: End logo swells, then settles back
techniques.summary: The end logo grows a little past its rest (1.06 -> 1.22, or x1.4 with a decaying rate), then settles or slowly shrinks a few percent while the ground brightens.
techniques.recipe: Two tweens on the mark's scale (E.snapOut up, E.strongInOut down) or a reversal on the mark. Anatomy: Up on an ease-out, down on an in-out; background brightens over 60 f. Sound: The music drops out under it; a quiet tail.
techniques.timing: Up 26-38 f, down 30-44 f.
techniques.use_when: The last beat of a film.
techniques.avoid_when: Bounces.

techniques.name: The mark lands inside a window of a real photograph
techniques.summary: The logo is not set on a flat ground: it spins in exactly inside the window glass of a warm photograph (a train window onto a mountain lake), sitting on the horizon, with the rest of the photo softly out of focus round it and a very slow push.
techniques.recipe: Photo framed on the window, a second blurred copy masked outside it, and the lockup placed in the window's rect.
