Anatomy: The window area sharp, the foreground and top blurred 12-18 px (a tilt-shift from two masked copies); the mark about 146 px across, centred on the horizon at 52 % of the window's height; push about 1 % over the beat. Sound: Spin-in on a whoosh; wordmark on the next hit. Materials: Choose a free photo whose window or frame is the composition; grade it toward the brand's ink so the mark owns the brightest colour.
techniques.timing: Holds about 90 f; the wordmark follows on the next hit.
techniques.use_when: A consumer brand with a place or a feeling; the end card of a lifestyle film.
techniques.avoid_when: Developer tools; busy photos without a calm window area.
techniques.materials: Choose a free photo whose window or frame is the composition; grade it toward the brand's ink so the mark owns the brightest colour.

techniques.name: Mark resolves in steps: de-pixel, ghost to ink, bold to final
techniques.summary: A pixel-art mark appears as very coarse cells and resolves to finer cells while it zooms out; a glyph inside a notched square steps from ghost to white to ink; a symbol appears heavy with its counters filled and thins until the holes open, with small ticks radiating.
techniques.recipe: Pixelate in-phase on the mark; HardStep for the ghost-white-ink states; weight via two outline paths morphed (Morph path). Anatomy: Cells 55 -> 20 px near-linear; glyph states 3-4 f each; weight thinning over 34 f. Sound: A ding; a drum on the bold state. Materials: The symbol is a jagged upscaled bitmap until the snap: while big it shows hard pixel staircases with 2-3 grey anti-alias levels per step (a 40 px bitmap scaled with nearest-neighbour, cells about 14 px), and on the one-frame snap to half size on a drum hit it becomes the clean vector.
techniques.use_when: Pixel or geometric marks.
techniques.avoid_when: Smooth tweens for these steps.
techniques.materials: The symbol is a jagged upscaled bitmap until the snap: while big it shows hard pixel staircases with 2-3 grey anti-alias levels per step (a 40 px bitmap scaled with nearest-neighbour, cells about 14 px), and on the one-frame snap to half size on a drum hit it becomes the clean vector.

techniques.name: Mark pops squashed and stretches to size
techniques.summary: The mark appears on the frame after a dot at full width but 79 % height (108 % wide), and stretches to its true proportions over 6 frames: a landing with squash.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: separate scaleX and scaleY tweens on the mark. Anatomy: Height 0.79 -> 1 cubic-out over 12 f; width 1.08 -> 1 over 26 f. Sound: A kick.
techniques.use_when: Marks that land on a beat after a dot or a drop.
techniques.avoid_when: Squash on type.

techniques.name: Brackets become strokes that shrink to dots as the logo grows
techniques.summary: At the last line the corner brackets turn into four diagonal strokes in an X around a centre dot, which shrink into small dots while the logo grows from the centre; one blink and the end card holds.
techniques.recipe: Markers rects morphed into diagonal strokes (rotated rects) then dots; Oversize from 0 is not allowed: the logo grows from the centre dot's size on E.snapOut. Anatomy: Strokes 90 -> 131 px then shrinking to 20-28 px dots; logo expo-out from the centre; one 1-frame blink. Sound: A sub-bass hit.
techniques.timing: Strokes 28 f; logo 25 f.
techniques.use_when: A film that used corner markers throughout: they hand over to the logo.
techniques.avoid_when: Without a marker system earlier in the film.

techniques.name: Panels shrink away and seeds build the logo
techniques.summary: Large blank panels shrink into one corner while coloured seed squares scatter and fly to build the logo in the opposite corner, and the words land in the accent: "one place".
techniques.recipe: Cards demote toward a corner + Wordmark assemble with parts starting from the panels' centres. Anatomy: Panels shrink to the corner; seeds fly on arcs; words 2 f apart. Sound: A ding.
techniques.timing: 34 f; glyphs 1-2 f.
techniques.use_when: Consolidation claims; the move from product to brand.
techniques.avoid_when: Logos without separable parts.

techniques.name: Start inside the mark and pull back to it
techniques.summary: Hard cut to the inside of a huge 3D mark; the camera pulls back about 12x with a roll (the first frame halves the size, the ratio relaxing after), then snaps to the flat mark.
techniques.recipe: zoomThrough in reverse (factor 1/12) with roll; HardStep to the flat mark. Anatomy: Pull back in log space, roll, final snap to the flat version. Sound: Kick, snare, kick across the pull.
techniques.use_when: The end of a film whose mark has a 3D form.
techniques.avoid_when: Marks without a recognisable silhouette.

techniques.name: The one dead-still hold at the end
techniques.summary: The film's only frozen frames are the end lockup: the card holds completely still for 1.2-3 s while the music drops out or a single final kick lands under it; a URL can pop on a sub-drop; the wordmark can scale in from 0.81 first; a split screen can hold one pane static while the others keep moving.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a static end card from the timeline with no creep (declare the still range so the checks accept it). Anatomy: Zero drift (frame difference near 0); optional URL pop in one frame; optional plain entrance (4 blank frames, a 40 f linear fade). Sound: The music tail drops out (to about -42 LUFS) or a final kick; a cork pop and a sub-drop on the URL.
techniques.timing: Hold 73-220 f.
techniques.use_when: Every end card.
techniques.avoid_when: Fading to black under the hold; freezing anything earlier in the film.

techniques.name: Wordmark slides out of the mark
techniques.summary: The mark travels aside to make room and the wordmark slides out from behind it, fading up from pale or revealed by a soft mask, and the whole lockup re-centres; after it lands the gap keeps closing until mark and word almost touch.
techniques.recipe: Lockup slide + Wipe gradient on the name, or Words with an x offset on E.snapOut. Anatomy: Slide 110-299 px cubic-out (38-42 % on the first step); wordmark opacity 0.3 -> 1 over 15 f, horizontally smeared at first; gap 20 -> 5 px in a slow tail. Sound: Often none (the music is in its tail). Materials: The wordmark can enter as a see-through wash: at 25-35 % opacity over the photo (the scene visible through the letters), doubled sideways by a ghost offset 20-30 px at half its opacity, turning solid brand colour as it slides 110-165 px into place over about 52 f.
techniques.timing: Slide 45-80 f; mask 20 f; gap tail 36 f.
techniques.use_when: Every lockup that does not need a hit.
techniques.avoid_when: The wordmark fading in place next to a static mark.
techniques.materials: The wordmark can enter as a see-through wash: at 25-35 % opacity over the photo (the scene visible through the letters), doubled sideways by a ghost offset 20-30 px at half its opacity, turning solid brand colour as it slides 110-165 px into place over about 52 f.

techniques.name: Wordmark letters blur-stagger in, a script suffix pen-writes
techniques.summary: The icon scales in, then the wordmark letters reveal left to right (about 1.3 f per glyph), each from a blur or a pale tint to full; a script suffix writes on with a pen; a dot can run a rounded path with a hairline trail.
techniques.recipe: Letters build with FocusWord-style blur per letter; script as a stroke path with strokeDrawn(). Anatomy: Per letter blur 20 px -> 0 and fade over 3-4 f; script 16-28 f; settle 100 f; optional 90 f fade to black. Sound: Kicks under the icon; a whoosh on the exit; audio to silence. Materials: The end fade dims the white ground to grey and black while the floor glow keeps its colour a beat longer (the ground's brightness falls over 90 f, the glow's starts 20 f later), so the coloured light is the last thing besides the wordmark, which deepens to a dark shade of the accent.
techniques.timing: Letters 22-24 f; script 16-28 f.
techniques.use_when: Soft, friendly brands.
techniques.avoid_when: Script suffixes in a brand without one.
techniques.materials: The end fade dims the white ground to grey and black while the floor glow keeps its colour a beat longer (the ground's brightness falls over 90 f, the glow's starts 20 f later), so the coloured light is the last thing besides the wordmark, which deepens to a dark shade of the accent.

techniques.name: Wordmark types on a beat grid, lands loose and tightens
techniques.summary: The wordmark's letters cut in one at a time on a grid locked to the music (every 8 f, triplets of the beat) or one per frame landing a little loose and tightening 3 %; a product mark resolves glyph by glyph with one glyph translucent and darkening in steps.
techniques.recipe: <Letters mode="pop" tracking> with starts on the beat grid. Anatomy: Letters cut on; landing +44 px loose, tightening over 10 f; one glyph darkening in steps. Sound: Letters within 23-33 ms of beats; a bubble pop at the end.
techniques.timing: Letters every 1-8 f; tighten 20 f.
techniques.use_when: A lockup for a product with a typed or technical feel.
techniques.avoid_when: Off-grid letter timing.

techniques.name: Blob launches, stretches, hangs and falls
techniques.summary: A blob pops off a bar as a small dot, rises above it stretched along its travel during the fastest frames, hangs at the top, and falls back: squash and stretch used once, on the one object that jumps.
techniques.recipe: Build: launchHangFall(f, { at, height }) (fx/Flight): up 29 f on E.glideOut, hang 8 f, down 21 f on E.buildIn; stretchOf(speed) gives the 1.38 : 1 stretch along the travel on the fastest frames only; anim squash() on the landing. Anatomy: Stretch 1.38:1 along travel for the fastest 4 f; hang 8 f; cubic up and down. Sound: Launch on a kick; land on the next kick.
techniques.timing: Up 29 f, hang 8 f, down 21 f.
techniques.use_when: A playful launch of a single element (an idea leaving the bar).
techniques.avoid_when: Stretch on type or UI panels.

techniques.name: Grid loader of blocks: lit row steps, copies in phase
techniques.summary: A tiny grid of accent squares is the loader: one row lit at full strength with a dimmer trail row behind it steps down the block on drum onsets (irregular holds 7, 3, 1, 3, 1 f), the other rows step down to a faint level in four linear frames, the loader zooms in until its grid becomes the screen's grid, and tiled copies each run in their own phase so the field shimmers.
techniques.recipe: Build: <BlockLoader start x y steps={onsets} color> (fx/Loaders): 4 x 4 accent squares (22 px on a 46 px pitch), the lit row and a 38 % trail step down on the onsets (house holds 17.5, 7.5, 2.5, 7.5, 2.5 f), the rest steps down to 17 % in four frames; tiled copies take a seed (own 1-7 f schedule) or a phase; zoom={{ at, to }} pushes in until its grid is the screen's. The 2 x 2 version is <QuadLoader> (clockwise head at 100 / 38 / 17 %, a step every 7.26 f; tile(step) puts a picture in the head cell). Anatomy: 4 columns, cells 22 px on a 46 px pitch at the start; lit row 100 %, trail 38 %, others 17 %; zoom expo-in. Sound: A water-drop or sub hit at the start; row steps on kicks.
techniques.timing: Zoom 18 f; row steps on onsets; dims 10 f in 4 steps; copies on their own 1-7 f schedules.
techniques.use_when: Openers and loading moments in grid-based brands.
techniques.avoid_when: Smooth fades between rows.

techniques.name: The caret waits and blinks
techniques.summary: The placeholder clears and a thick caret waits about 6 frames before typing starts; after typing, the caret blinks while the bar lifts away.
techniques.recipe: TypeOn caret with a pre-hold and blink. Anatomy: Caret 6 x 45 px; hold 12 f; blink on/off 16 f. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Hold 12 f; blink period 32 f.
techniques.use_when: Before and after any typing.
techniques.avoid_when: A caret that blinks during the typing.

techniques.name: Eyes open and blink
techniques.summary: A character or object gets life from its eyes: an eye springs open behind an object, gets a catch-light and blinks 1-4-1 frames; a character closes its eyes for about 4 frames.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: lid as a clip-path driven by a spring; blink as three stepped states. Anatomy: Lid spring zeta 0.70 with 4.5 % overshoot; blink 2/10/2 f. Sound: A UI pop on the open.
techniques.timing: Open 22 f; blink 15 f.
techniques.use_when: Mascots and characters.
techniques.avoid_when: Blinks on a regular metronome.

techniques.name: Chips and tags pop in place
techniques.summary: Tags with coloured status dots, secondary chips, an inline file chip in a prompt or a notification dot simply appear at full saturation in one frame, one every few frames: no fly-in.
techniques.recipe: HardStep visibility per chip. Anatomy: One-frame cut-on; 2-6 f apart; an inline chip appears as one token. Sound: None, or within another pop.
techniques.timing: 1 f each; gaps 4-12 f.
techniques.use_when: Secondary UI that should not compete with the hero motion.
techniques.avoid_when: Popping the hero element (give it an entrance).

techniques.name: Click answered by a colour pulse, not a bounce
techniques.summary: On the click the pointer vanishes and the button's fill ramps through a light tint and lands in its new state (with a check, an "Analyzing" label, a popover from its tail); or the colour drains upward through the button as its arrow launches; or the button flashes white and blurs for 3 f before turning to the active colour.
techniques.recipe: press() q drives a colour interpolation; HardStep for the white flash; springBox from the button for the popover. Recipe: background linear-gradient(0deg, next 0 %, current 66 %), background-size 100 % 300 %, background-position-y stepping 0 -> 100 % inside each 4 f state. Anatomy: Hover 8 f, click, colour ramp 9-23 f, hold, fade; popover pops from its tail in 3 f. Sound: A bubble pop at -1.2 dBFS plus a wood-block; a UI pop. Materials: The fill changes colour by a vertical gradient climbing through it: each new colour enters at the bottom edge and pushes upward through a soft gradient 1.5x the button's height, about 4 f per state through a short hue walk, then holds 18 f and fades in 6 f.
techniques.timing: Hover 12-19 f; ramp 12-23 f; popover 10 f in, 7 f out.
techniques.use_when: Send, copy, export, confirm.
techniques.avoid_when: A second multi-hue ramp in the same film.
techniques.materials: The fill changes colour by a vertical gradient climbing through it: each new colour enters at the bottom edge and pushes upward through a soft gradient 1.5x the button's height, about 4 f per state through a short hue walk, then holds 18 f and fades in 6 f.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Click feedback: dot, ring, tint
techniques.summary: On click a small dot blooms at the cursor tip, a thin ring expands around it to about 40 px, and the clicked area takes a light tint that holds.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Ripple at x y color shape={{ w, h }}> (fx/MicroUI): an 18 px dot blooms (2 f), a thin ring grows 10 -> 40 px (12 f, E.snapOut) and the clicked area takes a 14 % tint that holds (6 f). Anatomy: Dot 18 px, ring 10 -> 40 px fading, area tint over 6 f. Sound: A soft UI tap on the ring.
techniques.timing: 26 f in all; ring 12 f.
techniques.use_when: Clicks on flat areas without a button shape.
techniques.avoid_when: Glow halos (keep the ring thin).

techniques.name: Corner handles turn on one after another: a loading chase
techniques.summary: The four corner handles of a selection turn dark in sequence (TL, then TR and BL, then BR) and back: a six-frame loading chase built from the frame itself.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Corners chase={{ at, color }}> (fx/Corners): the corners turn dark TL, then TR and BL, then BR and back, a step every 2.5 f (15 f a cycle; cycles to repeat). Anatomy: 2-3 f per corner; colour swap only. Sound: None needed.
techniques.timing: 15 f at 60 fps per cycle.
techniques.use_when: A selection or a card processing.
techniques.avoid_when: Long chases (one or two cycles).

techniques.name: Cursor vanishes into an outlined button
techniques.summary: On click the cursor disappears and an outlined circle with an arrow appears at about 111 % and settles, as if the click produced the button.
techniques.recipe: Cursor visibility off on the click + Oversize from 1.11. Anatomy: One-frame swap; settle expo-out. Sound: None distinct.
techniques.use_when: A call to action at the end of a demo.
techniques.avoid_when: Keeping both cursor and button.

techniques.name: A dot grows into an icon
techniques.summary: A 4 px dot appears, becomes a rounded blob, then a thick plus already rotated that spins -90 deg into place; a point grows over 3 frames, jumps 4x in one frame on a note, settles and shrinks to a point; tiny dots scattered around a folder grow into file icons in a quick stagger while the folder pops.
techniques.recipe: MorphChain dot -> blob -> icon; SnapZoom-style one-frame jump on the note. Anatomy: Growth 12 f; snap 85 % in 1 f; settle 15 f; icons 10 f each staggered. Sound: A soft UI pop; the snap on an arpeggio note; pop SFX.
techniques.use_when: Building icons from nothing; motifs on a musical note.
techniques.avoid_when: Icons fading in.

techniques.name: Ellipsis dots arrive one by one
techniques.summary: The "..." after a status word arrives as three separate dots, accelerating (14 f, then 6-8 f gaps); a placeholder gains its dots one at a time while a more-button's dots resolve.
techniques.recipe: Build: <ThinkingDots ellipsis start> (fx/MicroUI): the dots cut on 14 f, then 7 f apart (22 f for three), then pulse; or HardStep visibility per dot. Anatomy: Dots cut on with shrinking gaps. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: 22-24 f for three dots.
techniques.use_when: Status lines and placeholders.
techniques.avoid_when: All three at once.

techniques.name: Input with a moving coloured border
techniques.summary: A dark rounded input whose border light travels around its outline in two brand colours, continuously.
techniques.recipe: A conic-gradient border (a baked plate) rotated by transform. Anatomy: Conic border rotated continuously. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Continuous (68 f per turn).
techniques.use_when: An AI input in a brand that owns that look.
techniques.avoid_when: House films (it reads as the stock AI look).
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo

techniques.name: Hover pulse on contact
techniques.summary: When the cursor touches a button its rim grows about 8 % in 2 f and decays back over 4 f.
techniques.recipe: Build: hoverPulse(f, at) (fx/MicroUI) on the rim's scale: +7.8 % in 2 f at 30 fps, back over 4 f. Anatomy: Scale +7.8 % in 2 f, decay 4 f. Sound: None, or a faint tick.
techniques.timing: 12 f at 60 fps.
techniques.use_when: Before every important click.
techniques.avoid_when: Continuous pulsing.

techniques.name: A screen-fixed voice waveform under moving shots
techniques.summary: A thin grey waveform with a tiny two-line caption stays fixed at the bottom centre while the camera whips and zooms underneath; its amplitude rises and falls like live audio and lies flat between phrases.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: an SVG polyline from noise(x, frame) times an envelope, placed outside the camera. Anatomy: About 60 points across, low contrast (about 30 % white), a new noise phase per frame under an amplitude envelope; outside the camera transform. Sound: It follows the voice.
techniques.timing: Active while the voice speaks, flat between.
techniques.use_when: Voice and call products; a narration cue without words on screen.
techniques.avoid_when: Films with captions.

techniques.name: Line icon draws itself on
techniques.summary: A line icon draws its strokes on (a paper plane while its bubble slides in; icons drawing onto objects, then updating; an icon rising inside a sphere as it blooms; an icon that breathes +12 % while its stroke inks in).
techniques.recipe: SVG paths with strokeDrawn() or a dash tween. Anatomy: Draw-on 8-17 f roughly linear; 5 px stroke at about 70 px icons. Sound: Soft ticks; the voice onset.
techniques.use_when: Icons in UI moments; labelling objects.
techniques.avoid_when: Filled icons (the draw-on needs strokes).

techniques.name: Icons and badges pop in with a small life
techniques.summary: Small icons arrive with character: a crown badge pops tilted onto the corner of the top icon; an emoji pops a beat after its bubble (40 % -> 100 %); a pixel icon flips in from a 1 px line in one frame, breathes and flashes white; pixel blocks pop one by one and land with a small overshoot; a drawn clock's second hand ticks.
techniques.recipe: Oversize from 0.4-0.7 on E.snapOut (allowed for small icons), HardStep for flips. Anatomy: Pops front-loaded 6-8 f; flips 1 f; breath +5-8 %; overshoot small. Sound: A chat pop or none. Materials: Pictorial elements arrive at full size but out of focus and sharpen over 4-6 f (blur 8 -> 3 -> 0 px, no scale), while saturation goes pale to full; text never does this. A block can also be born inside a letter of the word and slide to its slot as the word shrinks (6 f).
techniques.use_when: Badges, emoji, small rewards and states.
techniques.avoid_when: Every icon popping at once.
techniques.materials: Pictorial elements arrive at full size but out of focus and sharpen over 4-6 f (blur 8 -> 3 -> 0 px, no scale), while saturation goes pale to full; text never does this. A block can also be born inside a letter of the word and slide to its slot as the word shrinks (6 f).

techniques.name: A row of icons arrives staggered, the chosen one last
techniques.summary: Toolbar icons fade in one after another and the chosen one gets a filled tile behind it last; app icons develop into some slots in random order on the strongest hit.
techniques.recipe: Cards / kit Glyph with starts; Develop for the slots. Anatomy: Stagger 3, 3, 9 f; fades 5 f; random-order develop 1 f apart. Sound: The strongest hit for the develop.
techniques.use_when: Toolbars, app grids, options.
techniques.avoid_when: Even stagger for the chosen item (give it a beat more).

techniques.name: Integration icons slide in and pin to the pill
techniques.summary: Five app-icon tiles appear one by one around a central pill as each is named, and matching coloured dots pin to the pill's border, so the connections read.
techniques.recipe: Cards enterState per icon + small dots placed on the pill's border by angle. Anatomy: Slide about 16 f expo-out; onsets tied to the words; dots at the border points facing each icon. Sound: Each icon lands with its word.
techniques.timing: 86 f for five.
techniques.use_when: Integrations, connected sources.
techniques.avoid_when: More than about six icons.

techniques.name: Click or hover lights the object
techniques.summary: A click pushes the camera toward the caret and a soft light blooms at the click point; a glossy 3D object brightens and shifts colour under the hovering cursor.
techniques.recipe: SnapZoom (pre build) on the click; light as SnapZoom flash with a swell (gain 0.4). Anatomy: Push tau about 6.5 f; light attack 13 f, release 23 f; hover 84 f then a 20 f shrink. Sound: A click on the beat (+28 ms); a UI pop on the punch-in. Materials: Emissive heat under the cursor: a glossy object lit by the scene brightens to a hot emissive version of the accent when the cursor reaches it (brightness 1 -> 1.5 and saturation 1.4 over 40 f), its rims glow (drop-shadow 30 px in the accent) and a soft radial glow pools on the ground under it (about 60 % at the centre to 0 at 500 px).
techniques.timing: Push 15-20 f; light 36 f.
techniques.use_when: The decisive click of a demo; a hover on a hero object.
techniques.avoid_when: Halo glows in house films.
techniques.materials: Emissive heat under the cursor: a glossy object lit by the scene brightens to a hot emissive version of the accent when the cursor reaches it (brightness 1 -> 1.5 and saturation 1.4 over 40 f), its rims glow (drop-shadow 30 px in the accent) and a soft radial glow pools on the ground under it (about 60 % at the centre to 0 at 500 px).
conditions: light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo

techniques.name: The field bends like jelly where it is pressed
techniques.summary: As the cursor presses a button inside an input card, the card's edge and corner bow outward round the button (a soft bulge, the corner radius swelling), the edge goes slightly wavy along its length, then everything springs back.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: the rounded rect as an SVG path sampled at about 80 points, displaced each frame in closed form. Anatomy: Edge displacement d(s) = A exp(-(s - s0)^2 / (2 x 120^2)) along the normal, A peaking about 9 px at 1080p; a ripple of 2 px sin(2 pi s / 90 px - phase); stroke and shadow follow the shape; the cursor squashes 1 -> 0.8 -> 1 with it. Sound: The click, then a wood-block.
techniques.timing: Bulge 6 f, wobble 10 f, release 4 f.
techniques.use_when: The one press of a film that should feel physical; playful brands.
techniques.avoid_when: Serious enterprise tools; every click.

techniques.name: Round button with a liquid fill and a rim
techniques.summary: A round button with a thin up-arrow, a bright rim highlight and an accent liquid fill pooled at its bottom; it shrinks with the pull-back, pulses on hover and implodes on click.
techniques.recipe: Layered circles with a baked rim plate. Anatomy: Rim highlight, liquid pool, glyph. Sound: None. Materials: At rest the round glass button holds a swirling liquid in its lower third and a streak across the top; as the cursor approaches the liquid swirls up and fills the sphere (18 f), on touch it drains to a thin layer (16 f); fill blobs blurred about 10 px inside a hard circle mask, a white inner highlight at 30 %, a rim glow about 8 px. The arrow inside scrolls out of the top (8 f, ease-in), the button is empty for 4 f, and a fresh arrow rises from the bottom (8 f, ease-out), landing as the cursor touches.
techniques.timing: Static; implodes in 6 f.
techniques.use_when: A hero button in a brand with a glass language.
techniques.avoid_when: House films.
techniques.materials: At rest the round glass button holds a swirling liquid in its lower third and a streak across the top; as the cursor approaches the liquid swirls up and fills the sphere (18 f), on touch it drains to a thin layer (16 f); fill blobs blurred about 10 px inside a hard circle mask, a white inner highlight at 30 %, a rim glow about 8 px. The arrow inside scrolls out of the top (8 f, ease-in), the button is empty for 4 f, and a fresh arrow rises from the bottom (8 f, ease-out), landing as the cursor touches.
conditions: glass as a material with real frost or refraction, not a default card style

techniques.name: Loader arc grows into a ring and the core swells
techniques.summary: Inside a screen a dot becomes a short dash, then an arc that grows 30, 60, 90, 160 deg, accelerating to about 300 deg, closes into a ring, and the dot at the centre swells into the hero button.
techniques.recipe: Build: <ArcLoader at r x y color core={{ to }}>{icon}</ArcLoader> (fx/Loaders): a dot (3 f), an arc growing to 300 deg on E.buildIn while it turns 6 deg/f (15 f), closing (4 f), and the core swelling into the button on E.snapOut (8 f): 30 f in all. Anatomy: Arc length on an accelerating curve while it rotates; ring closure; core swell. Sound: The beat (+7 ms) on the first frame.
techniques.timing: Arc 0 -> 300 deg in 18 f; close + swell 10 f (30 f in all at 60 fps).
techniques.use_when: The moment between a request and the result; turning a loader into the next object.
techniques.avoid_when: A spinner that loops more than once before resolving.

techniques.name: A shine passes through text while it loads
techniques.summary: A soft band (about one word wide) sweeps left to right across a status line on every beat, turning the letters it covers white; a single word glows and returns to grey; skeleton cards pulse a diagonal shine twice; a textured shimmer passes over a filled prompt box before the press; an idle slider label shimmers letter by letter.
techniques.recipe: <LightSweep> clipped to the text, looped on the beat. Recipe until a primitive exists: background: linear-gradient(90deg, base 0 42%, band 48% 52%, base 58% 100%); background-size 250% 100%; background-clip text; background-position-x = 100 - ((f % period) / period) x 100 %. Anatomy: Band 150 px moving about 86 px/f near-linearly, then a rest; period = one beat (40 f, 90 BPM). Sound: The beat grid exactly. Materials: Anatomy of a type shimmer: the text is clipped to a gradient three times its width whose position slides one width per period. On a dark or tinted ground the band is white, about one word (5-7 letters) wide with 2.5 letters of feather each side, travelling about 0.7 letters/f and restarting at once (period about 40 f), with a slight bloom on the white letters. On a light UI invert it: a band darker than the grey base, about 40 % of the word wide, period 16-20 f; a dim band on near-white letters reads as a skeleton loader on type. Include the ellipsis in the sweep.
techniques.timing: Sweep 20-26 f; rest 18 f; pulses 22 + 20 f.
techniques.use_when: Loading states; an idle call to action.
techniques.avoid_when: Shimmer on headlines; glow halos.
techniques.materials: Anatomy of a type shimmer: the text is clipped to a gradient three times its width whose position slides one width per period. On a dark or tinted ground the band is white, about one word (5-7 letters) wide with 2.5 letters of feather each side, travelling about 0.7 letters/f and restarting at once (period about 40 f), with a slight bloom on the white letters. On a light UI invert it: a band darker than the grey base, about 40 % of the word wide, period 16-20 f; a dim band on near-white letters reads as a skeleton loader on type. Include the ellipsis in the sweep.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Brand mark rises alone and spins as the loader
techniques.summary: On black, the brand mark rises into place alone, sits for 5 frames, then words append beside it and the mark spins on its vertical axis as the loader.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Flip3D angle={spinAngle(f, start)} front={mark}> (fx/Flip): the mark turns on its vertical axis, a turn every 26 f, its back face hidden; Words appends the name beside it. Anatomy: Rise 123 px in 8 f; rotateY spin about 26 f per turn. Sound: A riser.
techniques.timing: Rise 8 f; spin 26 f/turn.
techniques.use_when: Product moments where the brand is the system.
techniques.avoid_when: Spinning the wordmark.

techniques.name: Context menu springs up over a blurred page
techniques.summary: On a right-click the board blurs out completely in 6 f and dims about 11 %, and a dark rounded menu springs up softly; the hover moves down its rows.
techniques.recipe: RackFocus levels on the page + springBox for the menu. Anatomy: Background blur expo-out; menu soft spring; hover 12 f per row. Sound: A pop.
techniques.timing: Blur 12 f; menu 46 f; hover 12 f.
techniques.use_when: Right-click and long-press actions.
techniques.avoid_when: Menus without the background reacting.

techniques.name: Pill grows around its label
techniques.summary: A pill builds around its words: an outlined pill pre-sized per phrase with words cut on inside it; a link icon first, then words, the outline widening symmetrically; a label pill growing up from its bottom edge beside a tile.
techniques.recipe: Morph box width from the measured text (FontGate); words pop inside. Anatomy: Words 4-6 f apart; width eases with each word (or pre-sized); growth from the bottom edge on an expo-out. Sound: A bubble pop and a mouse click 80-140 ms after.
techniques.timing: 10-20 f per pill; words 10-15 f apart.
techniques.use_when: Labels, tags, prompt chips.
techniques.avoid_when: Text that spills before the pill grows.

techniques.name: Pill marquee; selected pills fill
techniques.summary: Rows of outlined pills with words alternate with small line icons, scrolling as a marquee; the selected pills fill with colour from their left end, connectors draw between them, the rest dim.
techniques.recipe: Wipe kind 'feather' inside each selected pill; connectors as stroke draw-ons. Anatomy: Fill left-anchored 16-24 f; connectors 20 f; dim 18 f. Sound: Voice. Materials: The chosen outline pill fills with a horizontal gradient (a pale tint at its left end, the accent at 45 %, a near-black shade at its right end) revealed by width over about 20 f, under white text; its 2 px outline stays visible.
techniques.timing: 175 f in all.
techniques.use_when: Choosing among modes or capabilities.
techniques.avoid_when: Gradient fills in house films.
techniques.materials: The chosen outline pill fills with a horizontal gradient (a pale tint at its left end, the accent at 45 %, a near-black shade at its right end) revealed by width over about 20 f, under white text; its 2 px outline stays visible.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Progress line builds with counter-motion
techniques.summary: A dash becomes a line whose left end races left while the right end creeps; a short dash slides against the build direction under the bar; a coloured band scrolls once along the line.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: rect ends animated separately (left on E.snapOut, right slow); the counter dash a second rect. Anatomy: Width 42 -> 262 px cubic-out (peak 32 px/f at 20 %); counter-dash 13 -> 6 px/f. Sound: With the bar. Materials: A stepper advances as a 3D cursor passes under it: the next node goes from an empty ring (2 px, about 22 px) to a ring with a filled centre dot that scales in over 8 f, and the button dims to a pale tint over 16 f.
techniques.use_when: Progress, search bars forming, a line that becomes a field.
techniques.avoid_when: A second multi-hue band in the same film.
techniques.materials: A stepper advances as a 3D cursor passes under it: the next node goes from an empty ring (2 px, about 22 px) to a ring with a filled centre dot that scales in over 8 f, and the button dims to a pale tint over 16 f.

techniques.name: Rings ripple out from a click or a pill
techniques.summary: Rings expand from a click point or from around a pill, one after another in decreasing greys, each fading as it grows; or one large soft ring expands from the cursor.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Ripple at rings={3} every={10} shape={{ w, h, r }}> (fx/MicroUI): rings in the control's own shape (a stadium for a pill) launched 10 f apart, each 12 f and a step lighter. Anatomy: Stadium rings matching the pill's shape, launched every 10 f, each 10 f quad-out; greys stepping darker. Sound: A click or a hit. Materials: Filled tonal rings in stepped greys (four steps from light to near the ground) grow outward one after another, about 6 f apart, their outlines wobbling like jelly (a 4-6 px offset of the new ring for 2-4 f) before settling into a three-step tonal halo.
techniques.timing: 10-14 f per ring.
techniques.use_when: Calling attention to a control; a broadcast or connect moment.
techniques.avoid_when: Glowing gradient rings in house films.
techniques.materials: Filled tonal rings in stepped greys (four steps from light to near the ground) grow outward one after another, about 6 f apart, their outlines wobbling like jelly (a 4-6 px offset of the new ring for 2-4 f) before settling into a three-step tonal halo.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: A tiny seed square appears first, then unfolds
techniques.summary: A 15-40 px coloured square appears exactly where something will land and sits for 1-4 frames, then bursts into a photo tile, slides and widens with each typed character into a sticky note, stretches into a label bar whose text types, or a line end becomes a capsule that unfolds centre-out into a labelled card.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Seed at box color mode="burst"|"stretch"|"capsule">{content}</Seed> (fx/Seed): a 24 px square cut on at the landing spot, held 4 f, then burst (expo-out from a third of the way, 14 f), stretch (a bar of the label's height, 20 f) or capsule (centre-out, then open, 17 f); widths for a note that widens per typed character; seedOnsets(start, n) for a run every 4-6 f. Anatomy: Seed square (2-4 % of the frame) -> hold 1-4 f -> expo-out to the full box starting at a third; width follows typing instantly; capsule widens centre-out revealing its letters. Sound: A glockenspiel note on the first seed; none per seed after.
techniques.timing: Seed 2-8 f; tile 12-16 f; new tile every 4-6 f; bar stretch 20 f; capsule 14-20 f.
techniques.use_when: Building a layout tile by tile; labels and notes; any arrival that should feel planted.
techniques.avoid_when: Seeds that do not match the final element's colour.

techniques.name: Selection handles appear, drift and resize
techniques.summary: Four small square handles appear one by one clockwise around a subject and drift outward; they pull in until they overlap the corners, then spring back past rest; the cursor becomes a corner-bracket handle and drags a translucent selection rectangle; handles snap around a small word and the selection grows to swallow the cards around it.
techniques.recipe: <Markers boxes onsets blink> for the handles; the drag as a Morph box tied to the cursor. Anatomy: 24-32 px squares; appear 2-3 f apart clockwise; drift 47 px out; overlap then spring past rest; selection rectangle at 25 % white with corner marks. Sound: None, or soft ticks.
techniques.timing: Appear 32 f; drift 30 f; spring 15 f; drag 20 f.
techniques.use_when: Editing and selection tools; pointing at the subject of the film.
techniques.avoid_when: Handles in a film without an editing idea.

techniques.name: Send button launches
techniques.summary: The round send button detaches from its box and launches on a J-curve toward the camera (drifting right while rising and growing), or its arrow rotates to point back and flies along the input, erasing the text with a liquid smear.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: x on E.snapOut, y on E.buildIn, scale linear; the erase is a Wipe whose edge follows the arrow. Anatomy: x peak early, y peak late (J), diameter growing linearly; arrow rotate 90 deg on an ease, fly on an ease-in, a smear erasing behind it. Sound: A kick on the launch, a whoosh on the exit; or a silence then a sub-drop. Materials: The button that flew away comes back: about 2 s later a white disc spins in from a frame corner, motion-blurred (rotational smear for 6 f), and settles into the send slot of the new window (12 f, strong ease-out) on a sub drop.
techniques.timing: Launch 42 f; rotate 17 f, fly 26 f.
techniques.use_when: The moment a request is sent.
techniques.avoid_when: Sending without consequence (the next shot must show the result).
techniques.materials: The button that flew away comes back: about 2 s later a white disc spins in from a frame corner, motion-blurred (rotational smear for 6 f), and settles into the send slot of the new window (12 f, strong ease-out) on a sub drop.

techniques.name: Selection bar slides to the clicked item
techniques.summary: On click the cursor shrinks a little and a solid selection bar slides down the sidebar to the clicked item while the page cross-dissolves in 3-4 frames; a group expands its sub-items and pushes the items below down.
techniques.recipe: snapBox/E.snapOut on the bar's y; Cards stack for the group. Anatomy: Bar 8 f; dissolve 6-8 f; sub-items open in 12-16 f pushing 110 px. Sound: A UI click.
techniques.use_when: App navigation in a walkthrough.
techniques.avoid_when: Pages that slide (they cross-dissolve fast in real apps).

techniques.name: Twin controls split apart from the centre
techniques.summary: Two buttons that start overlapped at the centre slide apart to their places (one left, one right), then both drift outward slowly.
techniques.recipe: Two Cards with mirrored x on E.strongInOut. Anatomy: Symmetric in-out, peak 12.3 px/f at 43 %, then an outward ease-in drift. Sound: UI pops.
techniques.timing: 48 f; drift 14 f.
techniques.use_when: A composer's buttons appearing.
techniques.avoid_when: Asymmetric timing.

techniques.name: State changes in place without travel
techniques.summary: A control changes state the way software does: a toggle turns on without sliding (the knob dissolves on the left and reappears on the right while the brand colour switches in the same frame); a header label clears and the new label appears as the chevron slides to its width; sub-panels swap content on one frame; a frosted bubble is a solid button after a cut.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Toggle at mode="inPlace" w track trackOn knob> (fx/MicroUI): the knob dissolves on the left and reappears on the right while the track switches in one frame at the midpoint (26 f); other in-place swaps stay HardStep / stepValue with the chevron on a short E.snapOut. mode="spring" (house) crosses on SPR.landing clamped at 6 % with the track snapping 1 f after the click. Anatomy: One-frame swaps; the only eased part is the chevron or the colour. Sound: A state-change sound. Materials: A chip's label changes by the new label sliding in from the right inside the pill while the old one is clipped (both overlap for 4-6 f, about 20 f per swap); a phone screen can change content by a 6-8 f ghost dissolve (old 100, 50, 20, 0 %) while the device moves.
techniques.timing: 1 f swaps; label change 16 f; toggle 26 f.
techniques.use_when: Toggles, status labels, panels switching.
techniques.avoid_when: Tweening what software would switch.
techniques.materials: A chip's label changes by the new label sliding in from the right inside the pill while the old one is clipped (both overlap for 4-6 f, about 20 f per swap); a phone screen can change content by a 6-8 f ghost dissolve (old 100, 50, 20, 0 %) while the device moves.

techniques.name: Status labels swap faster and faster
techniques.summary: A status label fast-types (3-4 characters a frame), then swaps to the next; phrases change at shrinking intervals (15, 12, 18, 15, then 3, 3, 3, 3 f) before the cut, with giant cropped numbers beside them swapping too.
techniques.recipe: TypeOn kind="stream" per label with starts from an ACCEL list. Anatomy: TypeOn stream per label; HardStep swaps; intervals shrinking. Sound: A cut at the end.
techniques.timing: Labels 16 f each; final swaps 6 f apart at 60 fps.
techniques.use_when: Showing a process speeding to completion.
techniques.avoid_when: Text the viewer must read.

techniques.name: Thinking indicator: icon, label and pulsing dots
techniques.summary: A small status line says the product is working: an icon (a sparkle, a ring of circles, a face bubble), a word ("Thinking", "Searching") and three dots that pulse in turn (each darkening and growing about 1.4x, the wave passing left to right), sometimes with a token count.
techniques.recipe: Build: <ThinkingDots start size color> (fx/MicroUI) beside the icon and label: three dots darken and grow 1.4x in turn (20 f up, 20 f down, 25 f apart); ellipsis brings them on one by one first. Anatomy: Dot wave: each dot up 20 f + down 20 f, stagger 25 f at 60 fps (or a 12 f cycle); icon rises 14 f circ-out. Sound: None, or a soft tick per cycle. Materials: The assistant icon is a line drawing of a brilliant-cut gem (outer circle, eight kite facets, an octagon table) stroked with a vertical three-hue gradient, still, the only multi-hue element on a dark panel.
techniques.timing: Cycle 24-60 f.
techniques.use_when: Every wait in a product demo.
techniques.avoid_when: Long waits (cut away after about one cycle).
techniques.materials: The assistant icon is a line drawing of a brilliant-cut gem (outer circle, eight kite facets, an octagon table) stroked with a vertical three-hue gradient, still, the only multi-hue element on a dark panel.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Companion icon swaps on every tick
techniques.summary: A square icon tile beside a list changes its outline icon on every tick of the list (code, document, data, crop, image, link), one state every 4 frames.
techniques.recipe: HardStep over an icon list. Anatomy: One-frame swaps; 4 f per state. Sound: Ticks.
techniques.timing: 10 f per state.
techniques.use_when: Showing formats or types passing through.
techniques.avoid_when: Icons that are hard to read at speed.

techniques.name: Toast or chip arrives smeared or blurred, then sharpens
techniques.summary: A status chip enters sideways as a horizontal smear (a thin streak, then a smeared pill, then sharp); a notification grows from a blurred pill and rises; a toast pops blurred at the push's midpoint, rises and sharpens; a disc inflates behind an icon (the icon leads); a tab bar slides down as the scroll brakes.
techniques.recipe: Cards enterState with defocus (two ladder copies) and a 1-2 f horizontal ghost. Anatomy: Streak 1 f, smear 2 f, sharp; growth 1136 -> 1408 px in 7 f; rise 17 px; the disc starts 2-4 f after its glyph. Sound: A chat pop or wood-block on the cut; a soft note after whooshes.
techniques.use_when: Status messages, notifications, small UI pieces arriving.
techniques.avoid_when: Long smears on readable text.

techniques.name: Giant word rises in, cropped by the frame
techniques.summary: One word so large the frame crops it (cap height 31-55 % of the frame) rises or drops into place on a steep expo-out; often the layout pans at the same time, so the path is a J-shaped swoop, or the product swaps underneath it.
techniques.recipe: <Words> at display size with rise 0.8-1 em and dur 20-60 on E.snapOut inside a cropping frame; stepped variant inside <Stepped fps={16}>; the band is a LightSweep clipped to the text. Anatomy: A single display word at 3-6x body size; rise 330-740 px; variants: on every third frame held (stepped); with the whole layout panning left as it rises; dropping from above while a one-hue band about 1.5 letters wide travels through the letters. Sound: A spacebar-like click, or sub-bass plus kick when the product swaps under it.
techniques.timing: 17-60 f expo-out (tau about 15 f); pan 55 f on 16 fps steps; band crosses in 16 f.
techniques.use_when: Opening a film or a section with one word; a word that rides over a product shot.
techniques.avoid_when: Words whose meaning depends on the cropped letters.

techniques.name: A single glyph grows, spins upright and opens the film
techniques.summary: A single small mark appears at the frame centre on a dark ground, grows (half size within 2-3 f) and spins to upright on a longer, softer curve, landing exactly when the next device (a mask) starts; later it turns into a hole of the ground's colour and shrinks out spinning.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: an SVG mark with scale and rotate on separate curves. Anatomy: Scale on a steep ease-out over 40 f; rotation 65 -> 180 deg on a longer tail; invert in 1 f; exit shrink on an ease-in. Sound: The first music note at 0.05 s.
techniques.timing: 64 f in; exit 52 f.
techniques.use_when: Cold opens; a mark that seeds an iris.
techniques.avoid_when: A sparkle as decoration (use the brand's own mark or a neutral shape).
techniques.ban_safe_variant: The brand's mark or a plain dot as the seed.

techniques.name: Light lines shoot through the frame
techniques.summary: From black, a thin light bar shoots up from the frame edge to full height in a few frames; lines extend from a hero to the corners; thin light axes pierce an object one after another.
techniques.recipe: Build: <LightLine at from to color width> (fx/Streak): grows from from on E.snapOut (12 f) and thins to 35 % (10 f); stagger several 10-30 f apart for axes; flat by default, soft adds a static blurred copy on dark stages. Anatomy: Bar 60-100 px wide with a 20-30 px soft edge, or 2 px lines; grow from an edge or a point; thin afterwards. Sound: The first music hit right after.
techniques.timing: Bar 12 f quad-out (peak 462 px/f); lines 5-8 f; axes 10-30 f apart.
techniques.use_when: A cold open on a dark stage; a hero moment in a 3D world.
techniques.avoid_when: Neon glows (keep the lines thin and the halo small).
conditions: light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo

techniques.name: Shot opens already moving
techniques.summary: The first frame of a film or a shot already carries a lateral drift, a pan at full speed or a decelerating push (a third of the travel in the first 10 % of the move), which settles on the subject.
techniques.recipe: handoffShot()/carriedCut() for cuts; for the opener, a move on E.snapOut whose first frame is already partway. Anatomy: Pan 126 px/f decaying, or a push x1.43 with 36 % of the zoom in the first tenth, or a drift of 12.9 px/f plus a slow zoom-out that decays. Sound: The first music hit at about 0.15 s.
techniques.timing: Settle 36-80 f, front-loaded; critically damped.
techniques.use_when: The film's first frame; every shot after a transition.
techniques.avoid_when: Starting from a parked frame (it reads as a slideshow).

techniques.name: Picture montage that accelerates behind held copy
techniques.summary: A sentence holds still while images cut behind it with shrinking shot lengths (8-9 f down to 2-3 f); a front card swaps its photo by hard cuts accelerating from 7-12 f to 1-4 f; a central photo flip-book of tilted prints accelerates and the words re-centre to each print's width.
techniques.recipe: <Montage cuts> with an accelerating cut list (ACCEL.montage); prints as Cards with seeded tilt. Anatomy: Interval lists shrinking (6, 6, 3, 5, 3, 3, 4, 2...); prints tilted ±2-5 deg and different sizes; each new photo 12-15 % larger at landing. Sound: A silence then a whoosh run; a cut into silence at the end. Materials: Not every change is a cut: for 4-8 f the next image is double-exposed over the current one (screen or lighten at 40-60 %), and the last still leaves by smearing sideways (a blur ramp 0 -> 40 px over 8 f) with a spectral leading edge (red, yellow, white, transparent) in screen blend.
techniques.use_when: Breadth (use cases, styles, results) under one statement.
techniques.avoid_when: Text that changes during the montage.
techniques.materials: Not every change is a cut: for 4-8 f the next image is double-exposed over the current one (screen or lighten at 40-60 %), and the last still leaves by smearing sideways (a blur ramp 0 -> 40 px over 8 f) with a spectral leading edge (red, yellow, white, transparent) in screen blend.
conditions: the film's one spectral accent

techniques.name: A designed hold that clicks into place
techniques.summary: A held frame on purpose: the settled mark is bit-identical for 4 frames as it clicks into place; a stamped line sits perfectly still while only the background light pools move; a title holds over a second with under 3 px drift.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: no creep on the element for the hold (declare the still range); keep LightField or grain alive. Anatomy: 4-28 f of stillness; a living background layer. Sound: Silence or the voice.
techniques.use_when: After a landing that should feel locked.
techniques.avoid_when: Long dead holds without any living layer.

techniques.name: An empty beat before the logo
techniques.summary: After the last phrase blurs out, the frame stays empty (just the ground and its light) for about three quarters of a second before the logo arrives.
techniques.recipe: A gap in the timeline with the LightField still running. Anatomy: Ground only, light field alive. Sound: Quiet.
techniques.timing: 45 f at 60 fps.
techniques.use_when: Before the end card.
techniques.avoid_when: Longer than about 1 s; a dead black frame without the ground's light.

techniques.name: No low end until the reveal
techniques.summary: The opening plays over near silence or a light, high bed (soft high clicks on each hard step, an arpeggio with no kick and no bass), and the full-band music enters exactly on the reveal frame and stays.
techniques.recipe: Timeline: mute the kick and bass stems until the reveal cue and schedule a tick on every hard step before it. Anatomy: Before the drop the bed is high-passed at about 200 Hz and the ticks sit at -45 to -32 dB with centroids at 3.5-7 kHz; at the drop the RMS rises 6-7 dB and the low band goes from about 1 % to about 30 % of the energy, within one frame of the reveal. Sound: This is the sound device.
techniques.timing: The drop on the reveal frame, typically 4-6 s in.
techniques.use_when: Every launch film with a construction or build-up act.
techniques.avoid_when: Films that open on the product.

techniques.name: Whoosh run into a thud; the swap just before the kick
techniques.summary: A series of whooshes accompanies a collapse and an exit, then a heavy thud lands on the frame the title's letters land; a word swap is placed about 90 ms before the loudest kick, so the eye gets there first.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: cue the thud on the landing frame from Letters' letterFrames(); the swap at kick - 5 f. Anatomy: Whoosh run about 36 f; thud +9 dB; swap 5 f before the kick at 60 fps. Sound: This is the sound device. Materials: A kick roll builds under a pull-back (five kicks at 0.09-0.18 s intervals) and a bright water-drop sound (a sine sweep 900 -> 1600 Hz over 60 ms, fast decay, a little reverb) lands exactly as the button starts to separate.
techniques.timing: Run 36 f; lead 5 f.
techniques.use_when: Title landings; swaps on strong beats.
techniques.avoid_when: Thuds without a visual landing.
techniques.materials: A kick roll builds under a pull-back (five kicks at 0.09-0.18 s intervals) and a bright water-drop sound (a sine sweep 900 -> 1600 Hz over 60 ms, fast decay, a little reverb) lands exactly as the button starts to separate.

techniques.name: Montage of constant-rate dolly-outs cut on snares
techniques.summary: A run of shots (billboards, posters, streets) each with a steady pull-back at a constant log rate, cut on snares, so the whole run reads as one continuous retreat.
techniques.recipe: <Montage> with one travel (pull) and cuts on the accent list. Anatomy: Same log rate in every shot; cuts within 45 ms of snares; the last shot longer. Sound: Cuts on snares.
techniques.timing: Shots 25-50 f; final 85 f.
techniques.use_when: Showing the product out in the world; the climax montage.
techniques.avoid_when: Shots with different move directions.

techniques.name: One shot goes completely still
techniques.summary: After constant motion everywhere, one shot lands and holds completely still for half a second; the stillness becomes the emphasis.
techniques.recipe: A move on E.snapOut that ends exactly; then no creep for 28 f (declare the still range). Anatomy: Pull-out into the cut accelerating, the next shot opens still moving, then stops dead. Sound: A ding on the still frame.
techniques.timing: Out 14 f, in 20 f, still 28 f.
techniques.use_when: The keyword of the film ("Instantly").
techniques.avoid_when: More than once per film; holds longer than about 30 f.

techniques.name: No hard cuts: every change hides in a camera event
techniques.summary: A whole film with no plain cuts: every scene change rides a cloud dive, a foreground wipe, a whip, a white-out, a zoom-through, a velocity jump or an iris; about 13 sections of 2.7 s each.
techniques.recipe: One camera function for the film (lib/camera-moves), a seam list where every seam has a declared carrier. Anatomy: A carrier per seam from the transition families; sections 2-3 s. Sound: Transitions on whooshes and swells.
techniques.timing: Sections about 160 f each.
techniques.use_when: A launch film that should feel like one continuous journey.
techniques.avoid_when: Repeating the same carrier twice in a row.

techniques.name: Calm hold marked only by small label pops
techniques.summary: A grid holds almost still for several seconds and the only events are three small labels popping next to tiles about a second apart: rest that still has a pulse.
techniques.recipe: living hold + Words pop for labels. Anatomy: Camera creep only (0.98-1.0); label pops 1 s apart. Sound: A bubble pop and a click on the pops; a low hit.
techniques.timing: 344 f hold; pops 50-70 f apart.
techniques.use_when: After a busy run; to let a layout be read.
techniques.avoid_when: Holds longer than about 6 s.

techniques.name: Zoom energy decays shot by shot
techniques.summary: After a zoom transition, each following shot pushes in less than the one before (2.1 %/f, 0.54, 0.20, 0), so the sequence calms down without any shot being static.
techniques.recipe: Montage with push per shot decaying (MONTAGE ratio 0.3), or per-shot creep() rates from a decaying list. Anatomy: Per shot push rate times about 0.3. Sound: The bed thins with it.
techniques.timing: Over 65 f of shots.
techniques.use_when: The run of shots after a big transition.
techniques.avoid_when: Reversing the order (it reads as random).

techniques.name: The music stops for a breath before the reveal
techniques.summary: The music drops out (or dips 7-10 dB) for 0.2-0.5 s right before each big transition or reveal, and the reveal lands on the returning hit; long silences (0.65-1.75 s) can sit under holds and before reveals; a background can change on the silence; the film's only hard cut can land on a voice onset inside a drop-out.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: mark reveals in the timeline; the music ducker cuts the bed for 0.3 s before each. Anatomy: Drop to about -33 to -40 LUFS for 18-30 f; the hit on the reveal frame. Sound: This is the sound device: drop-out, then the hit.
techniques.timing: 12-30 f dips; silences 40-105 f.
techniques.use_when: Before every big reveal; two to five times per film.
techniques.avoid_when: Dips before small events (they lose their power).

techniques.name: The copy and the work continue on real surfaces
techniques.summary: After the product moment the work leaves the screen: the headlines continue as the copy of billboards and light boxes, the edited image appears as printed magazines, a print lifted through a hard window shadow, a poster wall, a street hoarding, a screen among plants; passers-by and cars cross the foreground as natural wipes.
techniques.recipe: Photo or Footage with the artwork placed by matrix3d onto the print's quad, a multiply shadow plate over it, and a blurred occluder cut-out translating across. Anatomy: 3-6 shots of 25-90 f; the hero artwork composited onto each surface by a perspective transform with a multiply shadow layer (a hard 45 deg window shadow at 55 %); at night light boxes at about twice the surround with a soft bloom; foreground occluders cross in 20-30 f. Sound: Music continues; cuts on beats. Materials: Real imagery leads: free photos of surfaces, the artwork composited, one shared light direction per shot; screens cast a faint glow on what is near them.
techniques.timing: Shots 25-90 f on the beat; a slow push of 1-3 % per shot.
techniques.use_when: Creative and brand tools: made here, used everywhere; the last act before the logo.
techniques.avoid_when: Internal tools with no visible output; weak mock-ups.
techniques.materials: Real imagery leads: free photos of surfaces, the artwork composited, one shared light direction per shot; screens cast a faint glow on what is near them.

techniques.name: Code streams in line by line
techniques.summary: Code lines appear in a panel about one line every 2 frames, stepped, carrying the only saturated colours in the frame (syntax colours), and keep streaming under a zoom-out.
techniques.recipe: TypeOn kind="stream" with a line-quantised count. Anatomy: One line per 2 f; syntax colours as the only saturation. Sound: None distinct.
techniques.use_when: Developer products; "it writes the code".
techniques.avoid_when: Readable fake code (keep it plausible, real-looking).

techniques.name: Button flies in carrying the pointer
techniques.summary: A call-to-action button enters bottom-right tilted and small, travels on a curved path carrying the pointer with it, and takes a word's slot in the line.
techniques.recipe: cursorMove on a bowed path with the button attached to the cursor's transform. Anatomy: Start -7 deg at 80 % size; x peak 147 px/f before y peak 32 px/f (curved path). Sound: A pop and whoosh.
techniques.use_when: Ending a demo on the action.
techniques.avoid_when: Pointer and button on separate paths.

techniques.name: The cursor as a character
techniques.summary: An oversized cursor (8-12 % of the frame height) with its own look lives in the shot: it banks into its motion within 2 frames, a thick 3D cursor half-spins about its axis and is edge-on at peak speed, a glossy cursor idles with slow decelerating drifts between clicks, an outlined cursor swings upright as it lands and morphs into an I-beam.
techniques.recipe: <Cursor shape scale shadow="cast"> with cursorTilt (swing) and a shape switch to ibeam. Anatomy: Size 120-170 px; bank = f(velocity); swing from -60 deg to upright over 3 f; idle drift 10 -> 0 px/f. Sound: Mouse clicks. Materials: A glossy 3D cursor (matte white body, a warm bevel gradient, soft drop shadow) rests on the first letter of a line, then rises and passes behind it for 6 f: the letter is drawn over the cursor's tip, as if the cursor were an object moving between layers of type.
techniques.timing: Travel 40-52 f (peak 50-80 px/f at about 50 %); swing 8 f.
techniques.use_when: Launch films where the product is used by "you".
techniques.avoid_when: Multiple cursor styles in one film.
techniques.materials: A glossy 3D cursor (matte white body, a warm bevel gradient, soft drop shadow) rests on the first letter of a line, then rises and passes behind it for 6 f: the letter is drawn over the cursor's tip, as if the cursor were an object moving between layers of type.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Cursor drags an object into place
techniques.summary: A grab-hand cursor drags a value cell (tilted about 15 deg, straightening as it drops), a folder into a grid, or a dashed selection marquee across a collage; the hand can squash +33 % on contact and relax.
techniques.recipe: cursorMove with the dragged object attached by a lagged spring (one per film) or a short delay. Anatomy: Object tilt -15 deg -> 0 on drop; drag expo-out; contact pop 3 f, relax 6 f. Sound: A drum on the drop.
techniques.timing: Drag 26-42 f; drop 8 f.
techniques.use_when: Drag-and-drop features; selections.
techniques.avoid_when: Dragged objects that do not tilt or lag (they look glued).

techniques.name: The cursor leaves in flight once the product acts
techniques.summary: After its click the cursor does not fade: it accelerates off the frame on a quad- or expo-in, banking upright as it goes (3 -> 270 px/f); or it travels to the next button, presses, and drifts off.
techniques.recipe: cursorMove with an exit move on E.buildIn off-frame. Anatomy: Exit speed x1.3-1.9 a frame; bank follows velocity. Sound: An impact as the last button is pressed. Materials: After the click the cursor does not just translate: it turns about 200 deg in 10 f (peak about 20 deg/f, expo-out) while it accelerates off the top-right like a flicked paper plane; no motion blur, so the turn reads as a run of poses.
techniques.use_when: After the last click of a demo moment.
techniques.avoid_when: Fading the cursor; leaving it parked on screen.
techniques.materials: After the click the cursor does not just translate: it turns about 200 deg in 10 f (peak about 20 deg/f, expo-out) while it accelerates off the top-right like a flicked paper plane; no motion blur, so the turn reads as a run of poses.

techniques.name: Cursor glides in, dwells, then clicks
techniques.summary: The cursor enters (often rising from below), decelerates onto its target, rests 5-8 frames, then clicks; the button darkens for a few frames; the card or the camera can start pulling back or pushing in right after the press; or the cursor simply cuts on already over the button and presses.
techniques.recipe: cursorState({ moves, click }) + press() on the target. Anatomy: Travel 22-44 f on an ease-out (172 px in 22 f), dwell 10-16 f, press 6-12 f; macro variant: a hand pressing a cropped send button in close-up. Sound: A click on the press; a kick on the following cut.
techniques.timing: 40-70 f per click.
techniques.use_when: Every click in a demo.
techniques.avoid_when: Clicking on arrival with no dwell.

techniques.name: Edits happen in place under the hovering cursor
techniques.summary: The cursor hovers and the image or label changes in place: a product label swaps in one frame after a slow push; a cheek is relit in one step, lips brighten slowly over 45 f; the rest of the picture is untouched.
techniques.recipe: HardStep or a short fade between two versions of the region (masked copies). Anatomy: One-frame steps for discrete edits; slow fades for continuous ones; masks per edited region. Sound: Key clicks.
techniques.timing: Steps 1 f; slow edits 45 f; push 40 f.
techniques.use_when: Image or design editing products.
techniques.avoid_when: Big transitions for small edits.

techniques.name: Hover states fire along the cursor's path
techniques.summary: The cursor sweeps up in one expo-out and every row it passes gets a hover outline for a few frames; a hover on an icon brings a small tooltip; a cursor wanders between the input and cards while the UI eases back.
techniques.recipe: cursorState + per-element hover flags from the cursor's position at each frame. Anatomy: Hover 6-8 f per row; tooltip hold 28 f. Sound: A whoosh as it enters.
techniques.timing: Sweep 52 f (44 % in 10 %).
techniques.use_when: Showing that a UI is alive and responsive.
techniques.avoid_when: Hover states lasting longer than the pass.

techniques.name: Thumbnails stay alive inside the cards
techniques.summary: Cards contain playing motion pieces: logo marks swap colour, words morph, images move, so a board of cards is never a still screenshot.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: each card renders a small composition in <Loop> with awkward periods. Anatomy: Per card a tiny loop with its own period. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Continuous; letter swaps 14 f.
techniques.use_when: Boards, galleries, dashboards with media.
techniques.avoid_when: Every thumbnail moving at once at full speed.

techniques.name: Dragged paint as a pixel mosaic trailing the cursor
techniques.summary: A blob of the accent rendered in 15-20 px mosaic blocks trails behind the cursor like dragged paint, growing, its tail lagging about 10 frames, then retracting.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: the cursor path (closed form) sampled back in time, each sample stamping blocks of a grid. Anatomy: Trail sampled from the cursor path over the last 10 f, rasterised to a block grid. Sound: None needed. Materials: The trail is a row of stamped copies of one rounded blob along the path, each older stamp darker and less saturated, all drawn through a coarse pixelation (16 px blocks at 1080p, downscale then upscale nearest-neighbour) so soft edges show 3-4 brightness steps; it grows, cruises and shrinks with the cursor's speed and is sucked into the button.
techniques.timing: 44 f; retract 35 px/f.
techniques.use_when: Drawing, painting, brushing tools.
techniques.avoid_when: Smooth gradients for the trail (the mosaic is the look).
techniques.materials: The trail is a row of stamped copies of one rounded blob along the path, each older stamp darker and less saturated, all drawn through a coarse pixelation (16 px blocks at 1080p, downscale then upscale nearest-neighbour) so soft edges show 3-4 brightness steps; it grows, cruises and shrinks with the cursor's speed and is sucked into the button.

techniques.name: Phone demo: pull back, tilt while scrolling, press, popup
techniques.summary: Close on the app header, pull back; the phone tilts away in 3D while its content scrolls with in-out gestures; a cursor clicks, a floating button presses, a popup grows from its anchor.
techniques.recipe: camera pull + Cards lean + Scroll + press + springBox from the anchor. Anatomy: Pull 26 f; scroll 70 f; press 6-8 f; popup 16 f from the anchor. Sound: UI clicks.
techniques.timing: About 190 f.
techniques.use_when: Mobile app walkthroughs.
techniques.avoid_when: Straight-on flat phones for the whole demo.

techniques.name: A pointer glyph turns to aim, then moves
techniques.summary: A small pointer shape (a paper plane, a triangle) first rotates to aim at its target, then travels; a tiny pointer drifts in an empty cell and the target appears exactly where it stops; a filled pointer glides into a vacated slot.
techniques.recipe: Cursor custom shape with cursorTilt then cursorMove. Anatomy: Rotate 30-90 deg over 16-20 f ease-out, then rise or glide; drift 2-4 px/f. Sound: None needed. Materials: Letter tiles in the pointer's path flip in 3D: a tile goes edge-on (a 4-6 px parallelogram) in about 4 f, starting 2-4 f before the pointer reaches it, a flipped tile shows its letter mirrored; the cut lands before the flip completes.
techniques.use_when: Illustrative, non-literal UI films.
techniques.avoid_when: Pointers that move before they aim.
techniques.materials: Letter tiles in the pointer's path flip in 3D: a tile goes edge-on (a 4-6 px parallelogram) in about 4 f, starting 2-4 f before the pointer reaches it, a flipped tile shows its letter mirrored; the cut lands before the flip completes.

techniques.name: Product UI framed over live footage
techniques.summary: A rounded screen with a thin rim floats over desaturated moving footage (a figure walking in a forest); a cut-out hand holding a phone slides in and rotates upright.
techniques.recipe: <Footage> graded down + a Card on top; the hand as a Cutouts piece. Anatomy: Footage desaturated; screen with rim; hand slide 91 px + 10 deg rotation circ-out. Sound: None needed. Materials: Before the edit demos, a few seconds of generated commercial footage of the subject and product (a wide studio shot with gear in frame, a profile close-up, a frontal close-up), cool seamless with warm skin, the last clip frozen under the edit overlays: the raw material the product works on.
techniques.timing: Hand 40 f; footage plays.
techniques.use_when: Putting the product in the world without a full live-action shoot.
techniques.avoid_when: Saturated footage competing with the UI.
techniques.materials: Before the edit demos, a few seconds of generated commercial footage of the subject and product (a wide studio shot with gear in frame, a profile close-up, a frontal close-up), cool seamless with warm skin, the last clip frozen under the edit overlays: the raw material the product works on.

techniques.name: One generated character carried across plates
techniques.summary: The same generated person appears in two or three photographic plates (worried in one place, shocked over a phone in another): the same face and clothes and a consistent grade, so the story has a protagonist without a shoot.
techniques.recipe: Photo plates sharing one grade; UI layers above. Anatomy: Shallow depth of field (an f/2 look), warm highlights and shadows pushed toward the brand hue; a slow push of 0.3 % per frame; UI cards and bubbles over the plate. Sound: The VO tells the pain; chat pops on the UI.
techniques.timing: Plates 100-160 f; cut on the counter-to-shock beat with a momentum zoom.
techniques.use_when: Problem-and-answer stories; reaction beats around UI cards and bubbles.
techniques.avoid_when: Uncanny results; more than three plates.

techniques.name: Detection boxes keep faces in true colour while the frame turns false-colour
techniques.summary: Over video panels thin white boxes lock onto every face; outside the boxes the footage turns into a false-colour gradient map while inside each box the face stays in true colour, and the map changes with each feature (a cool map, a mint map, a heat map) as small labels type in.
techniques.recipe: Footage twice: a full-frame copy under a static map filter and the plain copy clipped to each box (overflow hidden, offset by the box position). Anatomy: Boxes 1.5 px white, snapping with no easing, popping before the tint; outside a three-stop map (shadows deep, mids the accent, highlights pale); inside, the plain footage clipped to the box; the palette changes about every 80 f; the heat map adds a warm edge glow where luma changes fast. Sound: Soft ticks per label. Materials: Cool map deep teal -> cyan -> ice; mint map green -> mint -> near-white; heat map lilac -> peach -> warm edges with a pale highlight.
techniques.timing: Boxes pop in 4 f, tint in 8 f, labels type over 24 f; about 80 f per palette; a fade to white at the end.
techniques.use_when: Vision, detection, search-in-video and analysis products: showing what the model sees.
techniques.avoid_when: Products with nothing visual to detect.
techniques.materials: Cool map deep teal -> cyan -> ice; mint map green -> mint -> near-white; heat map lilac -> peach -> warm edges with a pale highlight.

techniques.name: Typing that accelerates into a whip
techniques.summary: The gaps between keys shrink (5, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1 frames) while the camera follows the caret on a decaying push, then whips away before the line ends.
techniques.recipe: <TypeOn kind="prompt" gaps={ACCEL.typing} skip> with typeOn() caret camera into whip(). Anatomy: Accelerating key gaps; camera tracks the caret (decay power 2.6) in close-up; the whip hides the last keys. Sound: One click per keystroke; the music drops out for 0.3 s before the next hit.
techniques.timing: Gaps 5, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1 f at 60 fps (20 f in all); close-up runs 12, 12, 7, 5, 7, 5, 5, 5 f per character.
techniques.use_when: Handing off from a typed request to the product's reaction.
techniques.avoid_when: A line the viewer must read to the end.

techniques.name: Placeholder deletes, the real value types in bursts
techniques.summary: A placeholder in a field deletes quickly, then the real value types in irregular 1-2 character bursts: the field is being edited, not filled.
techniques.recipe: Two TypeOn runs: the first with its count reversed (characters shown = n - count), the second human kind. Anatomy: Backspace run (about 11 characters in 10 f), a beat, then bursts. Sound: A chat pop mid-typing if a reply comes in.
techniques.timing: Delete about 33 characters a second; retype about 26 a second in bursts; 48 f in all.
techniques.use_when: A URL, a name or a setting being changed in the product.
techniques.avoid_when: Fields the viewer has not seen filled before.

techniques.name: Typing that starts mostly done after a cut
techniques.summary: After a cut, the prompt is already 50-80 % typed and the rest types with deceleration: the film skips the boring part.
techniques.recipe: <TypeOn from={0.65} kind="stream" ease={E.type}>. Anatomy: First frame 50-80 % typed; the rest decelerates. Sound: A keypress bed rather than per-key clicks.
techniques.timing: About 93 cps for 5 f, then 59, 51... slowing; 75 f for 51 characters.
techniques.use_when: Several prompts in a row, montages of requests.
techniques.avoid_when: The first prompt of a film (show one typed in full first).

techniques.name: Typing by a person, with word-end pauses
techniques.summary: Text types the way a person types: runs inside words, a pause of 1-2 frames at word ends, an I-beam caret; the UI around it reacts (a send button pops before the sentence ends, icons pop when it is done).
techniques.recipe: <TypeOn kind="human">; a send button pop is press/springBox started 4-6 f before the last key. Anatomy: Characters cut on (optionally a 4 f fade each); variants: a line typing above the previous one so the stack builds upward; a first word that pops whole and a second that types; a wrap onto a second line. Sound: Key clicks per keystroke at -13 to -24 dBFS, or none.
techniques.timing: 24-45 characters a second inside words, +2-4 f per space; human kind: 30 cps in runs, one key pause at commas.
techniques.use_when: A prompt or search typed into the product, a title on a device screen, any line that should feel human.
techniques.avoid_when: Machine output (use a stream); long paragraphs.

techniques.name: Prompt typing that slows on its last word
techniques.summary: A prompt types at a steady rate and slows on its last word, letter by letter, so the request lands with intent.
techniques.recipe: <TypeOn kind="prompt"> (last word x1.6 house; raise to x2.5 for emphasis). Anatomy: Steady about 30-33 characters a second, then one character every 4-8 f on the last word. Sound: Typing ticks, the last key softer. Materials: When the text outgrows the field it scrolls left under a feathered left edge (a 50-70 px mask) instead of a hard clip; once typing stops the caret blinks slowly (12 f on, 20 f off).
techniques.timing: Whole prompt 50-90 f; last word 1.6-3x slower.
techniques.use_when: The question that triggers the product's answer.
techniques.avoid_when: Typing that is cut before it ends.
techniques.materials: When the text outgrows the field it scrolls left under a feathered left edge (a 50-70 px mask) instead of a hard clip; once typing stops the caret blinks slowly (12 f on, 20 f off).

techniques.name: A wall of fields all typing at once
techniques.summary: Cut to a wall of question pills all typing word chunks simultaneously (offset 1-3 f), send buttons popping as they finish; the next cut pushes in with a new background colour.
techniques.recipe: Many <TypeOn kind="field"> with seeded starts. Anatomy: 6-12 TypeOn instances with seeded offsets; pops on completion. Sound: UI pops on the cuts.
techniques.use_when: Scale: many users, many questions.
techniques.avoid_when: Readable sentences (it is texture).

techniques.name: A band of glyphs traces every subject's edge
techniques.summary: Around every subject of a photo or plate a band of tiny white monospace glyphs hugs the silhouette like a typed outline (the heaviest glyph at the strongest edge, lighter ones further out, dots bleeding inside); it re-samples every frame so it shimmers as the plate moves, and before a cut it flares, wider, heavier and brighter, and the frame breaks into blocks.
techniques.recipe: The Ascii glyph atlas drawn on a canvas from a downscaled luma of the plate, with an edge magnitude per cell. Anatomy: Cells 13.5 x 14 px at 1080p, fixed to the screen; the glyph picked by edge strength on a blurred luma: over 0.6 a zero, 0.4-0.6 a small o, 0.2-0.4 a colon, 0.1-0.2 a dot, else empty; white at 0.75-0.9; the band sits mostly outside the silhouette (2-4 cells). Flare: threshold 0.4 -> 0.1 and alpha 0.6 -> 1 over 12 f into a pixelate cut. Sound: None of its own; the flare rides the rising whoosh into the hit. Materials: On strong straight edges the glyph follows the edge angle (tall glyphs on vertical edges, round ones on curves).
techniques.timing: Lives for the plate; flare 12 f, then the pixelate.
techniques.use_when: Generated imagery, vision and generation products; plates that need a signature texture.
techniques.avoid_when: UI shots; small subjects.
techniques.materials: On strong straight edges the glyph follows the edge angle (tall glyphs on vertical edges, round ones on curves).

techniques.name: Symbol string tiles the frame and resolves into an ASCII object
techniques.summary: A short string of symbols repeats in a grid that fills the panel, turns into character columns, and resolves into a flickering ASCII-dither globe.
techniques.recipe: Build: <AsciiField at x y w h src color> (fx/Ascii): the symbol string tiles the panel, turns into seeded character columns (from 22 f), the picture resolves through a dark-to-light glyph ramp (from 44 f, settled by 63) and flickers like a dither: about 6 % of the cells swap to a ramp neighbour every 3-8 f.
