Anatomy: Grid of characters; columns; luminance mapped to a glyph ramp; style flicker every 1-3 f. Sound: None needed.
techniques.timing: Settle 63 f; flicker every 3-8 f at 60 fps.
techniques.use_when: A film about the web, data or the world; a title reveal from code.
techniques.avoid_when: Without a plate to convert.

techniques.name: Radial lens chromatic aberration on light lines
techniques.summary: A red fringe on one side and cyan on the other of silhouettes and caption edges, present on every graphic frame as a fixed offset. Two flavours: a radial lens aberration over the whole graphic layer, so every thin luminous line is three lines (warm toward the frame centre, a green core, blue outside) with a split that grows with distance from the centre; or a lateral split on 3D edges that makes hard lines read as cut glass catching light.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: two tinted copies offset 2-3 px under the element. Recipe: render the graphic layer three times with mix-blend screen, each keeping one channel (feColorMatrix), scaled 0.982 / 1 / 1.018 about the frame centre (radial) or offset -1 / 0 / +1 px (lateral). Anatomy: Static offset of two tinted copies. Radial: channel scale about 1.8 % of the radius each way (red 0.982, blue 1.018 about the frame centre), so a line at r 450 px carries about 28 px of red-green-blue cross-section plus a wide soft blue glow outside (sigma about 20 px) and a warm haze inside; lines near the centre lose their fringe (a spiral loses it as it tightens). Lateral: 1-1.5 px each side (a warm line one side, cyan the other) round a white core, larger toward the frame edge, with a neutral grey glow. Sound: None. Materials: Static optical property: it animates only because things move through radius. Build it once as a layer over all graphics, never per element.
techniques.timing: Static.
techniques.use_when: A graphic, glitch-flavoured world.
techniques.avoid_when: Clean UI films.
techniques.materials: Static optical property: it animates only because things move through radius. Build it once as a layer over all graphics, never per element.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
the film's one spectral accent

techniques.name: Faint concentric rings behind the subject
techniques.summary: Very faint concentric ellipses or circles sit behind a word reveal or a centred line, sometimes with tiny accent satellites on them that rotate with a chip ring; a small concentric decal can sit under a hero core.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: static SVG circles; satellites placed by angle and rotated with the ring's closed-form angle. Anatomy: 4-5 rings at a few percent contrast; satellites about 6 px. Sound: None. Materials: Echo rings follow the morph: as the page darkens the faint concentric circles brighten into lines and, in sync with the centre circle becoming a rounded card, stretch horizontally into concentric stadium outlines (straight segment 0 -> about 700 px in 10-12 f, in-out).
techniques.timing: Static or rotating with the ring.
techniques.use_when: Centred statements; orbit and ecosystem ideas.
techniques.avoid_when: Rings strong enough to read.
techniques.materials: Echo rings follow the morph: as the page darkens the faint concentric circles brighten into lines and, in sync with the centre circle becoming a rounded card, stretch horizontally into concentric stadium outlines (straight segment 0 -> about 700 px in 10-12 f, in-out).

techniques.name: Graphic smear frames instead of motion blur
techniques.summary: Speed is drawn as designed frames, not shutter blur: 2-3 faint offset copies trail a fast card for a few frames; the nearest figure has a 50 % double behind it; a label box stretches along a hop for exactly one frame; a line lunges 64 px and smears one frame before a scale snap; words are doubled or streaked on the first frame after a cut; a logo's first frame is a rotational blur ring.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Rush copies={{ n: 3, lag: 1, fade: 0.45 }}> (fx/Rush): 2-3 copies where the element was 1-3 frames ago, at 45 %, 20 %, 9 %, only on frames faster than 18 px/f, never across the cut; <Corners mode="jump"> draws the same idea as echo bars on markers. Anatomy: Copies at decreasing opacity along the motion; one-frame stretch; one-frame ghost. Sound: A kick on the logo cut; none for most.
techniques.use_when: Stylised films where real blur would look soft; accents on single fast moments.
techniques.avoid_when: Using it everywhere (it is an accent).

techniques.name: Dither-pixel patch licks up through outlines
techniques.summary: A patch of light dither pixels (small crosses) sweeps from bottom to top through a line drawing and dies out; the same burst repeats once.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a seeded dither mask plate translated upward, multiplied with the line art. Recipe: a canvas clipped to the shape's path; per cell value = band(y + 6f) x (0.5 + 0.5 noise(x, y)); fillText the ramp glyph when the value is over 0.1. Anatomy: Coverage 0.9 -> 4.2 -> 0.8 %; bursts 21 f apart. Sound: A stab and a kick. Materials: A glyph patch licks up through a big shape and stays inside its outline: tiny light glyphs on a value ramp (dot < dash < equals < plus < x), denser in the middle and sparser at the edges, cells about 12 px at 1080p, colour a pale tint of the shape at 60-80 %; the band is about 45 % of the shape tall and scrolls about 6 px/f upward; each burst lives 32 f and repeats 52 f later.
techniques.timing: 30 f per burst.
techniques.use_when: End cards with line art; a "spark" without sparkles.
techniques.avoid_when: Coverage above about 5 %.
techniques.materials: A glyph patch licks up through a big shape and stays inside its outline: tiny light glyphs on a value ramp (dot < dash < equals < plus < x), denser in the middle and sparser at the edges, cells about 12 px at 1080p, colour a pale tint of the shape at 60-80 %; the band is about 45 % of the shape tall and scrolls about 6 px/f upward; each burst lives 32 f and repeats 52 f later.

techniques.name: Dot grid seen only under wandering light
techniques.summary: A black stage carries a fine dot grid that is only visible where two or three very soft light pools drift, so the ground breathes with light.
techniques.recipe: LightField pools with the dot-grid plate as their mask (mix-blend multiply on a static grid layer). Anatomy: 12 px dot grid (luma 17-63) multiplied by the light pools (radius 300-500 px). Sound: None. Materials: Lights tint the grid: in a dark grid room the lines near each glowing object take that object's colour and brighten (spill radius 150-250 px, near lines at about 200 luma, far lines 40-60), so the grid reads as lit by the objects and the tints move with them.
techniques.timing: Continuous.
techniques.use_when: Dark openers; tech films that want depth without objects.
techniques.avoid_when: Pools that move fast (keep them slow, every 6-18 f of drift).
techniques.materials: Lights tint the grid: in a dark grid room the lines near each glowing object take that object's colour and brighten (spill radius 150-250 px, near lines at about 200 luma, far lines 40-60), so the grid reads as lit by the objects and the tints move with them.

techniques.name: Rim highlight from a fixed light
techniques.summary: Every container has a 1 px hairline rim that is brightest at one spot, and the bright spot stays put as the container moves: the light source is fixed in the world.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a conic highlight on the border whose angle is computed from the card's position against a fixed light point. Anatomy: Rim highlight computed from the container's position relative to a fixed light. Sound: None. Materials: A spectral rim: a black wordmark on a bright gradient carries a 1.5 px rim at about 0.8, warm on the edges facing the light and cool on the opposite edges (two offset text-shadows), and its interiors carry a faint vertical gradient instead of flat black.
techniques.timing: Static per shot.
techniques.use_when: Floating cards in a soft, airy look.
techniques.avoid_when: Glass looks in house films.
techniques.materials: A spectral rim: a black wordmark on a bright gradient carries a 1.5 px rim at about 0.8, warm on the edges facing the light and cool on the opposite edges (two offset text-shadows), and its interiors carry a faint vertical gradient instead of flat black.
conditions: glass as a material with real frost or refraction, not a default card style
the film's one spectral accent
gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Ground made of vertical bars
techniques.summary: The background is a field of flat vertical bars (about 100 px wide), each a single shade, so a soft glow reads as a stepped poster; or vertical stripes with soft light gradients like fluted glass.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: render the light field into a few bands of flat colour (posterised horizontally), moved by transform. Shader or canvas: x quantised to 16 bars, band = smoothstep on the distance to a tilted line that moves, colour from a ramp at the bar's centre; the bars have hard edges, so banding is not an issue. Anatomy: Bars quantise a smooth field into steps; the glow can spread, sweep and wander. Sound: None. Materials: The glow is a staircase, not a gradient: hard vertical bars, each one flat colour stepping from a warm deep tone through the accent to violet and black across the frame (about 16 bars), with a smooth fade to black vertically; the glow band slides and tilts so the bars light up and go dark in waves, like an audio meter under the music.
techniques.timing: Spread 36 f; sweep 150 f; wander 244 f.
techniques.use_when: Brand-colour sections; checkout or store panels.
techniques.avoid_when: A second multi-hue field in the same film.
techniques.materials: The glow is a staircase, not a gradient: hard vertical bars, each one flat colour stepping from a warm deep tone through the accent to violet and black across the frame (about 16 bars), with a smooth fade to black vertically; the glow band slides and tilts so the bars light up and go dark in waves, like an audio meter under the music.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
glass as a material with real frost or refraction, not a default card style

techniques.name: A word seen through fluted glass, sliced into refracted strips
techniques.summary: The logo or a word sits behind reeded glass: it is broken into vertical bands, each a sideways-shifted, softened slice, so it flickers between sliced and legible while it moves; then the bands clear and the word is sharp.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: an SVG displacement map driven by a static repeating-gradient stripe image; the strength steps through fixed levels (pre-rendered copies cross-faded). Anatomy: Stripes 40-60 px; per stripe a sawtooth displacement of up to 15-25 px with a lens ramp inside each stripe; edges softened about 4 px; strength 1 -> 0 over 28 f. Sound: A whoosh on the logo's move.
techniques.use_when: A logo or a word reveal on a dark, lit ground; a clarity beat.
techniques.avoid_when: Long lines; flat light grounds.

techniques.name: A portrait drawn in two digits under a rising gradient
techniques.summary: A picture is set as a terminal dump of monospace digits: one digit fills the ground, the other draws the figure in two-by-two blocks like pixel art, and a vertical gradient (white at the top, the accent at the bottom) rises through the glyphs until the card is accent on accent.
techniques.recipe: AsciiField with a bitmap source and a two-glyph ramp, its glyph layer used as a mask over a baked dithered gradient plate that rises by transform. Anatomy: Glyph cap about 14 px at 1080p, pitch about 17 px; the figure from a 1-bit bitmap on a grid of two-by-two glyph cells; fill = a gradient clipped to the glyphs whose top edge rises from 100 % to -20 % of the card; afterwards the glyphs are a pale tint of the accent on the accent. Sound: The card morph sits on a kick. Materials: Stops: near-white at the top edge, then the accent, then a deeper accent at the bottom; glyph colour after the rise = the accent mixed 25 % toward white.
techniques.timing: Gradient rise 50 f expo-out, texture holds 75 f.
techniques.use_when: Developer, data and scraping products; the moment a card turns into what the machine sees.
techniques.avoid_when: A film that already leans on a glyph texture elsewhere.
techniques.materials: Stops: near-white at the top edge, then the accent, then a deeper accent at the bottom; glyph colour after the rise = the accent mixed 25 % toward white.

techniques.name: Grain and print texture as the picture's finish
techniques.summary: Images carry visible grain, low-contrast highlights and soft focus while vector type stays razor sharp on top; white type over imagery carries a speckled, slightly broken print texture; a near-black stage carries a barely visible vertical micro-texture (3-5 % luma).
techniques.recipe: Recipe: cycled grain plates (seeded), a static speckle mask on the type, a baked micro-texture plate. Anatomy: Grain changing every frame; print speckle static; micro-texture most visible near the hero's glow. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Grain every frame; others static.
techniques.use_when: Editorial, image-led or dark tech films.
techniques.avoid_when: Grain on UI text; texture strong enough to read.

techniques.name: Accent blocks jump between grid cells on kicks
techniques.summary: Solid accent blocks exactly one grid cell in size sit in the page grid forming steps and L shapes, and jump to new cells instantly, all together, on kicks.
techniques.recipe: HardStep positions from a table of cells indexed by the kick list. Anatomy: Blocks of one cell (192 px at 1080p); arrangements from a seeded table indexed by kick count. Sound: Kicks.
techniques.timing: 0 f transitions; rearrangements 13-25 f apart.
techniques.use_when: Grid-based brands; a beat-driven interlude.
techniques.avoid_when: Tweening the blocks.

techniques.name: Grid cells switch on in a wave
techniques.summary: Cells on a fixed grid switch on outward from a centre (each at one of a few random opacities), fade in as a radial wave and out centre-first, appear radially around a hub in a few steps, materialise in a diagonal wipe from a corner (duotone first, then colour), or multiply outward from one coloured cell.
techniques.recipe: Build: <CellWave at cols rows x y color shape="radial"|"diagonal"> (fx/Grids): cells switch on outward from origin at one of five seeded strengths (15-100 %), radial on E.buildIn over 23 f (on twos for the first 8 f) or diagonal (+1 f per column, +1.4 per row); fade={40} for a slow in-out, out={{ at }} leaves centre-first; render(cell) puts a thumbnail in each cell. Anatomy: Radial or diagonal threshold over a static grid; per-cell opacity from 5 levels (15-100 %); on twos for the first frames, then ones; cell 40 px on a 72 px pitch, or 60 px icons on a 95 px pitch. Sound: An onset on the wave; a sub on the gallery; a hit on the radial step. Materials: As cells multiply each holds the spreadsheet overflow mark in a dark tone; the clicked centre cell is the full accent and each ring of neighbours a lighter tint (five steps), so the wave reads as a heat map of distance; rows added every 5-6 f.
techniques.timing: 23-75 f; each cell 40 f in-out; wave 20 f across; diagonal onset +1 f per column, +1.4 f per row.
techniques.use_when: Openers, backgrounds that build, galleries of thousands, "it scales".
techniques.avoid_when: Cells that move (they only switch).
techniques.materials: As cells multiply each holds the spreadsheet overflow mark in a dark tone; the clicked centre cell is the full accent and each ring of neighbours a lighter tint (five steps), so the wave reads as a heat map of distance; rows added every 5-6 f.

techniques.name: Hairline layout grid as the ground
techniques.summary: A faint layout grid keeps empty space active: dashed grey cells on black that scale with the camera, a cutting-mat grid, hairlines a few percent darker than the page, guides with tiny square markers at intersections, grid paper with ruler ticks, a 1 px grid with small crosses at card corners, white rounded squares on near-white, a thin grid over photos; a wireframe grid of rectangles and nodes can pan and zoom.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a static SVG pattern (or a baked plate) inside the camera transform; markers as small rects at chosen intersections. Anatomy: Cells 16-210 px; 1 px lines; optional heavier line every 5 cells, tick marks on edges, crosses or nodes at intersections; the grid either moves with the camera or stays fixed while the content moves (a fixed grid reads as the screen). Sound: None. Materials: The dashed grid can be barrel-curved like a lens (each point pushed out by 1 + 0.06 d^2 from the centre, about 12 px of sag at the frame edges) and the curve swims as the camera pushes; dashes 14 px with 8 px gaps, 1 px mid-grey, cells about 210 px.
techniques.timing: Static; moves with the camera; a wireframe grid pans over 158 f.
techniques.use_when: Product, tool and design films; any minimal ground that needs structure.
techniques.avoid_when: Grids strong enough to read as content (keep lines 3-8 % off the ground).
techniques.materials: The dashed grid can be barrel-curved like a lens (each point pushed out by 1 + 0.06 d^2 from the centre, about 12 px of sag at the frame edges) and the curve swims as the camera pushes; dashes 14 px with 8 px gaps, 1 px mid-grey, cells about 210 px.

techniques.name: Holographic foil icons with frosted inner tiles
techniques.summary: Feature or integration icons are rounded squares whose surface swirls with pastel holographic foil (a cool rim, warm, pink and lilac sheen) under a smaller frosted-white tile that carries a plain white glyph; each icon's foil is turned to its own angle, so the grid shimmers as one family.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: one baked dithered conic foil PNG rotated by transform under a squircle clip, plus the white tile. Anatomy: Base conic gradient (rim hue -> warm -> pink -> lilac -> rim hue) blurred about 6 px inside the shape; inner tile inset 16 %, radius 20 %, white at 75 % with a 1 px white rim; glyph white with a 10 % grey shadow; icon about 80 px at radius 22 %; the foil angle differs per icon. Sound: Small pops on the arrivals. Materials: Example stops teal #2FA39A, peach #F2C1A6, pink #EBA3B9, lilac #C9C3EE; the foil is the film's one spectral accent.
techniques.timing: Develop 28 f (saturation pale to full while the focus clears), then hold.
techniques.use_when: A grid of features or integrations that must read premium and related; light grounds.
techniques.avoid_when: Dark grounds; brand icons that must keep their own colours.
techniques.materials: Example stops teal #2FA39A, peach #F2C1A6, pink #EBA3B9, lilac #C9C3EE; the foil is the film's one spectral accent.
conditions: the film's one spectral accent

techniques.name: A patch of light carrying a lattice sweeps under the text
techniques.summary: Before a send, a patch of pale light holding a fine white honeycomb lattice sweeps across the prompt box under the text; the lattice is only visible inside the light, so its edges dissolve, and the text and chips stay crisp on top.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: an SVG hex pattern masked by a moving radial gradient (a baked radial PNG as the mask) under the text layer, with a tint layer under the same mask. Anatomy: Light: a radial pale tint at about 70 % to transparent, about 420 x 300 px; hex cells about 55 px with 2 px white lines; travel about 30 px/f, decelerating. Sound: The send whoosh.
techniques.use_when: The send or run moment of a prompt box; a processing beat.
techniques.avoid_when: Every send; dark text on a dark box.

techniques.name: Glow and grain boil on held graphics
techniques.summary: While shapes hold still, their glow and grain change every frame by a few percent, so a held frame never freezes.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a set of 4-8 baked grain plates cycled by frame (seeded), at low opacity. Anatomy: Per-frame seeded noise on the grain plate and a tiny lightness wobble. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Every frame, amplitude 2-4 % luma.
techniques.use_when: Any hold longer than about 30 f on a graphic, especially on twos.
techniques.avoid_when: Visible flicker (keep it 2-4 % of luma).

techniques.name: Coarse pixel-mosaic ground behind UI
techniques.summary: The background is made of large square cells (30-45 px) like a low-resolution image of a soft colour field, also used as a dithered strip.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a baked low-res plate scaled up with image-rendering pixelated. Anatomy: Static cells. Sound: None.
techniques.timing: Static.
techniques.use_when: Image-generation brands; behind UI panels.
techniques.avoid_when: A second multi-hue field in the same film.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Concentric squares radiate at constant speed
techniques.summary: Square outline rings are born at the centre every few frames and expand at a constant speed, thick strokes and wide gaps, like a pulse leaving the centre.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Radiate start x y color stroke={75} speed={15}> (fx/Grids): square (or shape="circle") rings born every 10-15 f (seeded, or births on the beat), growing at one constant speed; swallow={{ at }} thickens them until only hairline gaps remain. Anatomy: Births every 4-6 f; 38 px/f; stroke about 75 px, gap about 98 px at birth. Sound: None.
techniques.use_when: A hub, an end card, a "broadcast" moment.
techniques.avoid_when: Easing the expansion (constant speed is the look).

techniques.name: Halftone, ASCII and dither as the picture's texture
techniques.summary: Pictures carry a print or screen texture: a grid of glyphs from a brightness ramp sits over the dark areas of images and re-samples irregularly; silhouettes are filled with a fine dot screen; clouds show a halftone in their shadows under a giant translucent wordmark; a light dot grid overlays a defocused photo; small dither pixels sparkle around subjects' edges.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a baked halftone or ASCII plate (rendered once from the image), cycled among 3-4 variants for the flicker. Recipe: the figure as a mask over three radial-dot patterns in pure red, green and blue, offset 1-2 px, screen blend on black; halftone radius per cell = r_max x sqrt(1 - luma). Anatomy: Dot pitch about 4 px at 1080p; glyph ramp . : o O 0; re-sample every 2-7 f (a soft flicker). Sound: None. Materials: Up close the halftone figures are printed in phosphor triads: the dot screen breaks into red, green and blue dots at the edges (8 px pitch, 3 px dots) with a grey core; on a mosaic glitch frame a fine dot grid at 25 % sits over the flat blocks like an LED wall. A frosted bar over a halftone sky averages the screen into soft colour (blur larger than the dot pitch).
techniques.timing: Static per frame or re-sampled every 2-7 f.
techniques.use_when: Image-generation, print, editorial or retro-tech films.
techniques.avoid_when: Texture on readable type.
techniques.materials: Up close the halftone figures are printed in phosphor triads: the dot screen breaks into red, green and blue dots at the edges (8 px pitch, 3 px dots) with a grey core; on a mosaic glitch frame a fine dot grid at 25 % sits over the flat blocks like an LED wall. A frosted bar over a halftone sky averages the screen into soft colour (blur larger than the dot pitch).

techniques.name: Picture sliced into offset slats
techniques.summary: A blurred figure is cut into 4-6 horizontal bands that are offset vertically by different amounts, so the image reads as a stepped, sliced object, then the offsets settle.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Slices kind="slats" at x y w h n={5} spread={0.08}>{picture}</Slices> (fx/Slices): 4-6 horizontal slats offset up and down by seeded amounts that settle to flat on E.snapOut (65 f). Anatomy: Bands 150-250 px; offsets decaying 16 -> 1.5 px/f. Sound: Under the hold.
techniques.timing: 65 f ease-out.
techniques.use_when: Section breaks on a portrait or a picture.
techniques.avoid_when: Faces that must be read.

techniques.name: Stills pushed into an expired-film spectral look
techniques.summary: Every still of a fast montage is pushed into one lo-fi spectral look: three or four saturated inks, a cyan fringe on one side of each edge and a red-yellow one on the other, a soft sideways smear, baked light streaks and heavy monochrome grain, so pictures from anywhere read as one printed, expired-film world.
techniques.recipe: Photo stills under a per-still stack: three channel copies offset by transform in screen blend, one fixed sideways-blur copy at 40 %, a grain overlay; the cadence is the flip montage's. Anatomy: Per still a local channel split (red sampled to one side, blue to the other, amount gated by a low-frequency noise so fringes are local, 15-30 px at 1080p), a one-axis blur copy (12 px) mixed at 40 %, monochrome grain about 1.5 px at 6 % re-seeded per frame; the palette pushed to a few saturated inks over a pale ground. Sound: Full music under the run, then a stop-down into the next line. Materials: Fringe = red copy +1.2 % of the width, blue copy -1.2 %, masked by a static soft-noise plate; grain monochrome, sigma about 1.5 levels; inks e.g. magenta, red, cobalt and teal over a pale periwinkle ground.
techniques.timing: Stills 5-22 f each on an accelerating cadence; the look holds constant across the run.
techniques.use_when: A montage of mixed generated or stock stills that must feel like one world; imaging and creative products.
techniques.avoid_when: Product UI; clean corporate films; more than one montage per film.
techniques.materials: Fringe = red copy +1.2 % of the width, blue copy -1.2 %, masked by a static soft-noise plate; grain monochrome, sigma about 1.5 levels; inks e.g. magenta, red, cobalt and teal over a pale periwinkle ground.
conditions: the film's one spectral accent

techniques.name: Thin speed lines while velocity is high
techniques.summary: Three to five thin lines trail a fast object, converging toward it, visible only while it moves fast; comic speed dashes trail travelling items; a burst of short accent dashes streaks across horizontal bands while a title decodes; three parallel stripes shoot in at constant speed and stop dead at the hero.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Rush lines={{ n: 5 }} lineColor> (fx/Rush): thin bars along the travel whose strength follows the speed (from 16 to 40 px/f at 60 fps), seeded rows, never drawn below the threshold. Anatomy: 1 px lines 200-400 px long, opacity tied to speed; dashes 8-60 px; stripes 20 px stopping dead. Sound: A decode bed; the music drops out on the hard stop. Materials: After the stripes stop dead at the hero, 3-4 very faint thin lines continue past it to the frame edge (opacity 20 % -> 0 along their length), as if the motion had passed through and left a trace.
techniques.timing: With the speed; bursts 42 f; stripes 12 f linear + a hard stop.
techniques.use_when: A thrown object, a travelling message, a decode with energy.
techniques.avoid_when: Lines on static frames.
techniques.materials: After the stripes stop dead at the hero, 3-4 very faint thin lines continue past it to the frame edge (opacity 20 % -> 0 along their length), as if the motion had passed through and left a trace.

techniques.name: A fan of curves that keep vibrating like strings
techniques.summary: From a hub (an app icon, a node) about sixteen curves fan out to the left and right and never freeze: their amplitudes swell and relax slowly, so they cross each other like vibrating strings or a moire; curves near the axis are saturated and thick, the outer ones thin and pale.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: 16-32 SVG paths recomputed each frame from closed-form amplitudes. Anatomy: Cubic curves from the hub's edge to the frame edge; stroke 2.5 px in the accent at the axis down to 1 px at 30 % outermost; amplitude oscillates 10-20 % on a 2-3 s period with a phase per curve; mirrored on the other side. Sound: VO only. Materials: Opacity and width fall linearly with the curve index; every curve converges exactly on the hub's edge.
techniques.timing: Continuous for 3-6 s.
techniques.use_when: Connection, sync, everything flowing into one; behind a hub while the VO speaks.
techniques.avoid_when: Under text; next to another line texture.
techniques.materials: Opacity and width fall linearly with the curve index; every curve converges exactly on the hub's edge.

techniques.name: A heat-mapped figure trailed by tinted time echoes
techniques.summary: Slow-motion footage of a figure is gradient-mapped like a heat image and trailed by soft translucent copies of itself a few frames behind, in one flat tint, so the movement reads as a long exposure; glyphs can trace its edge.
techniques.recipe: Footage three extra times with startFrom offsets under a static tint filter in screen blend. Anatomy: Figure: a three-stop map (deep, hot, pale highlight); echoes: three copies at -2, -4 and -6 source frames, one flat tint, blur 8 px, screen blend at 0.3, 0.2 and 0.1; grain about 4 %. Sound: Music. Materials: Echo tint flat over a pale ground; in a house film the tint is a pale shade of the accent.
techniques.timing: The echoes persist through the clip; often speed-ramped into a pixelate cut.
techniques.use_when: A sport, motion or generation beat; one hero clip.
techniques.avoid_when: Talking heads; UI.
techniques.materials: Echo tint flat over a pale ground; in a house film the tint is a pale shade of the accent.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Echoes in a pale tint of the accent.

techniques.name: Design-tool guides that track a mask's bounding box
techniques.summary: Behind a masked photo the faint lines are not a fixed grid: exactly two vertical and two horizontal hairlines sit on the edges of the mask's bounding box, extended across the frame, and they move with it as the mask breathes, like the guides of a design tool.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: four SVG lines placed from the mask's rect each frame. Anatomy: Lines 2 px at 1080p, about 10 luma off the ground, no blur; locked to the mask on every frame (no lag); they inherit the mask's breath and its contraction into the cut. Sound: A shutter click on the cut right after the contraction.
techniques.timing: As long as the mask: breath out 40 f, hold, in 10 f.
techniques.use_when: A shape-led identity; design and layout products; any masked hero image.
techniques.avoid_when: Busy grounds; together with a full grid.

techniques.name: Flat blocks burst out and reveal the next shot
techniques.summary: Hard-edged blocks take over the frame: outlined square blocks explode radially out of an icon and cover the frame, revealing a textured field; blocks retreat to one edge in steps while the next frame decodes; after a click, stepped white rectangles grow out of the button leaving a dark window around it; flat rectangles in two colours pop at random places for 1-2 frames each, the next shot showing through.
techniques.recipe: <BlockStep blocks> with a seeded block list growing from the source box. Anatomy: Coverage 8.7 -> 95 % in 10 f, or +12-16 % a frame; blocks 280-560 px wide; 2-4 new blocks a step. Sound: A bubble pop; a UI click; a drum cluster.
techniques.use_when: A click that changes everything; playful, graphic brands.
techniques.avoid_when: Gradient or glowing blocks.

techniques.name: Scene burns out to white
techniques.summary: The scene over-exposes into white: a bloom ring grows while tiles fly at the camera, a collage's contrast collapses through stepped tints, or a whip pan washes to white, then a hard cut to a white page.
techniques.recipe: <Exposure> with up = the ramp and swap at the peak, hue white. Anatomy: Luma 173-189 -> 234-237 over 5-16 f; tints stepped every 2-3 f. Sound: The loudest moment with a crack or uplifter; a whoosh.
techniques.timing: 30-40 f ramp.
techniques.use_when: Into a white end section; the loudest moment.
techniques.avoid_when: Tinted burns outside the brand colour.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: The burn is white or a pale tint of the accent only.

techniques.name: Things burst outward from the centre
techniques.summary: Satellites fly out radially, growing to about 1.45x, and leave the frame while the label swaps on a kick; a square becomes a deck of about 30 source tiles that fans and bursts along a spiral and stops in 2 frames.
techniques.recipe: Build: burstOut(f, { at, n, from, to, grow: 1.45, spiral }) (fx/Orbit): radial positions on E.buildIn (26 f) with growth; spiral (degrees per index at full travel) fans a deck along a spiral; stop it on a HardStep. Anatomy: Radius 640 -> 925 px on an ease-in with growth; spiral burst then a hard stop. Sound: A label swap on the kick; a kick on the burst.
techniques.use_when: Releasing a hub's contents; "from everywhere".
techniques.avoid_when: Calm films.

techniques.name: Bubble charges with colour, then snaps wide
techniques.summary: A typing pill fills with the accent on an expo-in while its dots fade and its width creeps, then snaps wide in one frame into a bar that eases to its final width.
techniques.recipe: MorphChain with a one-frame CHAIN_STEP after a fill window. Anatomy: Fill expo-in 28 f; width creep 185 -> 223 px; snap to 466 px in 1 f; ease 13 f. Sound: None needed; a soft hit on the snap.
techniques.timing: 44 f in all.
techniques.use_when: The answer arriving after a typing indicator.
techniques.avoid_when: Snapping without the charge.

techniques.name: Whole frame collapses into a chip or card
techniques.summary: The entire image shrinks fast under heavy blur into a small rounded chip; a design shrinks into a card on paper and cuts to it living on a billboard; a collage collapses into an app-icon tile; a lockup collapses while a strip of tiles grows from its centre glyph; a sheet collapses in hard steps to one cell that turns green and sinks.
techniques.recipe: collapse(f, { start, frames, square, into }) from MorphChain; stepped variant via HardStep widths. Anatomy: Collapse 10 f (about 230 px/f) with corner rounding and blur, then a linear shrink, a brief sharpening, a squeeze; stepped variant 835 -> 689 -> 413 -> 309 -> 277 px over 7 f. Sound: A boom; a drum (+39 ms); a sub-bass. Materials: A hairline outline (1 px white at 25 %, radius 8, inset 2 % from the text block) appears round the last words in 4 f and contracts with the photo into the chip (image corners 0 -> 40 px, extreme blur); the chip is a live window: a crop of the same photo keeps drifting about 0.75 px/f and lightens about 40 % over 70 f inside it while its label fades in 6 f.
techniques.use_when: Packing a whole scene into one object of the next scene.
techniques.avoid_when: Collapsing on an ease-out (it must accelerate).
techniques.materials: A hairline outline (1 px white at 25 %, radius 8, inset 2 % from the text block) appears round the last words in 4 f and contracts with the photo into the chip (image corners 0 -> 40 px, extreme blur); the chip is a live window: a crop of the same photo keeps drifting about 0.75 px/f and lightens about 40 % over 70 f inside it while its label fades in 6 f.

techniques.name: A colour block wipes the line on and lingers
techniques.summary: A block shoots across a line (its leading edge covering 400 px in 3 frames), leaving the words behind it, its trailing edge slower; on the second line it lingers on the last word, which cools from the block's colour.
techniques.recipe: Two Wipe edges (lead and trail) with different speeds; words revealed behind the lead. Anatomy: Lead edge fast, trail edge 3x slower; words cool 15 f. Sound: A pop.
techniques.timing: Lead 8 f; trail 23-50 f.
techniques.use_when: A tagline on.
techniques.avoid_when: A second multi-hue run in the same film.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Old layout whips out, new layout whips in from the same side
techniques.summary: The old composition accelerates out to the right and the new one arrives from the right moving left, decelerating: a swap that reverses direction at the cut.
techniques.recipe: Two whips with opposite directions; declare the seam as a position seam (not velocity). Anatomy: Out quad-in to 110 px/f; in cubic-out. Sound: An onset 48 ms after the cut.
techniques.timing: Out 30 f, in 42 f at 60 fps.
techniques.use_when: Comparing two states (before / after, old / new).
techniques.avoid_when: Using it as the default (it breaks velocity matching on purpose).

techniques.name: Outgoing scene melts by defocus under the next
techniques.summary: The background layer blurs, smears and darkens away while the next graphic draws on top; a soft blob rises from the bottom while the shot defocuses and tints; the outgoing headline lifts 22 px in one frame and defocuses as a tilted card rises over it.
techniques.recipe: <Dive> with a short occluder, or RackFocus levels on the outgoing layer while the next draws. Anatomy: Defocus on an ease-in, a darken or tint, a one-frame lift; the incoming element sharp from its first frame. Sound: A glockenspiel note; the voice phrase start. Materials: Before the colour finale, the photo is re-coloured into the gradient's palette as it blurs away: a faint pale blob breathes up from one corner (10 f), a second hue rises in its place (10 f), then the rest flood in from the other side and, on the same frame, the photo is gradient-mapped (dark -> deep hue, mid -> pink, light -> warm), blurred about 150 px and fades out over 16 f.
techniques.use_when: Layered scene changes where the new element arrives on top.
techniques.avoid_when: Fading without defocus (it reads as a crossfade).
techniques.materials: Before the colour finale, the photo is re-coloured into the gradient's palette as it blurs away: a faint pale blob breathes up from one corner (10 f), a second hue rises in its place (10 f), then the rest flood in from the other side and, on the same frame, the photo is gradient-mapped (dark -> deep hue, mid -> pink, light -> warm), blurred about 150 px and fades out over 16 f.
conditions: gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform

techniques.name: Zoom cut through a dither dissolve
techniques.summary: Between two frames a globe jumps from one size to 3.4x larger through a 3-frame pixel-dither dissolve, then the view tilts on an expo-out.
techniques.recipe: A static seeded dither mask plate stepped in three thresholds (HardStep) between the two shots. Anatomy: Scale jump on the cut; seeded dither mask dissolving over 3 f. Sound: None needed.
techniques.timing: Cut 1 f + dither 8 f; tilt 35 f.
techniques.use_when: Zooming into a planet, a map, an image.
techniques.avoid_when: Fine-detail subjects (the dither eats them).

techniques.name: Halves part like doors and the next card rises through
techniques.summary: The next card peeks up 32 px from the bottom edge as a preview, then the two halves of the current layout accelerate off left and right like doors, and the card rides up through the gap with their speed.
techniques.recipe: doorSplitState(f, { start, rise: { top } }): each half's `offset` (px away from the split) and the card's `rise` (px below its rest); draw the card above the halves. Anatomy: the card peeks 32 px over 12 f, 18 f before the doors move, then creeps; the doors run the measured door path (each step about x1.5 the last, leaving at about 250 px a frame at 1080p and 24 fps); the card rides up from the bottom edge a third into the doors' run, peaks with them (about 110 px a frame at 24 fps) and decays home. Sound: A pop, a hit, a punchy accent.
techniques.timing: Peek 12 f, from 18 f before the doors; doors 30 f; rise 50 f from a third into the doors' run.
techniques.use_when: Introducing the next product surface.
techniques.avoid_when: Halves with content that splits a word.

techniques.name: The next shot arrives as an LED dot matrix, then melts solid
techniques.summary: Over the current shot the coming one appears first as round dots on a regular grid, each dot the colour of the incoming picture at that cell, in blob and band shapes that grow frame by frame (an ellipse, then full-width bands); the gaps still show the outgoing shot, so the two interleave cell by cell; then the solid image fades in under the dots and the dots go.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a canvas drawing circles sampled from the incoming still where mask(x, y, f) is on, then the plain image by opacity. Anatomy: Cell 12 px, dot radius 4.5 px; mask = a soft ellipse (scale 0.3 -> 1.2) plus rows switching on by a seeded hash, stepped rather than smooth; the solid image under the dots, then the dots off. Sound: A tick cluster under the music. Materials: The dots keep the picture's own colours; the gaps show the outgoing plate, never black.
techniques.timing: About 28 f: first cluster 2 f, mask growth 14 f, solid fade 8 f, dots gone in 6 f.
techniques.use_when: A cut into a screen, a product UI or a digital world; once per film.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm films; a pixelate cut in the same act.
techniques.materials: The dots keep the picture's own colours; the gaps show the outgoing plate, never black.

techniques.name: Scene emerges from white, hero first
techniques.summary: A 3D room emerges from a white frame centre-out: the desk gains colour first, then the floor, the right wall, the ceiling, the window.
techniques.recipe: Develop per region (each region a mask over the plate) with starts in order. Anatomy: Per region masks developing in order of importance. Sound: A reverse-cymbal riser.
techniques.timing: 24 f power-out.
techniques.use_when: Revealing a set or a product scene.
techniques.avoid_when: Without separable regions.

techniques.name: Over-exposed frame with a negative ghost
techniques.summary: After a whip on an ease-in, one frame at about 92 % white carries a blurred grey negative ghost of the outgoing object, then one dark streak frame, then the next shot sliding in.
techniques.recipe: <FlashCut whip flash streak slide pull> (smear 'draw', house: the whip's tail and the slide's head streak). Anatomy: Whip ease-in; flash 0.92 with a 0.3 ghost; one streak frame; slide in 28 f, most smeared on its first frames, and pull back. Sound: On the swell peak.
techniques.timing: Flash 2 f.
techniques.use_when: A whip transition on a swell's peak.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm films.

techniques.name: A soft panel flies through the camera
techniques.summary: The card recedes while a large frosted white panel scales toward the camera and fills the frame, then the next scene comes out of it.
techniques.recipe: <Dive occluder={softPanel}> with the panel scaled from 0.6 to 3 on E.buildIn. Anatomy: Card to 0.86; panel fills (centre luma 188 -> 248); next scene resolves. Sound: A glockenspiel note; a level dip before.
techniques.timing: 48 f: 14 f up, 22 f down.
techniques.use_when: A soft, bright transition between UI scenes.
techniques.avoid_when: Dark films (the panel reads as a flash).
conditions: glass as a material with real frost or refraction, not a default card style

techniques.name: Side elements gather toward the centre into the cut
techniques.summary: Stickers and scraps around a headline slide 45-100 px toward it while their scale holds, fastest on the last frame before the transition.
techniques.recipe: MorphChain gather phase (linear drift then M.squeeze) or a simple E.buildIn toward the centre. Anatomy: Strong ease-in; peak 7 px/f on the last frame. Sound: The downbeat at the cut.
techniques.use_when: Before a cut or a pixelate on a collage.
techniques.avoid_when: Gathering that settles.

techniques.name: Pixel glint sprite on twos bridges a cut
techniques.summary: Right after a hard cut, a tiny cluster of 3-4 bright squares (about 66, 53 and 24 px) drops diagonally across the frame, changing its arrangement every 2 frames through six poses (diagonal triplet, tall bar + square + dot, wide block + tick, two bars + dot in an L, a long bar with dots above and below, a single square), then vanishes; the new scene rises behind it on ones while the stage flashes and decays.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Glint at x y color> (fx/Glint) on the first frame after the cut: six poses of 1-3 squares, a new pose every 4 f at 60 fps (on twos at 30), dropping down-right along a 330 px path; flip mirrors it; glintGlow(f, at) gives the stage flash (half gone in one 30 fps frame, then a 30 f tail). Anatomy: A pose table of rects in local px; the group travels a slightly accelerating path (about 34 px per pose); each square with a soft halo; stage glow to luma 36 then a decay over 30 f. Sound: A whip whoosh into the cut.
techniques.timing: 6 poses x 4 f at 60 fps (on twos at 30) = 24 f; path 340 px.
techniques.use_when: A cut that needs a bridge with character: from a send action to the result, into a new scene on a whip.
techniques.avoid_when: Glows on light grounds; using it more than twice per film.
conditions: light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo

techniques.name: Glitch run: distinct full-frame looks on twos
techniques.summary: A break out of live action in four completely different full-frame looks, each held exactly two frames, alternating bright and dark: a ghost smear with channel split, a blue block mosaic with the subject inverted, a scan-line displacement tear, a black frame with the caption collapsed into a streak; or a posterised 1-bit capture flash for four frames that breaks up.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: a sequencer of 2-frame looks, each its own layer: offset copies, a Pixelate block level, seeded horizontal strips, a black frame with a scaleY streak. Anatomy: States held 2 f each; luma high-low-high-low (139, 29, 117, 4); bands 10-40 px tall with seeded offsets. Sound: Starts on the end of the spoken phrase; a shutter hit on the capture.
techniques.timing: 4 states x 5 f (20 f); posterise 8 f + 4 f break.
techniques.use_when: Tearing the viewer from realism into the graphic world, once, on the end of a spoken phrase.
techniques.avoid_when: Calm films; more than once; gradual blending between states.

techniques.name: A glyph detaches and becomes UI
techniques.summary: A part of the logo (an asterisk) lifts off the wordmark and travels on an accelerating arc to become an icon in the UI; an icon dims and hands off to the matching glyph of the wordmark; a send icon flies across a cut as a smear and becomes a slider knob with the pointer.
techniques.recipe: logoParts() to isolate the glyph, a bowed path (cursorMove's bow) to the UI icon's box, MorphChain for the shape. Anatomy: Arc on an ease-in; cross-dissolve overlap of 6-8 f; momentum continues after the cut. Sound: The film's start; or none.
techniques.use_when: Brand to product and product to brand.
techniques.avoid_when: Glyphs that do not exist in both places.

techniques.name: Small element grows into the next scene
techniques.summary: A tooltip pill, a single cell, an inline photo pill or a white button grows (exponentially or on an expo in-out) until it is the next scene; a button can become a porthole the next subject rises into.
techniques.recipe: growThrough({ start, frames, from, to }) (E.buildIn); the porthole is Iris at the button's size with the next subject masked inside. Anatomy: Growth x1.15 a frame while the centre moves to the frame centre; x2.44 in one frame for a cell; an inline pill accelerating its own growth in the last 7 f of a push. Sound: Water drops then a sub-drop; an onset at the cover. Materials: A notch in a custom glyph of the wordmark becomes a slit that opens into the next shot: an 8 px sliver appears exactly in the notch, then widens into a photo band whose height grows 4, 6, 12, 20, 35, 50, 75, 95, 140 px (one value a frame at 30 fps, width leading height by about 8 f) while the wordmark greys and fades to 20 %.
techniques.timing: 14-48 f; the cover frame is the cut.
techniques.use_when: Opening a detail into its world; from a chip in a sentence to its full picture.
techniques.avoid_when: Growth that slows before the cover (it must accelerate into the frame).
techniques.materials: A notch in a custom glyph of the wordmark becomes a slit that opens into the next shot: an 8 px sliver appears exactly in the notch, then widens into a photo band whose height grows 4, 6, 12, 20, 35, 50, 75, 95, 140 px (one value a frame at 30 fps, width leading height by about 8 f) while the wordmark greys and fades to 20 %.

techniques.name: Object implodes into a point or vortex
techniques.summary: A ring spirals inward into a single bright point with the caption fading inside it; a button shrinks under the cursor and the next frame is a short soft swirling ring that births the title; a white disc dissolves from the inside out.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Implode at r x y color kind="spiral"|"vortex"|"hole"> (fx/Implode): spiral: the ring coils inward on M.squeeze, posed every 5 f (radius 1, .79, .60, .17, then a point held 6 f); vortex: three tightening arcs (12 f); hole: a ground-coloured hole grows in the disc while it dims (18 f). Anatomy: Spiral radius 369 -> 291 -> 223 -> 64 -> point on twos accelerating; swirl of 2-3 soft arcs for 6 f; an inner hole growing 35 -> 218 px while the disc dims. Sound: A pop or a spoken word; no hit for the spiral. Materials: Three constructions. Burn-out: a dark soft hole grows from the disc's centre (radius 12 -> 75 % of the disc) while the outer edge defocuses 0 -> 14 px and the luma drops to about 13 %, in 18 f. Swirl: the dot grid behind bends into waves curling round the target (displacement up to 20-40 px, falling off over 400 px, roughly doubling each frame) and a trail is sucked in as a thin tongue, 8 f into the vortex. Snake: the ring's tail erases while its head keeps drawing past 360 deg on a falling radius, on twos (20 f), the caption fading under the coil.
techniques.use_when: Ending a section on a point; birthing a title from an object.
techniques.avoid_when: Long vortices (keep under 12 f).
techniques.materials: Three constructions. Burn-out: a dark soft hole grows from the disc's centre (radius 12 -> 75 % of the disc) while the outer edge defocuses 0 -> 14 px and the luma drops to about 13 %, in 18 f. Swirl: the dot grid behind bends into waves curling round the target (displacement up to 20-40 px, falling off over 400 px, roughly doubling each frame) and a trail is sucked in as a thin tongue, 8 f into the vortex. Snake: the ring's tail erases while its head keeps drawing past 360 deg on a falling radius, on twos (20 f), the caption fading under the coil.

techniques.name: Three single frames with an inverted centre band
techniques.summary: A loop resets through three one-frame images (the product UI, the key word huge, scattered tiles), each with its centre band (about 56 % of the width) colour-inverted while the outer strips stay normal; then the main shot returns.
techniques.recipe: Build: <InvertBand at count={3} sources={[a, b, c]}> (fx/Flashes): each source one beat (2 f at 60), with an inverted copy clipped to the centre 56 % band; every image a declared flash. Anatomy: A fixed vertical band applying invert over three different sources, one frame each. Sound: None needed.
techniques.timing: 3 x 2 f; repeats every 104 f in a loop.
techniques.use_when: A loop separator; a beat between sections in a playful film.
techniques.avoid_when: More than once per loop.

techniques.name: One or two inverted frames between shots
techniques.summary: Between two shots, one frame of the scene (or two frames of the key word) appears with its colours inverted: black type on the accent, white on black.
techniques.recipe: HardStep a one-frame layer with filter invert(1) (or a pre-built inverted card). Anatomy: Inverted colours on one or two frames; the key word alone, centred. Sound: A chat pop. Materials: The flash frame can already carry the next scene's geometry (a dashed circle split by a line, two faint perspective lines) that only arrives seconds later: a seed planted in 4 f.
techniques.timing: 1-2 f at the film rate.
techniques.use_when: Punctuation between scenes; flashing the key word.
techniques.avoid_when: Long flashes; more than two per film.
techniques.materials: The flash frame can already carry the next scene's geometry (a dashed circle split by a line, two faint perspective lines) that only arrives seconds later: a seed planted in 4 f.

techniques.name: Iris opens from a point already on screen
techniques.summary: A circle opens from the object the eye is on (the gap between two words, a sparkle, the centre of a pixel field, the space under a header) and grows by a constant ratio a frame (x1.28 at 60 fps, x1.63 at 30) until it passes the corners, revealing the next scene already moving inside; a scalloped cloud edge makes the matte the subject; it can start already 40 % wide and cover in 4 frames; a pill can widen on an ease-in as the wind-up.
techniques.recipe: <Iris mode="rate" originFrom scallop>. Anatomy: r0 about 22 px (visible on frame one), constant ratio; scallop 9 lobes at 6-8 % depth with an 8-12 px feather; inner scene zooming; porthole variant under a header. Sound: A glockenspiel note or an orchestral stab on the first frame. Materials: Scalloped iris: about 10 round lobes on the rim (lobe radius about 0.18 of the radius), edge feathered 8-12 px; it grows from about 140 px to past the frame over 72 f (ease-in, then fast) while the footage inside is already moving; the shape that started it becomes a hole in the ground colour.
techniques.timing: 8-18 f to the far corner; cloud iris 74 f in two phases (40 f expo-out, 30 f ease-in to overfill).
techniques.use_when: Section changes; reveals from a word or a dot.
techniques.avoid_when: Eased irises that start invisible.
techniques.materials: Scalloped iris: about 10 round lobes on the rim (lobe radius about 0.18 of the radius), edge feathered 8-12 px; it grows from about 140 px to past the frame over 72 f (ease-in, then fast) while the footage inside is already moving; the shape that started it becomes a hole in the ground colour.

techniques.name: One jump frame hides the cut inside a zoom
techniques.summary: A zoom builds on an exponential ease-in, then ONE frame carries a huge scale step (+30-52 %, or 71-86 % of the log move) where the cut hides, often with a brightness flash; the move then eases out in the new shot (a zoom into the input where the typed text jumps ahead; an app pulling back into a wall of app tiles).
techniques.recipe: <SnapZoom pre post flash={{ gain }}> with the content swap on the jump frame. Anatomy: Ease-in 0.1 -> 3.7-16 %/f, the jump frame (with a +61 % luma flash optional), ease-out 11-30 f. Sound: An onset on the jump; a pop and a sub on the switch.
techniques.timing: Build 16-20 f; jump 1 f; land 20-30 f.
techniques.use_when: Hiding a cut or a content jump in a camera event.
techniques.avoid_when: More than one jump frame in a move.

techniques.name: Letterbox window swings open in 3D, then flattens into a card
techniques.summary: A thin letterbox image window slides, opens into a perspective quad with dots at its corners, swings, then flattens into a UI card, and the shot cuts.
techniques.recipe: Window steps for the opening plus a matrix3d swing of the quad; Markers on the corners. Anatomy: Letterbox 950 x 86 px; open 1 f; swing 6 f; flatten 2 f. Sound: A drum hit.
techniques.use_when: Turning an image strip into the product.
techniques.avoid_when: Text inside the swinging window.

techniques.name: Letters replaced by product objects
techniques.summary: The letters of a word are swapped in place for product renders (laptop, headphones, camera) with soft contact shadows, the row spreads, then implodes.
techniques.recipe: Recipe: Letters positions as anchors, per letter with a FloatShadow. Anatomy: Per letter a render at the letter's box; spread circ-out; implode 13 f. Sound: None needed.
techniques.timing: Swap 10 f; spread 90 f; implode 13 f.
techniques.use_when: Commerce, product catalogues.
techniques.avoid_when: Without real product renders.

techniques.name: A soft light band carries the old graphic out
techniques.summary: The diagram slides out on an expo-in while a soft band of light travels across the frame, accelerating, taking the old graphic with it.
techniques.recipe: <LightSweep frames={44} gain={0.55}> + the diagram's exit on E.launchIn. Recipe: an SVG fractal-noise filter stretched vertically (baseFrequency 0.06 x 0.0015) coloured to the accent, masked by a horizontal gradient, translated; bake it as a plate for render speed. Anatomy: Band about 0.45 of the width; ease-in. Sound: Voice. Materials: The light is textured: fine vertical streaks (6-20 px, plus or minus 15 % luminance) run through the band like a light curtain or a long-exposure aurora, its edge falling off to black over about 300 px; it drifts slowly, then accelerates across as the wipe (about 44 f).
techniques.use_when: Clearing a diagram or chart.
techniques.avoid_when: A glow that is not part of the band (a halo round type).
techniques.materials: The light is textured: fine vertical streaks (6-20 px, plus or minus 15 % luminance) run through the band like a light curtain or a long-exposure aurora, its edge falling off to black over about 300 px; it drifts slowly, then accelerates across as the wipe (about 44 f).

techniques.name: UI revealed inside a growing circle whose edge is a band of light
techniques.summary: After the logo, the product UI appears inside a circle growing from a corner of the panel, and the circle's edge is a band of light rather than a line: the UI brightens to white at the front, saturates to the accent behind it, then falls off to the ground like a scanner passing, and the UI under the band keeps full detail.
techniques.recipe: Iris for the mask plus a ring layer of the same radius in screen blend (a baked radial band PNG scaled by transform). Anatomy: Radius expo-out from about 150 px to beyond the diagonal; edge band 90-120 px: an inner white wash at +60 % luminance, the accent at 70 % alpha in the middle, an outer fade to the ground; the ring thins and fades as it leaves the frame. Sound: Cut on an 8th onset. Materials: The band is screen-blended over the UI, never replacing it.
techniques.timing: 76 f; the cut on an 8th.
techniques.use_when: The first product reveal from a corner or a sidebar.
techniques.avoid_when: Dark-on-dark with no accent; repeated reveals.
techniques.materials: The band is screen-blended over the UI, never replacing it.

techniques.name: Line parts from the middle, layout swaps on frame three
techniques.summary: The two halves of a title move apart from the middle (7 px, then 31-38 px) and on the third frame the whole layout is replaced.
techniques.recipe: doorSplitState(f, { start, frames: 6 at 60 fps, rise: false }) on the title layer only (the measured door path: each step about x1.5 the last; no card rises), swap on its third frame. Anatomy: Ease-in split; swap on frame 3. Sound: An orchestral stab.
techniques.timing: 6 f at 60 fps.
techniques.use_when: A quick change of scene from a centred title.
techniques.avoid_when: Long splits (the swap must come early).

techniques.name: Flat layout cuts into the same layout in the world
techniques.summary: A flat graphic layout pans (or the camera pushes toward a monitor) and cuts into real footage where the same layout is a street hoarding or the monitor's content full-frame: the design steps out into the world.
techniques.recipe: zoomThrough to the monitor's box then handoffShot; for the hoarding, match the layout's corners with a matrix3d onto the footage. Anatomy: Exit ease-in; the matched element at the same screen place on both sides; the cut can be silent. Sound: The cut on a beat with a boom; or a silent cut inside a silence.
techniques.timing: Pre 42 f; post 145 f.
techniques.use_when: Showing a design or a screen in use.
techniques.avoid_when: Without footage that matches the layout's geometry.

techniques.name: Small object becomes the next word, card or cell
techniques.summary: A chip, dot, button or circle carries the film into its next state instead of a cut: a squeezed chip swells +52 % and is replaced by a word at the chip's pre-swell size; a dot becomes a text caret in 2 frames and drops into the field; an icon box springs into a pill; a chosen comment collapses into a request pill; a button turns accent and shrinks into the first cell of a chart; solid capsules fly in, flash and become labelled chips; a circle grows and morphs into a rounded card; two shapes merge and pop to a new colour; a toast collapses and a larger card blooms in its place.
techniques.recipe: <MorphChain states windows> (house: swell on M.swell 24 f, collapse 16-20 f, camera push on E.glideOut from the swap). Anatomy: Gather (linear drift, then a squeeze), swell +40-60 % on an ease-in straight into the swap, the new content at the old object's pre-swell size; radius and aspect animate with height leading width; colour flashes 2 f on a merge; one spring allowed (13 % overshoot). Sound: A beat or kick on the swap; a soft UI tap the frame before a heavy thud.
techniques.timing: Hand-offs every 8-32 f; swell 12-24 f; caret 2 f + an over-damped 8 f drop; card bloom 4 + 42 f.
techniques.use_when: Any handoff between product states; the strongest transition family for UI films.
techniques.avoid_when: Morphing objects with no relation; slow morphs (keep each step short).

techniques.name: An object continues through the cut in a new role
techniques.summary: One element keeps moving across a hard cut and changes role on the other side: an avatar accelerating upward becomes the small header of a chat; a mark keeps shrinking while the background cuts; a finished line keeps breathing apart through the cut; a prompt card drifts up and jumps (+10.5 %) into a sent message bubble.
techniques.recipe: handoffShot(carry: ['x','y','k']) with the element drawn in both shots at the matched place; declare a velocity seam. Anatomy: Same screen position and speed on both sides (±20-30 px); scale may jump up to +10 % hidden by the cut. Sound: The cut on the beat (-27 ms); a footstep-like hit after. Materials: The logo icon survives the wipe: as a feathered white wipe erases the wordmark, the icon stays fully visible on top of the white for one frame, and on the next it is a small black glyph on a white tile already in its slot inside the new UI (a position jump of about 120 px).
techniques.timing: Pre-cut 15-42 f ease-in; post-cut 23-89 f.
techniques.use_when: Linking two states of the product; the brand mark entering the product.
techniques.avoid_when: Changing the element's speed at the cut.
techniques.materials: The logo icon survives the wipe: as a feathered white wipe erases the wordmark, the icon stays fully visible on top of the white for one frame, and on the next it is a small black glyph on a white tile already in its slot inside the new UI (a position jump of about 120 px).

techniques.name: Cut through exactly one blank frame
techniques.summary: A hard cut through exactly one empty frame (black, pure white, or the brand's background colour) separates two sections like a breath.
techniques.recipe: blackDipState({ black: 1, fadeUp: 0 }) or a one-frame flat Sequence. Anatomy: One full frame of a flat colour. Sound: Between voice words, or a shutter click and a drum just after. Materials: A panel can start from one empty frame of its ground (2 f) before the first block, again before a loop restart.
techniques.timing: 1 f at the film rate (2-3 f at 60 fps).
techniques.use_when: Between story and finale; a section break inside a voice-led film.
techniques.avoid_when: More than one per minute; two frames (that reads as a glitch).
techniques.materials: A panel can start from one empty frame of its ground (2 f) before the first block, again before a loop restart.

techniques.name: Next scene's tiles fly over the outgoing shot
techniques.summary: Tiles of the next scene fly into the frame over the outgoing card a few frames before the cut; or the old panels hold 1-3 frames over the new photo, then blank tiles re-tile into the new layout and fill.
techniques.recipe: Cards enterState per tile starting 8 f before the cut; HardStep holds for the overlap. Anatomy: Tiles settle expo (34 % on the first moving frame); overlap 4 f; re-tile 12 f, fill 12-20 f. Sound: An onset at the tiles; speech then a glockenspiel.
techniques.use_when: Grid-based films; image-led sequences.
techniques.avoid_when: Tiles that do not belong to the next scene.

techniques.name: One panel at 2x for one frame
techniques.summary: From a four-quadrant grid, all quadrants make their last move and on the final frame one quadrant fills the frame at 2x for exactly one frame, then a hard cut.
techniques.recipe: HardStep the cell's scale to frame size for one frame. Anatomy: A one-frame full-frame of one cell, scaled 2x. Sound: None needed.
techniques.use_when: Leaving a grid of shots.
techniques.avoid_when: More than one frame.

techniques.name: Panel pushes the shot off in two stages
techniques.summary: A solid panel wipes in from one side to half the frame, holds while something starts inside it (typing begins), then completes the wipe; or a coloured panel floods one side in the last frames; or a hard-edged panel wipes across in 3 frames already carrying the next word.
techniques.recipe: <Wipe kind="push"> (its house stages are this device: the edge starts off-frame so the outgoing shot is already moving, arrives fast and settles to 0.483 of the frame in 54 f, creeps, then leaves on E.buildIn over 42 f and is cut at speed; the footage rides 0.62 of the edge's travel in the arrival; the edge streaks 0.3 of its step, and smear 'draw' (house) streaks the pushed footage, 'shutter' declares it as camera blur instead). `stages` for other runs ([{ to, frames, ease, push, gap }]: a gap holds and creeps before the next stage), `ride: 1` pins the incoming panel to the edge as a sliding sheet. Anatomy: arrival to just under half, creep, stage 2 at speed; the hard panel 0 -> 58 -> 74 -> 95 % coverage. Sound: Voice; a riser into stage 2. Materials: Both layers smear: at the fastest frames the entering panel and the pushed footage carry a horizontal blur of 25-35 px (blur = speed x 0.3), the footage pushed at 0.64x the edge speed and the panel's edge soft over about 30 px; the blur is gone by the park, 24 f in.
techniques.timing: Arrival 54 f to 0.483 of the frame (the edge from 0.075 off-frame, its speed peaking a quarter of the way in at about 7 % of the frame a 60 fps frame), creep 0.13 % a frame, leave 42 f on E.buildIn; the hard panel 8 f + settle 13 f.
techniques.use_when: Moving from footage to product UI; a beat that needs a hard graphic change.
techniques.avoid_when: Gradient panels that are not baked and dithered.
techniques.materials: Both layers smear: at the fastest frames the entering panel and the pushed footage carry a horizontal blur of 25-35 px (blur = speed x 0.3), the footage pushed at 0.64x the edge speed and the panel's edge soft over about 30 px; the blur is gone by the park, 24 f in.

techniques.name: Parts detach and reassemble into a big shape
techniques.summary: The type is cut away and its coloured tag fills detach as bars, rotate and slide into a giant arrow that fills the panel, then exit.
techniques.recipe: assembleState with parts given explicit from offsets and rotations. Anatomy: Bars rotate and translate to target slots; quart-in exit. Sound: None needed.
techniques.timing: Assemble 30 f; exit 18 f.
techniques.use_when: Turning labels into a direction (next, forward, go).
techniques.avoid_when: Too many parts (more than about 8).

techniques.name: The full stop becomes the next object
techniques.summary: The last mark of a sentence (a period, a signature's dot, a hero point, a bar) turns into the next thing: it scales into a shaded ball and drips a stem that becomes the next shot's line; pops oversized, swells and drops onto a planet; grows exponentially to frame centre and cuts to an inverted frame at the same size; swells into a planet disc; or a bar retracts into a sphere that falls into the end card.
techniques.recipe: MorphChain from the period's measured box (FontGate) to a ball, then growThrough or a drop on E.buildIn; the full-stop zoom via zoomThrough with an inverted next frame. Anatomy: Pop that starts oversized (r 14 -> 6.6 px), swell on cubic-in, drop on a quart-in with gravity (73 px/f); exponential growth x1.10 -> x1.26 a frame; a stem with 5 % overshoot. Sound: An onset on the pop, a UI pop and kicks on the drop; voice names the next thing. Materials: The swollen dot is first a flat, soft-edged disc with grain (edge feather 10 % of the radius, grain about 6 levels that changes on held frames) for 12 f, then real footage develops into it from one edge (a diagonal mask in 2-3 steps on twos) until it is a photograph.
techniques.timing: 28-75 f in all; pop 20 f, swell 10 f, drop 17-25 f.
techniques.use_when: Ending a statement into the next scene; into the end card.
techniques.avoid_when: Punctuation the viewer has not noticed (give it a beat).
techniques.materials: The swollen dot is first a flat, soft-edged disc with grain (edge feather 10 % of the radius, grain about 6 levels that changes on held frames) for 12 f, then real footage develops into it from one edge (a diagonal mask in 2-3 steps on twos) until it is a photograph.

techniques.name: Tags dissolve through low-res pixels into dots
techniques.summary: Tags breathe wider slowly, then dissolve as pale low-resolution pixel blocks into two small dots that hold.
techniques.recipe: Pixelate out-phase on the tags, then two dots via HardStep. Anatomy: Breathe +3.8 %; dissolve 5 f; dots hold 8 f. Sound: A plucked note.
techniques.timing: 65 f in all.
techniques.use_when: Ending a data moment into a minimal mark.
techniques.avoid_when: Large blocks.

techniques.name: Pixel-staircase wipe stepped on twos
techniques.summary: A wipe in the next scene's colour built from 22-23 px square blocks advances diagonally with a random staircase edge, stepped on twos, with a faint fringe; or horizontal bands of the next scene slide in over the old with a dither-staircase edge.
techniques.recipe: Build: <StairWipe at color outgoing incoming> (fx/Grids): 22 px blocks advance diagonally (35 deg) with a seeded staircase edge (12 %), stepped at 12.5 fps, 80 % of the coverage in the middle on M.pixelStair (55 f); a fringe of blocks in the next scene's colour leads it (fringeAlpha={1} for a solid accent edge); a wipe seam. Anatomy: Coverage 0.3 -> 22 -> 62 -> 85 -> 99 % on 12.5 fps steps, 80 % in the middle 0.36 s; cells 8-23 px. Sound: A riser peak; crunchy clicks under the steps.
techniques.use_when: Image or pixel-flavoured films; a beat with crunchy clicks.
techniques.avoid_when: Smooth films.

techniques.name: Cut tighter mid-move, same vector
techniques.summary: A hard cut to a 1.16-2.5x closer framing of the same thing, inside a continuing move: the content keeps moving the same way and decelerates, or the close-up pulls back 9 % on a decay, or just creeps on; a jump cut can skip forward inside an expansion.
techniques.recipe: handoffShot with a scale factor (carry x, y); SnapZoom with pre: 0 for the one-frame version. Anatomy: Scale step 1.16-2.5x on the cut; the motion vector continues; decay or creep after; two one-frame punch-ins can coexist with two marker sets. Sound: On the beat (+40 ms) or a keypress just before.
techniques.timing: Settle 30-70 f (34 % in the first 10 %); creep 0.4-0.6 %/f.
techniques.use_when: Emphasis on a word, a field, a button while the action continues.
techniques.avoid_when: Cutting to the same scale (a jump cut that reads as a mistake).

techniques.name: A straight row curls into a ring
techniques.summary: A strip of tiles starts rotating with acceleration and both ends wrap around (the leader over the top, the tail along the bottom) until the row closes into a ring, on the kick after a short silence.
techniques.recipe: Build: <RingCurl at n pitch x y render={(i) => tile}> (fx/Gather): every tile rides a curve bent from the row into a circle of the same length by its arc length (32 f on E.buildIn: it closes at speed), the whole turning 45 deg, then still turning and slowing (tau 10 f). Anatomy: Arc-length parametrisation: tiles move along a path that morphs from a line to a circle while the whole rotates. Sound: A kick exactly on the fastest frame after a 0.35 s silence.
techniques.timing: 32 f on an ease-in; the ring closes 4-6 f after the fastest frame.
techniques.use_when: Turning a list of things into a cycle or an ecosystem.
techniques.avoid_when: Fewer than 5 tiles.

techniques.name: Rush: geometric acceleration into the cut
techniques.summary: The rush: a line or a scroll drifts, then roughly doubles its speed every frame (2, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 18, 34, 88 px/f) and is hard-cut at the peak; the next shot opens at that speed and halves it every frame (259, 131, 54, 30, 18 px/f); a card can whip crisply (no blur) into the cut and be caught by a decelerating pan; shots can arrive smeared and settle their pan.
techniques.recipe: Build: <Rush cut dir vCut from out in lines lineColor> (fx/Rush): the outgoing layer builds on lib/handoff launch() (speed roughly doubling every 24 fps frame) and is cut on its fastest frame; the incoming one opens at the cut speed and halves it every 24 fps frame (carry()); copies draws 2-3 faint smear copies on the fastest frames, lines thin speed lines above 16 px/f; declares a velocity seam and camera blur above 100 px/f. Anatomy: Ratio x1.4-2.4 a frame on the way in; x0.5 a frame on the way out; crisp text up to about 52 px/f. Sound: A speech onset or a sub on the cut; a punchy hit.
techniques.timing: Exit 30-43 f; entry decay 30 f.
techniques.use_when: Energy peaks; the hook of a launch; moving from one product moment to the next with force.
techniques.avoid_when: More than two or three rushes per film; slowing before the cut.

techniques.name: Shape contracts and hands its outline to the next shot
techniques.summary: Before each caption cut an outline circle contracts faster (expo-in in its last 3 frames) and the next shot opens on another outline of the same shape; coral circles shrink and cut to a photo with matching thin outlines that contract in place.
techniques.recipe: Outline as an SVG ring; handoffShot carrying its radius. Anatomy: Outline contracts on an expo-in; the next outline at the same size and place. Sound: A kick on the cut (-17 ms).
techniques.timing: Last 6 f expo-in; outlines settle 16 f.
techniques.use_when: Photo films; chaining captions with one shape motif.
techniques.avoid_when: Changing the motif shape between shots.

techniques.name: A text-height slot opens behind the line onto the photo
techniques.summary: On the word swap a hard-edged slot exactly the height of the text opens behind the line and shows the coming photo; the type flips from grey to white inside it and the caret becomes a selection block for one frame; later the photo fills the frame.
techniques.recipe: Photo clipped by an inset to the line's band, a colour step on the text, then a full-frame Photo fade. Anatomy: Slot about 9 % of the frame tall with hard edges, the photo blurred 4 px inside it; text ink -> white as the slot opens; caret block about 0.6 em at 40 % for 2 f; the full frame fades in 40 f later. Sound: The music returns on the reveal hit after a short dropout.
techniques.timing: Caret block 2 f, slot fades in 6 f, colour flip 2 f, full frame over 40 f.
techniques.use_when: A line that introduces imagery: a new way to see.
techniques.avoid_when: Multi-line copy.

techniques.name: Snap back from a giant word to the full line
techniques.summary: From a giant first word (or a line panning off the edge while it types), a hard cut to the full line at about 36-97 % of the scale, landing slightly small and blurred and growing to rest as the defocus clears.
techniques.recipe: punchOut-style cut with scaleBreath mode 'same' (open 0.97) and a short defocus. Anatomy: Cut lands at 0.974 scale, grows 6 f; defocus clears; the pan before runs on an expo-in. Sound: A speech hit 2 f before the cut.
techniques.timing: 1 f + 12 f at 60 fps; pans 56 f.
techniques.use_when: Revealing the whole sentence after a close-up word.
techniques.avoid_when: Landing exactly at rest (the slight undersize carries the motion).

techniques.name: Full blur straight into a near-static calm shot
techniques.summary: From a 6800 px/s smear on white, cut straight to a calm, sharp, full-bleed landscape with a small tagline; the frame before the blur cut can show the outgoing scene sharp in an earlier position, a frozen anchor before the smear.
techniques.recipe: Scroll or whip at peak speed with the blur pass on its frames, cut to a Photo with a 0.3 px/f drift. Anatomy: Blur at peak speed on the last frames; one sharp anchor frame; the calm shot barely moving. Sound: The blur's whoosh cut dead by the calm shot.
techniques.timing: Cut on the grid (+120 ms vs the beat).
techniques.use_when: Contrast between product speed and a calm promise.
techniques.avoid_when: Blending the two speeds.

techniques.name: Spin accelerates and the frame empties at peak
techniques.summary: A field of tiles spins faster each frame (x1.15-1.43 a frame) while zooming out; the words are erased one every 2 frames so the frame is text-free at peak spin, the cut lands on the fastest frame and the strongest accent, and the spin decays after.
techniques.recipe: Build: spinUp(f, { start, cut, from: 0.35, to: 7.25 }) (fx/Orbit): the spin grows by one ratio a frame into the cut on its fastest frame and decays after it with no speed step (rotationDecay from the peak); zoom out on the camera, erase the words on HardStep every 4 f so the frame is empty at the peak. Anatomy: Spin 0.7 -> 14.5 deg/f, zoom x0.90; words erased every 4 f at 60 fps; empty for 6-8 f. Sound: The peak on the strongest accent (a kick); a pop after the cut.
techniques.timing: Spin-up 23-30 f; empty 8 f; decay 33 f.
techniques.use_when: A galaxy of features or sources, into the next act.
techniques.avoid_when: Text left on screen at peak spin.

techniques.name: Frame halves flip to a new ground in turn
techniques.summary: The left half of the frame flips to a new ground for 3 frames, then the right half (the left reverting), then the whole frame.
techniques.recipe: HardStep on two half-frame layers. Anatomy: Hard halves, one beat each. Sound: A snare, then a whoosh.
techniques.timing: 6 + 8 f, then full.
techniques.use_when: A rhythmic flip into an end section.
techniques.avoid_when: More than one per film.

techniques.name: One block stamped into a plus of five
techniques.summary: On one frame the loader block is replicated into a plus of five blocks (each in a different phase of its animation) at 58 % scale, which then pulse smaller twice.
techniques.recipe: HardStep the copies on one frame; each copy's animation offset by a phase. Anatomy: One-frame stamp; pulses -15 % then -11 % expo-out. Sound: An orchestral stab (+10 ms).
techniques.timing: Stamp 1 f; pulses 22 f each.
techniques.use_when: A loader or icon multiplying into many.
techniques.avoid_when: Without a loop-able element to replicate.

techniques.name: Two frames of streaks with stripe artefacts
techniques.summary: Two frames of heavy horizontal streaking with vertical stripe artefacts (like a smeared barcode), then the next page arrives.
techniques.recipe: FlashCut's streak frame without the flash (streak only), held 2 f. Anatomy: The outgoing image stretched horizontally and cut into lines. Sound: A whoosh.
techniques.timing: 4 f at 60 fps.
techniques.use_when: A whip between two product pages.
techniques.avoid_when: More than two frames.

techniques.name: The swap hides in a blur peak
